The other day I came across research that showed one-third of British families believe that mum and dad should never stop paying for the family trip. Generation Z are even holding firm that the parent should contribute 52 per cent of the family holiday funds. And it’s already happening: multi-generational holidays are booming with more than double the number of British people going on holiday compared to four years ago.

In many ways, I was completely shocked. How on earth can anyone afford to take their family on holiday, especially when their children are in their 20s and early 30s? Why would anyone expect that? Why on earth should parents foot the bill for holidaying when everyone is now becoming cash-strapped?

Surely the Bank of Mum and Dad has to shut down at some point? For most, it’s not even possible for parents to keep paying for their children, especially when they’re not really children anymore.

open image in gallery Parent trap: it is a time of cost of living struggles, sure – but young people expecting the all-inclusive treatment is unacceptable ( HBO )

But then I realised that I’m guilty of this too. I am 60 at the end of this year and I wanted to organise a special family holiday to celebrate. I have four children and my second son is in a very serious relationship, so there was going to be six of us on holiday. I currently don’t have a partner, so we weren’t factoring that in. But we were thinking of taking my 92-year-old mother.

When it came to deciding where to go, I thought about previous holidays I enjoyed: Scotland, the Isle of Wight, North Devon. Unfortunately, my birthday is in December so we decided we would go after Christmas to get a cheaper holiday – and, at my children’s request, to go somewhere warm.

So we were looking at Thailand or Kenya, where I used to work as a volunteer teacher when I was 18 – or Tanzania or Zanzibar. I have various friends who go to South Africa in the winter. I also know that people go to the Caribbean.

We sat down and tried to work out the cost of a week's holiday for six people. Once you had factored in flights, seats, accommodation and food, I don’t think we were going to get much change out of £20,000. And while my children want to contribute, they don’t have spare income. So most of that was going to fall to me. Imagine doing that every year?

I love my children and I do understand that they are working and the cost of living has gone up, but I’m constantly shelling out £200 here and £200 there because there’s a shortfall in their rent or the car needs fixing, or they’ve run out of petrol. It's not that my children – 19, 22, 23 and 29 – don't work. They do work. However, their salaries do not keep up with the cost of living. Also they are saving for their rent, or they are putting aside money to potentially – and hopefully – buy a flat at some point.

open image in gallery ‘I couldn’t believe parents were paying for their grown-up children – then I realised I’m guilty of doing just that’ ( Lucy Cavendish )

I imagine that going on a holiday where everything is pretty much provided for must feel like manna from heaven for them. Yet it is financially horrifying.

When is this going to stop? When are children going to realise that at some point they’re no longer children and that they need to stand on their own two feet financially speaking?

When I was younger, this didn’t happen, mainly because you didn’t go on holiday with your parents; once I hit 18, that was the end of it. A family holiday when I was in my twenties would have been unthinkable.

However, that has totally changed. Lots of families holidaying together. And it all looks as if it is costing a pretty penny.

Not only is my social media feed full of pictures of friends of mine, various influencers and celebrities all somehow managing to holiday together with their adult children, I know countless people who are going on holiday with not just their adult kids but their children’s partners and sometimes even grandchildren.

I asked them how any of them can afford it – given the fact that I know young people don’t earn much money these days and the cost of living is crucifying, they basically tell me that they are funding the holiday.

Some of them even tell me they’ve paid for the entire holiday.

They’ve rented villas in Greece. They’ve booked onto activity holidays in the Dordogne. They are swimming around islands in Croatia. If they’re doing a staycation, they’ve rented very expensive holiday homes in Cornwall or Norfolk.

When is this going to stop? When are children going to realise that at some point they’re no longer children and that they need to stand on their own two feet financially speaking?

And it’s not just the cost of the accommodation. Everyone's got to get to wherever it is.

The last time I tried to book flights for myself and my 19-year-old daughter to Greece, the return fare including hold luggage (of course she needs to take every lotion and potion going plus many changes of outfits) and the designated seat so we could sit together came to over £1,000 – and that's just for two people.

How on Earth can anyone afford to do this regularly?

open image in gallery Holidays can be stressful as it is – adding your adult children into the mix is only going to complicate matters ( Various Artists Limited/BBC )

For many people of my generation it feels like an impossible situation. Not only are our children coming on holiday and ordering the most expensive thing off the menu - steak anyone? They are also piling on the drinks, renting jet skis, going shopping, asking if friends can come along.

Yet many people of my generation are still sandwiched between looking after elderly parents (and helping out financially) while also paying off student loans. And it is not only young people that the cost of living has affected. Whenever I look at my grocery bills, I almost faint with the shock. Despite using less electricity and gas, my direct debit has gone up. Nothing is going to get any cheaper in the future. Also, our work is precarious. Many of us are either out of work or freelance or being replaced by AI. In the press recently, there have been many articles by women in their 50s saying that they can no longer find a job despite the fact they are highly qualified.

The Bank of Mum and Dad is shuddering under the pressure. And, as a single parent, I am just the Bank of Mum. So when I realised how much my birthday trip would cost, the plan was shelved.

Unfortunately, this bank is shutting its doors.

Instead, we’ll have dinner at a local pub – not glamorous, and we won't be posting pictures all over social media – but I think it’s about time that we all got realistic about what we can afford and what we can’t afford.

News.content:

President Donald Trump’s Chairman of the Joint Chiefs, General Dan Caine, is seeking an “off-ramp “ from the ongoing war in Iran, according to a new report.

Caine has privately told other top administration officials that the country needs to find a way to exit the war, according to CNN, which cited three sources familiar with the matter.

Despite Trump claiming throughout the war that a peace deal, which would include his demand that Iran never obtain a nuclear weapon, was within reach, fighting has continued for more than five months.

“Caine is looking for an off ramp,” one of CNN’s sources said.

The general’s meetings with Trump officials, including Vice President JD Vance and Secretary of State Marco Rubio, are just to make clear the limitations and pitfalls of different military options, according to the sources.

open image in gallery President Donald Trump’s Chairman of the Joint Chiefs, General Dan Caine, is seeking an 'off-ramp' from the ongoing war in Iran, according to a new report ( Getty Images )

Joseph Holstead, a spokesperson for Caine, told CNN, “We do not discuss the Chairman’s confidential conversations with the President, the Secretary, or other senior leaders, nor do we comment on anonymous, agenda-driven characterizations of those conversations by sources who were not privy to them”.

A White House official praised Caine’s know-how, calling him an “incredible asset to President Trump’s national security team.”

“The General always provides accurate, unbiased information and a host of options to the Commander-in-Chief, who ultimately makes decisions based on what he feels is best for US national security”, the official said.

The Independent has reached out to the White House, the Office of the Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff and the Department of State for comment.

Trump’s war has primarily been an air campaign, relying on fighters to launch strikes against Iran instead of deploying ground troops. Caine and other Trump officials privately think it's unlikely that an air campaign alone can put enough pressure on the Iranians to agree to a deal that’s favorable to the president, according to multiple people familiar with recent discussions who spoke with CNN.

open image in gallery The Iran war, which is both costly and unpopular with Americans, has dragged on for more than five months ( AFP via Getty Images )

Meanwhile, Trump has denied recent reports that the US military’s weapons stockpile is dwindling.

“The U.S. has massive amounts of ‘munitions,’ especially of certain types. Additionally, large amounts are being manufactured and shipped to the U.S. as needed. Defense companies are building the largest number of plants and factories in our country’s history.

“The ‘leakers’ of these treasonous statements are being hunted down. Long term jail sentences will be sought!” Trump wrote on Truth Social Thursday.

Trump’s threats came after Reuters reported Tuesday, citing two unnamed sources, that the Army has used “virtually all” of its long-range Army Tactical Missile Systems and Precision Strike Missiles.

A recent report has also found that the Pentagon is running low on missile interceptors.

The US military had 2,330 Patriot systems and 452 Terminal High Altitude Area Defense systems before the war, according to the report from the Center for Strategic and International Studies. As of July 27, an estimated 759 to 827 Patriot systems and 234 to 278 THAAD systems remain, the report said.

open image in gallery Despite Trump claiming throughout the war that a peace deal was within reach, fighting has dragged on ( Getty Images )

During a Senate Appropriations Committee hearing last month, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said US military operations in Iran have cost an estimated $37.5 billion. He also asked Congress for an additional $67 billion to, in part, replenish weapons stockpiles, blaming the Biden administration for not properly funding the Pentagon.

The price of gas has also surged during the war, sitting above $4 a gallon Friday, according to motor club AAA. The price of a gallon of gas was just below $3 at the start of the war, according to the Associated Press.

Just 28 percent of Americans said they approved of Trump’s handling of Iran in a new Reuters/Ipsos poll.

President Donald Trump derided a federal appeals court ruling halting construction of his White House ballroom and demanding he seek congressional approval, insisting it would “severely jeopardize the lives and welfare” of White House staff.

In a lengthy Truth Social post Friday afternoon, the president said two judges on the D.C. Court of Appeals had made a “politically motivated” and “totally wrong” decision and characterized his White House ballroom project as crucial for national security.

“The Circuit Court’s decision, which is totally wrong on the vital subject of STANDING, of which the plaintiff has none, severely jeopardizes the lives and welfare of the people who work, and will be working, at the White House — including all future Presidents of the United States, and their families, as well as the lives of all those visiting…” Trump wrote.

In a 2-1 decision, the appellate judges said the president was only a “temporary tenant” of the White House and had unprecedentedly knocked down the East Wing, paid for with American tax dollars, to build a 90,000-square-foot space without consulting Congress.

But Trump disagreed and further characterized his project as a national security matter because the administration is building an underground bunker, complete with a military facility, emergency operation center and more.

open image in gallery President Donald Trump has rushed the construction of his White House ballroom, claiming its necessary for national security purposes ( AFP/Getty )

“It is all tied together as one big, expensive, and very complex unit, which is vital for National Security and Military Operations of the United States of America!” Trump wrote.

Though the president is insisting the project should continue, the judge’s ruling allows necessary national security construction to continue as legal challenges play out. It only halts above-ground, non-national security-related construction.

The court’s ruling will take effect for two weeks to give the Trump administration time to appeal to the Supreme Court, which the president said he would do.

Judge Patricia Millet, an Obama appointee, and Judge Brad Garcia, a Biden appointee, ruled in favor of the National Trust for Historic Preservation, the group suing the administration to stop construction of the ballroom.

“We are aware of no instance in American history in which a President unilaterally and using privately collected funds demolished substantial portions of the White House that Congress authorized to be built and American taxpayers paid for. Until now,” they wrote.

open image in gallery Last year, the president demolished the historic East Wing of the White House to make room for his new ballroom – sparking outrage from Democrats and members of the public ( Getty )

In doing so, they agreed with a lower court ruling, issued in April, that found Trump overstepped his authority when he demolished the East Wing to make room for the new ballroom.

“This holding has nothing at all to do with whether the proposed ballroom is desirable, or not, as a matter of policy. This ruling does not even necessarily mean that the Defendants may not ultimately construct the ballroom. What it does mean is that the Defendants may not do so during the district court’s expeditious litigation without securing Congress’s authorization, as the Constitution and laws require,” the judges added.

Meanwhile, Judge Neomi Rao, a Trump appointee, said she would have sided with the administration.

The Independent has asked the White House for comment.

Last year, Trump announced he would build the new glamorous ballroom, without using American taxpayer dollars, to serve as an entertaining space for state dinners and events.

open image in gallery Progress on the White House ballroom construction, pictured July 11, shows the administration moved forward with above-ground work while legal challenges played out ( Reuters )

But much like Trump’s other D.C. beautification projects, the cost, scale and public understanding of the project have changed over time.

The cost of the ballroom has surged from its original $200 million estimate to $400 million – with some believing it could cost upwards of $600 million. While Trump has said private donations will pay for the ballroom itself, in June the administration transferred more than $300 million from the Secret Service budget to cover security upgrades to the White House.

The administration has continued building the ballroom as legal challenges play out, arguing the ballroom is essential for national security because they are building an underground bunker containing a military complex, a hospital and an emergency operations center.

As judges have increasingly ruled against the construction of the White House ballroom, the administration has increasingly characterized the project as a pivotal national security or military project.

In Friday’s Truth Social post, the president referred to the project as “the desperately needed Military Center” even though the dispute is over the ballroom.

News.title: Gomes scores for Aston Villa in defeat by Bayern Munich in Hong Kong
News.content:
Aston Villa 1 Bayern Munich 2

Aston Villa’s tour of the Far East ended in defeat as they lost 2-1 to German champions Bayern Munich in a pre-season friendly at the Kai Tak Sports Park in Hong Kong on Friday.

Bayern took the lead inside the final 10 minutes of the first half, with defender Kim Min-jae heading in from Tom Bischof’s sublime free-kick. Villa goalkeeper Marco Bizot made a string of saves in the second half to keep Bayern’s lead at one goal until former Liverpool forward Luis Díaz smashed in Bayern’s second off the underside of the bar.

Just as the game appeared to be out of reach for Aston Villa, who had struggled to create much going forward for most of the game, Unai Emery’s side showed some life late on. Summer signing João Gomes’s goal from the edge of the box gave them hope before Tammy Abraham nearly brought them back onto level terms, only to be denied by a fine save from 40-year-old Manuel Neuer.

Aston Villa are next in action in six days’ time when they take on Paris St-Germain in the Uefa Super Cup before kicking off their Premier League campaign at Brighton. Bayern have one more friendly to come against RB Leipzig before the DFL-Supercup against Borussia Dortmund. They then kick off the defence of their Bundesliga crown against Stuttgart at home on August 28.

News.title: Suspected Ebola case on packed Congo river boat sparks testing rush
News.content:
Congolese health authorities have intercepted and detained a river boat on its way to the capital after a suspected Ebola case onboard.

Authorities have set up a mobile clinic to test more than 200 passengers after one of them disembarked and died earlier on the voyage.

The boat travelling from the northeastern commercial hub of Kisangani was stopped and held in Maluku, some 40 miles from Kinshasa.

Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) is dealing with its worst ever outbreak of the viral haemorrhagic fever, which has seen nearly 4,000 cases and killed around 1,801 people according to the latest government figures.

Samuel Roger Kamba, the health minister, said a 32-year-old man had disembarked in Pimu in Mongala province, before developing ‌suspected Ebola symptoms and dying.

“We did not say it was Ebola. We said there was a suspected case for which we are being cautious,” the health minister told a press conference, according to MediaCongo, a local news site.

He said there had been no other reports of deaths among travellers.

The virus has so far spread to five provinces, though more than 90 per cent of cases have been recorded in the north eastern Ituri region.

News.title: The best luxury hotels in the Cotswolds
News.content:
From gracious old farmsteads and magnificent manor houses to an ancient coaching inn creaking with Tudor character, the top luxury hotels in the Cotswolds combine a wonderful sense of history with contemporary style and outstanding modern British cuisine. Whether near picturesque Broadway in the north of the region or close to Bath in the south, location is a key attribute to them all: some offer serene escapes in acres of their own rolling parkland; others sit amid superb gardens; and several take over classic honey-stone villages that look as if they have been beamed in from a halcyon era of the past.

They all excel in providing creature comforts, whether crackling fires by kick-back sofas, canopy beds with soft throws, or suites with terraces and hot tubs. Facilities are top-notch too, ranging from beautiful bars and quiet terraces to blissful spas with inviting pools and even an opportunity for equine adventures. Read on to discover our pick of the best luxury hotels in the Cotswolds.

News.title: El Nino could cause explosion of rabid seals, animal health experts warn
News.content:
This year’s El Nino weather event risks propelling an outbreak of rabid seals around the world, the world’s animal health body has warned.

Countries in South America and Australasia are being urged to look for signs the deadly infectious disease has reached their waters, only two years after it was first confirmed in South Africa.

The 2024 discovery of rabies in South Africa’s Cape fur seals was the first significant outbreak ever found in marine mammals and has been described as a “significant shift in rabies ecology”.

More than 100 cases have been confirmed in South Africa and Namibia since then, raising fears that aggressive rabid seals could infect humans, pets and other wildlife.

Changing patterns in fish stocks caused by the El Nino phenomenon now potentially risk widening the spread, as uninfected seal populations migrate for food and come into contact with rabid colleagues.

Scientists believe warming sea temperatures off Antarctica could send seal populations northwards into Southern African waters, where they could be exposed to rabies.

They could then return to their home waters, taking the virus with them and infecting other seal populations.

News.title: ​Arteta’s ‘dynasty’ dream collides with Arsenal’s harsh reality
News.content:
Arsenal 1 Real Betis 3

Mikel Arteta says he wants to create a “dynasty” at Arsenal as he threw down the gauntlet to his players to retain their Premier League title and reach a “different level”.

Arsenal are on the verge of completing a £75m deal for Brazil midfielder Bruno Guimãraes from Newcastle and have not given up hope of landing Real Madrid winger Vinícius Júnior, who has been offered an improved contract by the Spanish giants.

The Premier League champions slumped to a 3-1 defeat to Real Betis in Dublin on Wednesday night, when they paid the price for individual errors and a lethargic, sloppy defensive display.

But that did little to quell Arteta’s ambitions for the new season. “I’m even more excited [about this season], and we’re going to go and attack every possible title because that’s the ambition that we have,” he said.

“We know that we have the ability. We will go from a strength to a strength as well, whether it’s with the players that we have to take them to a different level, and with the market that is still open to recruit as well, so we are very optimistic about it.

“All the work that we’ve done – that I’ve done through the summer – is to understand what we need to do to win again and to create a dynasty in this football club. That’s the aim.”

Despite Arteta’s bullishness, he conceded Arsenal would have to be a lot better than they were against Betis. When asked about the mood in the dressing room, he said: “Very upset, given a hard time. They are fuming, but this is good. That’s what we need.”

Telegraph Sport analyses some of the talking points from a disappointing evening at the Aviva Stadium.

No Saliba a concern

The importance of goalkeeper David Raya and centre-backs William Saliba and Gabriel Magalhães to Arsenal hardly needs overstating. Their title success was built on the foundations provided by that triumvirate at the back.

Raya has yet to report back from holiday after Spain’s World Cup triumph and Saliba is facing an extended spell on the sidelines with a back injury. Gabriel did appear for the second half but, watching this, Arteta is unlikely to have been dissuaded from the belief he needs another top defender to compensate for the loss of Saliba.

It may have been only Arsenal’s second game of pre-season, so a degree of legginess was understandable.

But the ease with which they were cut open and overloaded by the Spanish side, and the volume of individual errors, did not sit comfortably with Arteta with just over a fortnight until they kick off their title defence at home to newly promoted Coventry City.

Only once in 63 matches last season did Arsenal concede three goals in a single game but they were fortunate Betis did not score more. “In the first half there are two different things: to play well and to compete,” said Arteta, who saw his side trail 3-1 at the interval.

News.title: Ebola outbreak outpacing containment effort, WHO chief warns
News.content:
Caused by the rare Bundibugyo strain of Ebola, for which there are no vaccines or treatments, it has been extremely difficult to contain, according to experts on the ground.

“The outbreak is spreading faster than our scale-up of the response, with new cases doubling in some hotspots over the past week alone,” Dr Tedros said on X.

Part of the difficulty is that the virus was circulating undetected for weeks before the outbreak was formally declared in mid-May, leaving health officials even now racing to catch up with the spread.

Prof Placide Mbala, director of research, clinical trials and innovation at Africa CDC, told the Telegraph: “It’s mostly the fact we arrived a bit late. It took us some time before we detected this virus outbreak. And when we detected the outbreak, we already had a total of I can say more than 200 suspected cases. It’s been difficult to catch up. That’s where we are.”

While the DRC has a wealth of experience in tackling haemorrhagic fever outbreaks, the effects of that initial delay are still being felt.

Prof Mbala said: “We have some experience dealing with the cases, the labs, the communication, the infection prevention and control.

“We have some experience... But my observation is that we were very slow, and it’s why we’re in this situation.

“We are slow detecting the people, slow responding, we are slow deploying people, we are slow to recruit the community healthcare workers to improve contact tracing, we are slow to deploy the safe burials.”

DRC’s largest outbreak had previously been from 2018 to 2020, when 3,481 cases were recorded.

The West Africa outbreak recorded 28,616 cases and 11,310 deaths according to the WHO.

Prof Mbala said insecurity was also severely hampering attempts to curb the virus. The outbreak epicentre is in Ituri province, which has been wracked by ethnic strife for decades and is also home to militias competing to control mining.

He said: “There are many, many mining groups controlling most of the mining places. We have a big issue with those places, because they are places where the response team cannot go.”

Medics and aid workers have also been undermined by violent public distrust of their efforts.

Locals in the area have either doubted the existence of the virus, or have accused health teams of deliberately spreading the infection, or somehow benefiting from it.

More than a dozen health facilities have been set alight and several health workers have been killed.

Prof Mbala said: “The local people, they also sometimes are very upset, because they believe that it’s a kind of a business, and people who are coming here, they are getting a lot of money, [so] don’t want this disease to stop.”

He said he hoped that immunity was starting to rise in some areas and this would start to curb transmission.

However there was also a risk that people fleeing the outbreak would spread the virus further afield.

He said: “The second scenario is the fact we are seeing people moving from the affected area to new areas, to run away from the response team because they do not want to go to the treatment centre.

“And in complicity with their family members living in other areas, they are now the ones who are spreading the disease to new areas

“So we’ll see new places affected because people are moving around from the affected zone to the non-affected zone.”

News.title: Mykhailo Mudryk returns as Chelsea slip to Juventus defeat
News.content:
Chelsea 0 Juventus 1

Mykhailo Mudryk made his first Chelsea appearance since November 2024 as Xabi Alonso’s team succumbed to their second pre-season defeat.

Mudryk replaced Nicolas Jackson in the 82nd minute against Juventus, marking his return to competitive football after a long doping ban that was resolved this week thanks to changes in Wada regulations.

There were a couple of crosses delivered from the left flank by the Ukrainian winger, who could yet leave Chelsea on loan or on a permanent basis before the close of the transfer window.

Juventus were the victors though, thanks to a sumptuous 68th-minute goal by Kosovo winger Edon Zhegrova.

Alonso had 21 players on his bench, and made 12 second-half substitutions.

Levi Colwill and Cole Palmer featured in the defeat by 10-man Spurs on Saturday, but sat this game out as they continue to build fitness. Danny Welbeck did start though, reunited with former Brighton team-mate Joao Pedro up top.

Chelsea scored just one goal against Spurs and Juventus, but the thrust provided by right-back Marco Palestra in tandem with first Geovany Quenda and then Estevao was a bright spot for Alonso.

Chelsea continue their pre-season against AC Milan on Saturday, before they host Real Sociedad at Stamford Bridge on August 15.

They begin their Premier League campaign at Fulham in the Monday night slot on the opening weekend.

News.title: The underground lab where ‘princess mosquitoes’ are treated like royalty
News.content:
Beneath the grand Art Deco headquarters of the London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine lies a vast labyrinth inhabited by weird and wonderful creatures.

In this maze of subterranean labs, store rooms and corridors live colonies of disease-bearing insects and arachnids from all over the world, from bed bugs, sand flies and microscopic dust mites to the so-called kissing bugs that spread Chagas disease – a sinister condition that can cause its victims to drop dead of heart failure without warning, albeit decades after the first (silent) infection.

Behind a series of doors, contained in stacks of mesh boxes, you can even find the flies that spread trachoma, the Dickensian eye disease that is still a leading cause of blindness around the world. But be warned: entering the room is not for the faint of heart – the flies feed on human excrement and the smell is impossible to forget.

There are also many varieties of mosquito, including several species of the Anopheles genus that spread malaria, Culex and Aedes mosquitoes that are also vectors for human and animal diseases, and even Toxorhynchites, perhaps better known as the elephant mosquito, a friendly giant which doesn’t bite people but preys on other mosquitoes.

These animals have been studied intensely since the insectaries were established in the building’s vaults in the 1960s, underpinning many breakthroughs in the control, surveillance, and understanding of vector-borne diseases in the developing world.

LSHTM researchers are now looking closer to home. They have established the UK’s first laboratory colony of Aedes vexans mosquitoes, a species native to the British isles, to study whether they could harbour diseases like West Nile virus, Rift Valley fever, Zika or Japanese encephalitis.

Sports.title: Celtic's dream end to transfer window as £17m duo signs and World Cup star stays put
Sports.content:
Celtic's dream end to transfer window as £17m duo signs and World Cup star stays put

Celtic have made two attacking signings so far this window and are continuing their quest to build a Champions League-ready squad

View 5 Images Martin O'Neill plans to lead Celtic to more success this season (Image: Getty)

Celtic have signed the fewest players in the Scottish Premiership so far this summer. But Martin O'Neill has championed "quality over quantity."

‌



It was Camilo Duran who became the first to enter the gates of Parkhead, signing a five-year deal from Qarabag for around £6million. Next up was long-term target Kasper Hogh, who broke the club's transfer record when he arrived for £11m.

‌



The former Bodo/Glimt striker penned a four-year contract with the option of a further year. This duo scored a combined 10 goals in the Champions League last season. But fans will not be satisfied with these two signings to end the window, especially if they are to lose key players.

‌



Arne Engels has been heavily linked with a move to West Ham, with the Hoops bracing themselves for a third bid from the Championship side. Here, Mirror Football details what a perfect ending to the summer could look like for O'Neill's Celtic.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

OPINION Man Utd dream attack as Marcus Rashford exits plus free agent striker and World Cup star join by Abbie Meehan

‌



£17m duo signs

The main transfer target for Celtic is Real Oviedo's Haissem Hassan. The Egyptian winger impressed at the World Cup, assisting once and running the show for a period against Argentina.

Oviedo-based newspaper La Nuevo Espana claims that Celtic are pushing forward for the 24-year-old with a move to Parkhead now extremely likely. Sky Sports reports that an initial bid of £6m has been submitted and it could rise to around £9m if all bonuses are met.

View 5 Images A deal involving Hassan is moving quick (Image: Getty)

‌



Frosinone's Fares Ghedjemis is the other star Celtic are interested in - although they may have to compete with bitter rivals Rangers for the 23-year-old. The Hoops had been keen on the Algeria international in January but were unable to get a deal over the line.

Now, they have reignited this interest and Frosinone reportedly want at least £8m for his signature. It is understood that the Italian outfit rejected a bid of a similar price from the Gers, who have since moved on to target Celta Vigo winger Couhaib Driouech.

View 5 Images Signing Ghedjemis is a tough ask for the Hoops (Image: Getty)

‌



Celtic could now swoop in and stump up the cash for Ghedjemis. This would represent a dreamy £17m outlay for both players, but fans would see this as a reasonable price to pay ahead of their Champions League qualifying match-up with LASK.

World Cup star stays put

Alistair Johnston has been attracting considerable interest following his impressive performances for Canada at the World Cup. He started every game for the host nation and reached the round of 16, where he was eliminated 3-0 by Morocco.

Throughout his Celtic career, the right-back has 21 goal contributions and is beloved by the fanbase for his tough-tackling and positive attitude. Yet Everton have registered an interest in the 27-year-old, with O'Neill confirming that manager David Moyes contacted him regarding Johnston.

‌



View 5 Images Johnston has earned plenty of interest (Image: Getty)

He said: "In fairness, David Moyes did call me last week and say that there would be contact. But I don't know how far that has progressed, if it has at all.

"But yeah, that would be disappointing obviously. But I suppose it's to be expected, you know, players who have done well. Our job is to try and do our best to keep them. If that's not possible, naturally, we'll have to try and get replacements in. To replace those players would be a difficult task."

‌



It seems like O'Neill has kept to his word for the time being as the Toffees' interest in the right-back has cooled off. The Daily Record has confirmed that the Premier League side are working on other options after failing to meet Celtic's £15m asking price. If the club want to end the window in style, keeping Johnston is a must.

Defensive reinforcements arrive

Should Celtic retain Johnston, they may opt to add to their defensive line with another loan move for Brentford's Benjamin Arthur. The 20-year-old arrived at Parkhead last season under the same circumstances, spending the second half of the campaign in Glasgow.

View 5 Images Arthur could return on loan (Image: Getty)

Article continues below

Reports claim that the Hoops have already seen a bid from rejected, with Arthur part of the Bees' long-term plans. The defender only made four appearances in the 2025/26 season, but this was clearly enough to impress O'Neill.

A loan move could be beneficial for all parties, giving Arthur some European experience and allowing Celtic's defensive line to relax knowing they have back-up waiting in the wings.

Sports.title: 'I signed five-year deal at Arsenal and left after six months – I didn't trust manager's plan'
Sports.content:
'I signed five-year deal at Arsenal and left after six months – I didn't trust manager's plan'

Arsenal have handled plenty of transfers over the years but one five-year contract renewal ended prematurely

View 3 Images David Bentley's Arsenal tenure ended rather abruptly (Image: Getty)

David Bentley left Arsenal just six months after penning a five-year deal. The midfielder cited a lack of trust in Arsene Wenger, who was the last manager to guide the club to a league title before Mikel Arteta's success last season.

‌



The Gunners have earned major credit following their Premier League title win and some big names are being linked with a move to north London this summer. Arteta has secured Piero Hincapie, Illan Meslier and Christos Tzolis so far.

‌



But one former player who would have enjoyed more time in north London, in hindsight, is Bentley. The Englishman joined the Gunners at 13 and enjoyed his youth career in north London. He signed his first professional deal in 2001 and debuted under Wenger two years later. However, Bentley went out on loan to Norwich City in 2004 and handed in a transfer request upon his return.

‌



FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Arsenal forced to release short statement after Christos Tzolis debut READ MORE :

Arsenal could still add another blockbuster signing aside from Vinicius Jr or Bruno Guimaraes READ MORE :

He secured a move to Blackburn in January 2006 after impressing on loan and eventually signed for Arsenal's rivals Tottenham for £15million in 2008. But, during an appearance on the Undr The Cosh podcast, Bentley admitted that he should've spent more time with the Gunners but didn't have confidence in Wenger's plans.

View 3 Images Bentley spoke out about his time as a Gunner (Image: Undr The Cosh/YouTube)

‌



He said: "When we were playing, you were under much more pressure than players are nowadays. Much more pressure. Because, if you found yourself out the team, you were criticised more than you are now. Now, you're a squad player. Just having a rest, not in the squad today.

"[I left Arsenal because] I wanted to play. I signed a five-year deal and left after six months! Wenger was like, 'No, do this.' He had a plan, didn't he? But I couldn't see that plan. Didn't trust it.

"Potentially, I could have stayed; I should have stayed. Remember, I saw the young lads come through, Cesc. I made my debut with Fabregas - my full debut.

‌



"Absolutely unbelievable performance from him. We beat Wolves 5-1 at Highbury. He dominated the game at 15 years old. I was only like 17. Eighteen months older, or two years older than him."

After leaving Arsenal, Bentley's time at Blackburn was the peak of his career. The midfielder was named the club's Player of the Year in 2007 as he was linked with a move to Manchester United.

View 3 Images The Englishman would go on to sign for Spurs (Image: Getty)

Article continues below

In 2008, he headed to Spurs and his first goal for his new side was arguably his greatest. Bentley fired in a 43-yard volley during a 4-4 draw with his former club Arsenal.

This incredible goal was not indicative of what was to come, as the ex-England international would go on loan four times while at Spurs. He had stints at Birmingham City, West Ham, FC Rostov and a return to Blackburn before retiring at just 29 after being released by Tottenham.

Sports.title: Stevenage down Wycombe with stoppage-time winner to book place in Carabao Cup second round
Sports.content:
Stevenage down Wycombe with stoppage-time winner to book place in Carabao Cup second round

Stevenage scored in the dying embers of Friday's Carabo Cup first round draw with fellow League One side Wycombe to claim a 2-1 victory.

View 3 Images Stevenage manager Alex Revell saw his side claim a stoppage-time victory over Wycombe in the Carabao Cup on Friday

Stevenage debutant Josh Magennis scored an injury-time winner to secure a 2-1 victory over Wycombe and book Alex Revell's side's place in the Carabao Cup second round.

‌



The Northern Irish international, 35, who signed from Exeter City this summer, headed it home in the fifth minute of injury time to break Wycombe hearts at Adams Park on Friday, ensuring it would be a winning start to the competitive season for The Boro.

‌



On the same night, Wolves comfortably saw off League Two side Port Vale 3-0 at Molineux while Middlesbrough defeated Wrexham 1-0 in an all-Championship affair in the other two Carabao Cup games.

‌



Carabao Cup first round TV guide: How to watch every match live this weekend READ MORE :

Both Wycombe and Stevenage welcomed fresh faces into their starting XI's following relatively busy summers, with the hosts giving competitive debuts to goalkeeper Conor Hazard, winger Silko Thomas, right back Sam Parker, and veteran defender Steve Cook, while the visitors started former Burton defender Terence Vancooten from the off.

It took a while for the game to get going, with nothing much to shout about inside the opening 25 minutes as both sides failed to convert several crosses into the box.

However, it was the experienced Dan Kemp in midfield for Stevenage who finally broke the deadlock just before the half-hour mark, pouncing on a poor touch from Wycombe defender Connor Taylor before taking the ball round his man and burying it into the near bottom corner.

‌



View 3 Images Wycombe Wanderers manager Michael Duff saw his side fall to a 2-1 defeat on home soil

The visitors could've doubled their lead within a minute as they countered at pace and caught Wycombe sleeping, though winger Phoenix Patterson could only fire low and hard into Hazard's arms.

Much to the relief of the home fans, however, Wycombe finally dragged themselves back into the game and leveled the scores in the 39th minute, with Scottish midfielder Ewan Henderson playing a neat one-two with Thomas before finding the bottom left corner.

‌



Wycombe ended the first half the better of the two sides, though Kemp came so close to doubling his and Stevenage's tally with a piledriver from the edge of the penalty area that smacked the underside of the crossbar before bouncing back out.

The Chairboys continued their positive play into the second half as the lively Fred Onyedinma caused plenty of problems down the right, while several penalty shouts for the hosts were also waived away by referee Jamie O'Connor.

View 3 Images Stevenage midfielder Dan Kemp opened the scoring in the first half

Article continues below

On the opposite flank, debutant Thomas was also causing problems for Stevenage's defense, but Wycombe just couldn't carve out an opening that would give them the lead in the tie.

Both teams pushed for a winner in the final embers of the game, but neither could find the winner they so desperately craved, until Magennis, fresh off the substitutes bench, popped up with a header in the dying seconds to win the game for Stevenage and book their spot in Monday's second round draw.

Both sides are next in action on the opening day of the League One season next weekend, when Wycombe travel to face Blackpool and Stevenage face Burton, both on Saturday, Aug. 15 (3 p.m.).

Sports.title: Man Utd contacted by Newcastle after launching Lewis Hall transfer enquiry
Sports.content:
Man Utd contacted by Newcastle after launching Lewis Hall transfer enquiry

Newcastle have sold Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali this summer, with Bruno Guimaraes also set to leave, and attention has now turned to Manchester United target Lewis Hall

View 2 Images Newcastle don't want to sell Lewis Hall (Image: Serena Taylor/Newcastle United via Getty Images)

Newcastle have made it clear to Manchester United that Lewis Hall is not for sale this summer at any price. United are keen to sign a left-back in this window and have kept an eye on Hall for some time, but it seems Michael Carrick won't get his man this summer.

‌



United prioritised central midfield in the early stages of the window, with Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos arriving from Aston Villa and Chelsea respectively for a combined £87million.

‌



Left-back is now a position on the agenda, with Carrick wanting competition for Luke Shaw, who impressed last season but has a chequered injury history. Academy graduate Harry Amass would be allowed to leave for the right price, while last summer's signing Diego Leon has failed to kick on so far and Tyrell Malacia left on a free transfer.

‌



Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui can both play left-back if needed, but Patrick Dorgu has shone further forward, convincing United to go back into the market.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

United thought they could take advantage of the turmoil at Newcastle this summer, with Eddie Howe being replaced by Matthias Jaissle. But the departures of Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and the pending exit of Bruno Guimaraes to Arsenal has worked against them.

‌



Sky Sports reports that Newcastle have told United in no uncertain terms to look elsewhere. The Magpies first communicated their stance two weeks ago and consider the matter to be settled.

Newcastle's hierarchy are under pressure to steady the ship following the exits of Howe, Gordon, Tonali and Guimaraes. Sporting director Ross Wilson has taken the approach of publicly explaining the £75m sale of Guimaraes to Arsenal.

"What we had to weigh up was, very respectfully from Bruno with his behaviour towards us, very emotionally as well, he effectively told us he wanted to leave and move on," he said.

‌



View 2 Images Bruno Guimaraes' exit has strengthened Newcastle's stance on Lewis Hall (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

"That doesn't mean he can go, but it certainly plays a part in what our thinking is when we hit a certain range of number. There's no part in saying it was part of our strategy and was in our thinking this summer - it wasn't. But we have got to be flexible and react to things that happen."

Unlike Guimaraes, Hall is not agitating for a move. The 21-year-old joined Newcastle for £35m from Chelsea three summers ago and has been a regular fixture on the left side of defence.

Article continues below

With Hall appearing to be a dead end, United could turn their attention to Racing Santander's Jorge Salinas, who is considered to be a viable alternative. The 19-year-old is highly rated and has a €16m (£13.7m) release clause, although United could face competition from Barcelona. Bologna's Jhon Lucumi, who is valued at €25m (£21.7m) is another option.

Sports.title: FA announce changes after tragic death of ex-Arsenal footballer aged 21
Sports.content:
FA announce changes after tragic death of ex-Arsenal footballer aged 21

Former Arsenal youngster Billy Vigar suffered a significant brain injury back in September last year, with changes now being put in place by the Football Association

View 2 Images Billy Vigar passed away in September (Image: David Price/Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

The Football Association (FA) have announced that solid walls around the perimeter of pitches have been banned following the tragic death of Billy Vigar. The former Arsenal youth player died from a head injury after colliding with a wall last season.

The incident occurred with Vigar playing for Chichester City against Wingate & Finchley FC back in September. The 21-year-old collided with a concrete wall surrounding the pitch, resulting in a significant brain injury.

Vigar was part of Arsenal’s youth sides before moving to Hastings United in 2024. He signed with Chichester City last summer, a few months before his death.

The wall at Wingate & Finchley FC has now been removed, with the FA confirming a review of pitch surroundings for non-league grounds . The findings of the review have now been released.

It has been confirmed that the FA: "no longer permits solid brick, breeze block or concrete barriers around pitches across the National League system for men [steps 1-6], and the Women's National League [tiers 3-4]".

UEFA could boycott 5 tournaments in next 11 months after new Gianni Infantino statement READ MORE :

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Article continues below

In a statement, the FA added: "Any existing solid brick, breeze block or concrete barriers must be removed as soon as reasonably practicable, or covered with suitable protection if they cannot be removed for structural reasons. We have informed the clubs at this level that will be required to take action as a result of these changes.

"Matches may continue to be played at affected grounds during this period; however, clubs should assess the safety of their pitch perimeter barriers on an ongoing basis, and where alterations to these structures have been recommended during this review, they should develop a plan to complete any such alterations within a reasonable timeframe."

Non-league clubs will be helped with funding the changes with the money coming from both the FA and the Premier League. The Press Association reports that 160 of the 900 clubs who play at the levels have been contacted over changes that will have to be made to their stadiums.

View 2 Images The FA have announced changes following the youngster's tragic death (Image: Getty Images)

The FA added: "The initial phase of the programme is already underway, and we will continue to provide full support to the clubs involved in this process.”

Following the announcement, a PFA spokesperson said: “Following the tragic death of Billy Vigar last year, we again highlighted these concerns and made clear our view that the lack of progress and leadership on this issue had been unacceptable.

"As part of working groups set up by the FA following Billy's death, we pushed for the FA's Stadium Accreditation criteria to be amended to ban these types of walls so that there is a clear and centralised policy for clubs to follow.

"Given that, it's a welcome step that the FA's regulations have now been changed to reflect that position.

"However, it will now be important for progress on the removal of such walls - and effective mitigation of risks ahead of their removal - to be properly monitored, and for clubs to be given the support they need so that these changes can happen as soon as possible. Player safety must always come first."

Sports.title: Arsenal could break unwanted transfer record as Mikel Arteta green lights two deals
Sports.content:
Arsenal could break unwanted transfer record as Mikel Arteta green lights two deals

Arsenal are still chasing a blockbuster signing in the summer transfer window and Mikel Arteta's side need to lay the groundwork first by making space in the squad

View 2 Images Mikel Arteta knows that sales are needed this summer (Image: Stuart MacFarlane/Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

Arsenal could finally eclipse their record sale with Gabriel Martinelli attracting interest from Turkey. The Gunners' focus recently has been on Bruno Guimaraes and Vinicius Junior, but exits are also in the pipeline.

‌



Guimaraes is poised to join Mikel Arteta's side for £75million after a compromise was reached with Newcastle. But the pursuit of Vinicius has ended in defeat, with the Brazilian forward set to sign a new contract with Real Madrid.

‌



Arsenal will now turn their attention to other targets as they chase a blockbuster deal, and while the identity of their alternative signing is not yet known, the groundwork is being laid. Leandro Trossard (Besiktas), Jakub Kiwior (Porto), Karl Hein (Werder Bremen) and Christian Norgaard (Everton) are currently the only players to leave and bring in transfer fees this summer.

‌



It is something that sporting director Andrea Berta knows he must address, especially if a world-class forward like Julian Alvarez and a centre-back to cover for the injured William Saliba is to arrive before the deadline passes on September 1.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Liverpool's firm stance on Djed Spence transfer as Reds battle defensive injury crisis READ MORE :

Martinelli has entered the final year of his contract with Arsenal, posing the possibility of his exit, over seven years after he joined the club. The 25-year-old has 62 goals in 278 appearances for the club since his £6million move in 2019, but his time may have come.

‌



Arsenal are reportedly considering a sale to Galatasaray, who are interested in landing the Brazil international. And were a move to come to fruition it could see Martinelli become Arsenal's record sale, with the £35m earned for Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain's move to Liverpool in 2019 surprisingly still the high-water mark for the club.

Their inability to sell well has become an issue for Arsenal, who have often seen their rivals out-perform them. Trossard pulled in £17m from Besiktas, while Norgaard earned just £7m from Everton. If Arsenal are to achieve their goals in terms of incomings then Martinelli and Gabriel Jesus could become facilitators.

View 2 Images Gabriel Martinelli and Gabriel Jesus could both be sold (Image: Stuart MacFarlane/Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

‌



Jesus has become a fringe player at Arsenal, with Viktor Gyokeres and Kai Havertz ahead of him in the pecking order and is attracting interest from Napoli and AC Milan. The 29-year-old's contract expires in June 2027, meaning this window is Arsenal's last realistic chance to earn a decent fee.

Arsenal are understood to be seeking a fee in the region of the £17m they got for Trossard, but as time ticks by in August they could be forced to compromise.

Arteta knows that Arsenal must strengthen their squad this summer if they are to stand any chance of defending their Premier League title in 2026/27. "We are really active, trying to improve and evolve the team. That's clear," he said in a post-match press conference after facing Girona on the weekend.

Article continues below

"We expect to have movements in the next few weeks, obviously, because we want to get better like anybody else. And you can just see it. The transfer market and our opponents, what we are doing, we won't sit still. And we are very ambitious in what we want to do."

Sports.title: 'I'd rather fight Aaron for world title' - Walsh dismisses Stevie McKenna call-out
Sports.content:
Callum Walsh would entertain a fight against Aaron McKenna over Stephen McKenna, insisting all-Irish clashes only make sense with the world title on the line.

Walsh (16-0, 11 KOs) fights former European champion Tyler Denny on the undercard of Aaron McKenna's IBF world middleweight title showdown with Etinosa Oliha at Dublin's 3Arena this Saturday, live on Sky Sports.

It's the headline act of six middleweight bouts on a stacked card that also sees Stephen McKenna face Owen O'Neill over eight rounds before assuming corner duties for his younger, world title-chasing brother.

Walsh has been identified as a potential future opponent by Stephen McKenna (16-1, 15 KOs), but the unbeaten 25-year-old believes he's already at another level.

Responding to McKenna's challenge, Walsh told Sky Sports: "If there's anyone that I'm looking at, it would be the fella with the world title, not the fella with the loss.

"In my mind, it doesn't make sense unless it's for a world title. There are bigger names than Stevie McKenna calling me out.

"Shane Mosley Jr is a bigger fight than Stevie McKenna. His brother Aaron is fighting for the world title. If I was going to fight either of them, I'd fight Aaron for the world title."

Image: Walsh on the scales ahead of his middleweight fight against Denny (Photo by Ed Mulholland/Zuffa Boxing)

'It makes sense for him, not for me'

Walsh believes an all-Irish fight without a world title on the line could needlessly jeopardise the momentum middleweights are currently generating in Ireland.

"It's a big time for Irish boxing," he added. "As an Irish fighter from such a small place, there are three of us now in Zuffa Boxing. Why would we want to eliminate each other unless it's for a world title?

"If it's for a world title, at least you can get paid for it. You're going to be able to sell out an arena and put on a big show for everyone involved. Why have an all-Irish fight on an undercard somewhere when it doesn't make sense?

"It makes sense for him. It makes no sense at all for me. His brother's fighting for the world title. There are bigger names calling me out. I've had bigger fights. It doesn't make any sense."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Stevie McKenna is determined to have an all-Ireland clash against Walsh should both of them emerge victorious at Zuffa Boxing 10 this weekend

Walsh believes Stephen McKenna would be better served avenging his sole loss as a professional, a majority-decision defeat to Lee Cutler in 2024.

"He doesn't even want to fight the fella who beat him," he said. "He was asked if he wanted a rematch and he said no.

"Go back and fight the fella who beat you. That's the one I'd be looking at if I was him. He's in the same division, the same league, and he's begging for the rematch."

'I'll fight Aaron or the other fella'

Walsh, who fights in Dublin for the first time since knocking out Przemyslaw Runowski in two rounds in 2024, is confident he can overcome Denny and believes Aaron McKenna will become Ireland's newest world champion.

Victory for both men would set up the mouth-watering prospect of an all-Irish world title fight, and Walsh insists he would have no problem facing Aaron should he emerge as champion.

"I don't know much about his opponent, to be honest," Walsh added. "I'm sure Aaron will win. I presume he will.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Walsh insists he's not complacent ahead of Saturday's fight with Denny, while the former European champion is confident he can cause the upset in Dublin

"It's a big opportunity and a big night for him to go out there, perform and win the world title in Dublin. I think he will.

"If Aaron wins and they want me to fight him, I'll fight him. If he doesn't win, maybe I'll fight the other fella.

"I just fight whoever they tell me to. I'm not out here calling anybody out. It's just the same old habits."

Watch Zuffa Boxing 10, headlined by Aaron McKenna vs Etinosa Oliha live on Sky Sports this Saturday.

Sports.title: Araujo set for surprise Liverpool loan move
Sports.content:
Liverpool have agreed a surprise deal for Barcelona defender Ronald Araujo to join on loan for the season.

The deal is a straight loan for the 27-year-old, who signed a new contract until 2031 last year.

The Uruguay international joined Barcelona B in 2018 before being promoted to the first team in 2019.

The 27-year-old centre-back will add to Andoni Iraola's options at the heart of his defence following the departure of Ibrahima Konate to Real Madrid and fitness concerns over relatively inexperienced 21-year-old Jeremy Jacquet.

The summer signing from Rennes has made fewer than 100 senior career appearances and has not featured in pre-season yet after missing the second half of last season following shoulder surgery.

Sports.title: McKenna vs Oliha and Walsh vs Denny big-fight predictions
Sports.content:
Experts have their say ahead of the Aaron McKenna vs Etinosa Oliha middleweight world championship clash and Callum Walsh's crucial clash with Tyler Denny, live on Sky Sports from 7pm.

Aaron McKenna vs Etinosa Oliha

Chris Billam-Smith (former cruiserweight champion): McKenna's got so much to his game I think. He's shown he can box a bit but he's got an intensity and a workrate. He punches hard enough to get people's respect. We saw a lot from him in the Liam Smith fight, of what he can do. I will pick him to win. Probably on points but he could overwhelm him as well.

Johnny Nelson (former cruiserweight champion): Aaron McKenna gets an inside-the-distance stoppage win I think. His engine, his pace will be too much.

Oliha can't afford to get hit too easily because McKenna won't leave you alone. It's a good fight, especially for McKenna boxing in Dublin for the first time in his professional career.

I think McKenna in the first half of the fight.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Aaron McKenna and Etinosa Oliha locked in a tense face-off ahead of their IBF world middleweight title clash on August 8

Johnny Fisher (heavyweight star): McKenna's been based in America for a little while, this is now his homecoming fight. Tremendous amateur record, hopefully that pedigree comes through. I think this crowd will give him that extra lift. If he uses that crowd and doesn't let it be detrimental to him, that's what's going to carry him over the line.

Callum Walsh (middleweight contender): I presume that Aaron will win. It's a big night, a big opportunity for him to go out there and perform and to win the world title in Dublin. I think he will.

Connor Coyle (middleweight contender): I think McKenna will win, I think he'll win on points. I know McKenna's boxing, I've known him growing up through Irish boxing. That's why I know he's a good boxer.

I think he'll become IBF world champion on Saturday night.

Sam Hickey (middleweight prospect): Oliha, he's obviously a good level but I think Aaron McKenna will get the job done. Aaron's a good fighter. He's got pedigree.

It's a kind of a new breed of middleweight coming through.

Patrick O'Connor (cruiserweight prospect): I think Aaron McKenna will win by decision. From what I see, I think Aaron is going to beat him on points, maybe late stoppage. It's going to be great for Irish boxing to have a world champion, it's a big thing.

Owen O'Neill (middleweight fighter): McKenna on points. He's a very technical boxer, he's very smart and he's very good. I've been in there with him [in sparring] and he's tall, he's got big arms and he punches hard too.

Callum Walsh vs Tyler Denny

Billam-Smith: The Callum Walsh fight is interesting. I know Tyler, I've watched him a lot over the years and he always brings it. And if you're not on your game and you switch off and your head's elsewhere, he'll beat you.

He's a good fighter. He's shown it. His first breakout win was Brad Rea, a really good win at the time.

He's not affected by his losses. He's been beat, come back and won and he's looked good doing so. So it's a really interesting one. I can't really pick a winner because I know how good Callum is but nothing would surprise me in that fight.

Nelson: On paper you'd lean towards Walsh because of where he's at in his career, but then you look at what Tyler Denny's done, the heads he's snatched because they've looked through him, looked past him. This is going to be a test of Walsh's heart, Walsh's desire. Because Tyler Denny is not one of those guys that folds easily.

I'd lean towards Tyler, but on points.

If he establishes his jab, fights at range, it's Walsh's fight to win. I pick Walsh but I like Tyler Denny, I like his tenacity. He's fought some of the top guys in the division. Although I pick Walsh I wouldn't be surprised if it goes the other way.

Hickey: Tyler Denny's a good fighter, he can make people look average. If you're not on your best night he can make a mess of the fight. Look at his last fight with George Liddard, it was a close one.

That's an interesting fight because Callum Walsh has obviously made his career over in America. You'll really see the level that Walsh is at. It's different because when you move up the levels, fighters can take the power. If Walsh is a serious puncher he can maybe get him out of there but he's moving up the levels so he might end up having to go the rounds and we'll see how good a fighter he is.

Sports.title: Debut Lankshear goal sees Boro past Wrexham as Wolves & Stevenage progress
Sports.content:
Will Lankshear's debut strike ensured Middlesbrough made a winning start to the season as they beat Wrexham 1-0 in the Carabao Cup first round.

Lankshear, a £10m summer signing from Tottenham, scored the only goal of the game in the 61st minute as he hooked home an excellent first-time volley.

Middlesbrough almost claimed a seventh-minute opener, but while Adilson Malanda prodded Sebastian Berhalter's cross goalwards from close range, Danny Ward kept the ball out with a superb point-blank save.

Danny Imray wasted a decent chance for Wrexham when he failed to make a proper connection from Callum Doyle's cross, and the visitors went close again six minutes before the break when Sam Smith fired a low shot into the legs of Sol Brynn after he was rolled into space by Nathan Broadhead.

Lankshear came close with an effort that was curled just over the bar at the start of the second half, but the 21-year-old did not have to wait too much longer for his first goal in a Boro shirt.

Leo Castledine headed Jeremy Sarmiento's cross into Lankshear's path, and the striker swivelled neatly before hooking a superb first-time volley into the far corner.

Boro almost doubled their lead with three minutes remaining, but Morgan Whittaker's low strike rebounded off the post.

Wolves coast past Port Vale as Jimenez makes return

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of Wolves' clash with Port Vale in the first round of the Carabao Cup.

Wolves progressed with a comfortable 3-0 win over Port Vale in which all three goals came in the first half. Adam Armstrong, Andre and Fer Lopez took the game away from the League Two side as Cesar Peixoto marked his first game in charge with a win.

Jon Brady's Port Vale had opportunities. Jordan Lawrence-Gabriel hooked an extraordinary chance away from the Wolves goal before the break, before Mo Faal's low penalty was saved by the legs of Dan Bentley to deny the travelling fans a consolation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Port Vale's Jordan Lawrence-Gabriel misses a chance from six yards out in his side's Carabao Cup clash with Wolves.

The Wolves supporters among the crowd of 21,360 at Molineux were more interested in serenading their returning hero. Raul Jimenez, the club's Premier League top scorer, re-signed this summer after three years at Fulham and came on as a late substitute.

The Mexican centre-forward did fire off one fierce shot on goal but he was unable to mark the occasion with a goal that would have been cruel on a competitive Port Vale side. But it is Wolves who take their place in the second round of the Carabao Cup.

Stevenage strike late to beat Wycombe

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the first round Carabao Cup match between Wycombe Wanderers and Stevenage.

New signing Josh Magennis headed the winner in the dying seconds to send Stevenage through to the second round of the Carabao Cup with a 2-1 victory at Wycombe.

It was a fitting start to the Boro's 50th anniversary season as substitute Magennis, a summer capture from Exeter, rose to score from Phoenix Patterson's left-wing corner in the fifth minute of second-half stoppage time.

The visitors had shaken off early pressure to take the lead against the run of play in the 27th minute.

Midfielder Dan Kemp took advantage of hesitancy in the Wycombe defence as he raced through to fire home a low shot.

That stung the home side into action and Ewan Henderson equalised in the 38th minute. Winger Silko Thomas crossed from the left and the Scot slipped through the visiting defence to score right-footed from just outside the six-yard box.

Stevenage scared their Sky Bet League One rivals again on the stroke of half-time when Kemp rattled the bar with a shot from the edge of the box.

Wycombe took control after the break but struggled to break through.

New boy Emre Tezgel, on for Cauley Woodrow, was thwarted by Boro skipper Carl Piergianni as he attempted to force home Thomas' cross from the left in the 77th minute before Magennis settled the issue.

The Carabao Cup is back for the 2026/27 season, with every first-round tie available to watch live on Sky Sports!

West Ham, Burnley and Leicester are among those in action on Saturday - and you can follow the goals as they go in from all 29 ties on Soccer Saturday.

Every match from the opening round will be shown live on Sky Sports, with clubs from the Championship, League One and League Two entering the competition.

Sports.title: New Zealand begin South Africa tour with flattering win over Stormers
Sports.content:
New Zealand's first full-scale tour of South Africa in 30 years began with an underwhelming 38-21 win over the Stormers.

The scoreline flattered a scratch All Blacks side which was favoured to win comfortably.

The makeshift Stormers - in pre-season mode - rallied twice to tie the score, which was knotted at 14-14 until 13 minutes to go.

When the Stormers lost their second scrum-half and had no more reserve backs, the patched-up backline was ruthlessly exposed by New Zealand, who scored three tries in the last eight minutes.

But the result only papered over a performance that was blighted by ill-discipline, three yellow cards, and a struggling set-piece.

They overcame those with six tries to three by the Stormers in front of a 47,130 crowd.

Image: New Zealand started with an unconvincing win on their tour of South Africa

The good news for the All Blacks was they appeared to finish with no major injuries, seven players made their first appearance in the black jersey this year, and two more made their debuts off the bench; prop Siale Lauaki and inside back Josh Jacomb.

But the most impressive players in the stadium were Stormers fly-half Yaqeen Ahmed, who looked comfortably cool in his first-class debut at age 20, and flanker Deon Fourie, the dynamo who will be 40 next month.

"It was a good introduction for us to South African rugby," said New Zealand head coach Dave Rennie. "We started ​very well and it looked like which side had the ball ⁠got rewarded by the referee.

"When we had ⁠the ball we were really dangerous. We knew they would bring line speed [in defence]. We just weren't quite clinical enough ‌to expose them.

"They came at us with their set-piece and we need to be better in those areas. We expected a lot of aerial attacks and we probably did ‌not handle that as well as we could have."
