World.title: Controversy trails Nnewi market billion naira shops allocation
World.content:
Governor Soludo

By Vincent Ujumadu

Controversy is trailing the billions of naira allegedly generated from the allocation of shops at the Agbedo Motor Parts Market in the industrial town of Nnewi, with some stakeholders questioning the whereabouts of the money several months after the allocation exercise.

A prominent Nnewi businessman had alleged that the over N4 billion realized from the allocation of shops at the market was misappropriated and shared as political patronage.

However, the Chairman of the Market, Mr. Kennedy Oguaju wondered why people should be making unsubstantiated allegation on issues concerning the project, which he described as wholly a private initiative of the traders. “The market was financed and owned by traders and executed through a contractor appointed by the market committee”, Oguaju said.

Reacting on the issue, the chairman of Nnewi North Local Government Area, Hon. Echezona Anazodo, said he was surprised to see a viral video alleging that he was involved in the allocation of the shops, insisting that the council had no financial involvement in the privately executed market development project. According to Anazodo, neither he nor the council collected or managed any funds connected with the Agbedo Motor Parts Market project.

“I did not collect any money from anybody. Neither I nor the local government received or managed any funds for that project.

“We were aware of the project and facilitated its implementation, but the work itself was carried out by a contractor appointed by the market committee.

“I encourage members of the public to visit the project site and speak with the people directly involved. They should investigate what actually transpired and verify whether any money was paid to the local government,” he said.

Anazodo acknowledged that Agbedo Motor Parts Market project was a private arrangement between the market stakeholders, who own the property, and a contractor engaged by the market committee, adding that the local government’s role was limited to providing security and creating an enabling environment for the execution of the project.

World.title: Can Tinubu dvice Governors On What He Controls? By Emmanuel Aziken
World.content:
Aziken

President Bola Tinubu’s extraordinary intervention in the freezing of an Osun State Government account by the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission has brought into sharp relief a question that has increasingly shadowed his presidency: who exactly acts in the President’s name, and how much of what is done around him carries his prior knowledge and approval?

The EFCC had secured a court order restricting withdrawals from an Osun State statutory allocation account as part of an investigation into the alleged fraudulent handling of about N11 billion in Ecology Funds, Intervention Funds and FAAC allocations. Coming barely days before the August 15 governorship election, however, the action inevitably acquired a political colour.

Tinubu apparently recognised the danger. In a personally signed statement, he directed the EFCC to return to court immediately to vacate the order. He said he was “deeply embarrassed”, not by the commission performing its statutory duty, but by the timing of the action, and stressed that no federal institution should create the impression that Abuja was trying to influence the Osun election.

That distinction is important. The President did not absolve Governor Ademola Adeleke’s administration of any allegation under investigation. Neither did he order the EFCC to abandon its statutory responsibilities. What he did was insist that law enforcement must not become indistinguishable from partisan warfare.

In the circumstances, it was the correct intervention.

Osun is particularly sensitive terrain for Tinubu. The state is one where his APC has suffered two politically significant defeats in recent years. Adeleke defeated incumbent APC Governor Gboyega Oyetola in 2022, polling 403,371 votes against Oyetola’s 375,027. Months later, in the 2023 presidential election, Tinubu lost Osun to the PDP’s Atiku Abubakar, who polled 354,366 votes against Tinubu’s 343,945.

The political confrontation therefore has history behind it.

It became even more complicated by the crisis within the PDP and Adeleke’s flirtation with the APC. Adeleke’s camp has publicly maintained that he did not reject an invitation to join the APC but that his movement was resisted by Oyetola and the Osun APC establishment. Adeleke eventually moved to Accord, on whose platform he is seeking re-election.

For some within the APC, the calculation may have appeared straightforward: with the PDP weakened and federal power behind the ruling party, Adeleke could be politically overwhelmed.

That calculation underestimates the governor.

Whatever assessment anyone makes of Adeleke’s record in office, he belongs to one of Nigeria’s most enduring political families. His father, Senator Raji Ayoola Adeleke, an ally of Chief Obafemi Awolowo, was elected to the Senate on the Unity Party of Nigeria platform during the Second Republic. His elder brother, Isiaka Adeleke, became Osun’s first civilian governor in 1992 and subsequently served twice in the Senate. Ademola himself represented Osun West in the Senate before becoming governor.

That is political infrastructure accumulated across generations.

Then there is the Adeleke family’s extraordinary cultural reach. Governor Adeleke’s nephew, Davido, is one of Africa’s most recognisable music stars and gives the family access to a youthful constituency that conventional politicians would pay heavily to cultivate. Celebrity cannot substitute for organisation or performance, but in a close election its mobilisation value should not be dismissed.

Tinubu’s intervention consequently does more than rescue Osun from a potentially destabilising confrontation days before an election. It also protects the President himself.

The more troubling question is how such a politically explosive action came to be taken at such a politically explosive moment before presidential intervention became necessary. The EFCC is an institution with statutory responsibilities and had obtained a court order. Yet the President’s public embarrassment over the timing raises legitimate questions about political judgment and coordination within the federal establishment.

It would be reckless to conclude, without evidence, that “rogue elements” deliberately engineered the affair in Tinubu’s name. But it is reasonable to ask whether officials around the presidency and federal institutions sufficiently appreciate that their actions can carry consequences for the President’s credibility.

Tinubu therefore has a larger assignment than merely extinguishing the Osun fire.

Where federal institutions repeatedly take controversial steps that force the President into public reversals or damage his political standing, he must establish who authorised what, on what information and with what appreciation of the consequences. Accountability cannot stop at correcting decisions after public outrage.

There is a biblical injunction in Proverbs 25:5: “Remove the wicked from the king’s presence, and his throne will be established through righteousness.” The principle remains relevant to political leadership. A ruler is ultimately judged not only by his intentions but also by the conduct of those exercising authority around him.

Tinubu has acted wisely in Osun by insisting that the August 15 election must not carry the stain of federal interference. The APC is entitled to campaign vigorously for Bola Oyebamiji. Adeleke is equally entitled to defend his mandate. The EFCC is entitled to investigate credible allegations. But the people of Osun alone must decide who governs them.

If Tinubu wants this intervention to count towards his legacy, he must go beyond Osun. He should ensure that nobody, whether political ally, presidential aide or federal official, can weaponise the enormous authority of the Nigerian state for partisan purposes.

The best “fix” for Osun is therefore not an APC victory or an Adeleke victory. It is a credible election whose outcome cannot reasonably be attributed to Abuja.

That would be a victory for Tinubu too.

World.title: Making your roots proud of you, by Muyiwa Adetiba
World.content:
All Igbobians – students of Igbobi College – must know about the big fruit tree between the Dining Hall and the Chapel. This tree has been there like forever serving as a rendezvous of sorts for many school events. I believe it is one of the fixtures that can tell the story of the school. Some forty-five years ago, a handful of Old Igbobians met there for an event. I remember it was early evening and visibility was low.

We were asked to introduce ourselves by stating name, set, house and the sports we participated in while in school. It was not an uncommon ritual. I had just finished this chore when I heard a voice behind me say ‘so Muyiwa Adetiba came to Igbobi. No wonder.’ I looked back in surprise to identify the voice. It was from an older man, probably a senior who had left school before I entered. I met a warm smile as I nodded my head in acknowledgement and respect. Honestly, it was at the time, one of the best compliments I had received in years. All true Old Igbobians would know why.

The moral and intellectual standards set by the school were high and this seemingly off-handed compliment, was for me, a tacit acknowledgement, that I had at least, met some of them. I was to be a proud recipient of a few ‘no wonder’ comments from Old Igbobians during my years as an interviewer. Some of them were probably in school about the time I was born. Quite a few willingly helped me to get difficult interviews by either using their connections or vouching for me. A good example was Chief Chris Ogunbanjo, an Old Igbobian, whose vouching for me overcame the understandable reluctance of Chief Justice Fatai Williams when I wanted to interview him immediately after the Supreme Court judgement on Chief Obafemi Awolowo’s presidential bid.

Another notable ‘endorsement’ came about ten years ago after I had more or else rested my pen. Someone I have a great respect for, an Old Igbobian whom I never met in school, approached me to help a prominent Nigerian with his memoirs. I don’t just jump into working on anybody’s memoirs. For me, it is a labor of love that I have to be able to invest emotionally in. Fortunately, this prominent Nigerian was someone I had admired from afar so it wasn’t difficult to accept. Unknown to me, this great man was reluctant. His fear was that he had sensitive stories he wanted to be careful in divulging. When he was told that I was not only a fellow Old Igbobian, I was like him, the school’s Merit Award recipient, he said ‘oh, that is good enough for me”. Those seven words meant the world to me. People normally trust those they have had a good relationship with. In his own case, he was prepared to trust me with sensitive documents because we shared the same Alma Mater.

I have issued a few ‘no wonder’ comments of my own as well when I hear or read about the accomplishments of some distinguished Nigerians and I go through their CV to discover that they passed through the portals of Igbobi College. Most of them were in academia and the professions; hardly in government. In fact, we used to lament that Igbobi College didn’t prepare us for the intrigues and duplicities in governance. A welcome departure was Babatunde Fashola, whom I had long admired for his elocution and intellect until I found he had a stint at Igbobi College and my ‘no wonder’ comment came out. Of course anybody would be proud to share school colors with Professor Yemi Osinbajo, a junior in whom I have always been well pleased. I have also found myself to be more relaxed and trusting of people just because we share the same Alma Mater. This sentiment is not peculiar to Old Igbobians alone. Many Old Boys of Kings College, St Gregory’s College and the Government Colleges all over the country, share this sentiment too. Underpinning the sentiment is the belief that if you were good enough to pass through the four walls of their school, you were good enough.

Yoruba parents require of their children to ‘remember the child of whom they are’. if I have heard it once, I have heard it countless times. It is an admonition not to stain the family name or cast it into aspersion. It stems from the belief that a good name is better than wealth and a good pedigree is worth its weight in gold. To many, this administration is the face of Yoruba. But in reality, it is more personal as it is the fulfilment of someone’s ‘emilokan’. It is not surprising that many a true ‘Omoluabi’ will find it difficult to identify with or be proud of some of the goings on in this government. The question must be asked if this administration Is cleaning up the mess left by past administrations or adding a few of its own. Is it wiping the glass clean or smudging it? is it the best we can be? That is, if this administration is really the face of Yoruba as some people mischievously claim.

I feel particularly pained about the PFIPC scam that would not go away because Femi Gbajabiamila, one of the men in the eye of the storm, is both Yoruba and an Old Igbobian. Although he didn’t meet me in school, I still share vicariously in his successes and his failures. He needs to clear his name. For his sake. For the sake of all of us who identify with his roots one way or another. He is presumed innocent until proven guilty and evidences adduced so far point more to systemic failures and systemic abuse than to him. He possesses the intellect, the elocution and the confidence of an Igbobian.

Enough to say ‘no wonder’. But Igbobi College was never about intellect alone. Character has always been important, if not more important. In our time, Aggrey House, my House, made all Form One students to memorise the poem ‘IF’ by Rudyard Kipling. The poem is about what it takes to be a man of character. Igbobi College is about molding a boy into a man of nobility who will be a light unto the world. Which is why the most important line in the school song is ‘wherever there is an Igbobian, there also is a noble Nigerian’. Which is why we sometimes refer to ourselves as ‘the Noble One’.

Finally, if those in the public space thought more about their names and their roots than money and instant gratification, there would be less of these scams and Nigeria would begin to turn around for good.

World.title: $1trn Coastal Asset: SDAL charts eco-friendly future for Lagos
World.content:
•As Omotola warns against profit-driven devt

By Ishola Balogun

The Shoreline Developers Association of Lagos (SDAL) was formally inaugurated yesterday, with its President, Lai Omotola, urging stakeholders to look “beyond profits to sustainability” in the face of rapid shoreline property growth and environmental threats.

Speaking at the Ebootcamp in Wasimi, Omotola highlighted the surge in shoreline property values, which have risen by 751% in the past five years, alongside a 300% increase in planning permit and title registration fees. He warned that unchecked development risks damaging Lagos’ natural endowment.

“There is a rush by businessmen to join the fray without concerns for environment and nature,” Omotola said. “Our vision is to see the beauty of nature complimented by development towards improving lifestyle and living conditions.” Omotola stressed that shoreline development must go beyond sandfilling, pointing to untapped opportunities in fisheries, wind farms, coastal railways, renewable energy, port logistics, and eco-tourism.

“Shoreline development is not sandfilling carelessly — that is just the scratch of the surface,” he declared. “It is time for all stakeholders to fund a 50 to 100-year master plan for Lagos’ coastal line, which makes up 40% of our land mass.”

He also raised concerns about global threats such as sea level rise, storm surges, and groundwater extraction sinking Lagos at 4mm per year, calling for urgent investment in drainage networks, environmental impact assessments, and high-end technology.

Omotola emphasized collaboration between federal and state agencies, noting that the Nigeria Inland Waterways Authority (NIWA) should remain the lead regulator, while Lagos State retains authority over permits once reclaimed land is established.

“There should not be conflict among agencies of federal Government and Lagos State Government,” he said. “This cures multiplicity of roles.” The SDAL President concluded by underscoring the economic potential of shoreline development, describing Lagos’ coastal assets as an “unlocked $1 trillion opportunity” that could transform the state into a global eco-friendly tourist destination.

“There is no amount of investment that goes into shoreline development that cannot be recovered,” Omotola affirmed. “This is the essence of SDAL — advocacy, development, transformation, and sustaining luxurious lifestyle.”

World.title: Tense Osun Poll: Vote Buying Worries INEC
World.content:
*CSOs flag 13 high-risk LGAs, appeal for police neutrality

*Kudos, knocks trail Tinubu’s directive to unfreeze state’s account

*Police assure Nigerians of peaceful, credible governorship election

Adedayo Akinwale, Sunday Aborisade and Linus Aleke in Abuja and Yinka Kolawole in Osogbo

Ahead of the August 15 governorship election in Osun State, the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) yesterday expressed concern over the growing threat of vote buying, warning that the practice could undermine the credibility of the poll if not decisively checked by security agencies.



This comes as Civil Society Concerns on Election Security in Osun urged the Nigeria Police Force and other security agencies to remain neutral and professional during the state governorship election.

Also yesterday, reactions continued to trail President Bola Tinubu’s Thursday’s directive ordering the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) to return to court and vacate the order freezing the Osun State Government’s bank accounts, with political parties, civil society organisations and security agencies expressing divergent views over the development.



While the Inter-Party Advisory Council (IPAC) in Osun State and the opposition Accord Party commended the President’s intervention as a demonstration of respect for democracy and the rule of law, the Civil Society Legislative Advocacy Centre (CISLAC) warned that the directive could undermine the operational independence of anti-corruption institutions.

The House of Representatives Minority Caucus said the directive issued by the President to the EFCC was due to massive public outcry and not by respect for the rule of law.



Also, the Inspector-General of Police (IGP), Olatunji Disu, yesterday assured Nigerians that adequate security arrangements had been put in place to ensure a peaceful, free, fair and credible governorship election.

Speaking on INEC’s level of preparedness, a senior official of the Commission who spoke to THISDAY on condition of anonymity because he was not authorised to comment publicly on the election, said while the electoral body was fully prepared for the exercise, vote buying remained one of its biggest concerns given the heightened political atmosphere in the state.



The official disclosed that the commission had completed virtually all critical preparations for the election, including the deployment of election materials, training of personnel and testing of its electoral technology.

“As far as INEC is concerned, I can confidently say we are over 90 per cent prepared for the election,” the official said.

He revealed that INEC Chairman, Prof. Joash Amupitan, recently led a comprehensive readiness assessment in the state, which involved six National Commissioners, directors, senior officials and technical staff.



According to him, the exercise, which lasted about five days, involved a thorough review of every aspect of the commission’s preparations, including a mock accreditation exercise to test the effectiveness of the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS).

The official, however, stressed that INEC alone could not guarantee a credible election, saying the success of the poll would depend on the conduct of security agencies, political parties and their supporters.



He described the political environment in Osun as “quite tense,” urging all stakeholders to exercise restraint and uphold the rules of engagement.

“Our biggest concern is vote buying, which we fear could be widespread. We want the Nigeria Police and other security agencies to remain professional, impartial and above board in enforcing the law.



“Vote buying is prohibited under the Electoral Act. It is a criminal offence and one of the greatest threats to the integrity of Nigeria’s electoral process. Anyone arrested for the offence should face the full weight of the law,” the official added.

Meanwhile, the Civil Society Concerns on Election Security in Osun has urged the Nigeria Police Force and other security agencies to remain neutral and professional during the state governorship election.



The group made the call yesterday, during a press conference at the Nigeria Police Force Headquarters in Abuja.

Executive Director Samson Itodo, who spoke on behalf of the group, warned that public confidence in the electoral process would depend largely on how security personnel conduct themselves before, during and after the poll.



“This is the last major election to be held ahead of the 2027 general election. Therefore, it has a lot of significance, and it’s a unique opportunity to inspire public trust, not just in the management of the election, but election security.

“The public would want to see institutions demonstrate neutrality so they can have confidence in those institutions,” Itodo stated.

He warned that the level of pre-election violence and political tension recorded in parts of Osun State could undermine public trust and confidence if not effectively addressed.



He disclosed that findings from Yiaga Africa’s election observation and risk assessment showed that 13 of Osun State’s 30 local government areas have been classified as high-risk due to recurring violent incidents and heightened political tension.

These he said included Irewole, Osogbo, Boripe, Obokun, Ife North, Ife Central, and parts of Ijesaland.

He added. “Our comprehensive assessment and monitoring process shows that there have been about 34 known fatalities across incidents recorded between 2025 and June 2026.”



In the meantime, reactions have continued to trail President Tinubu’s directive ordering the EFCC to return to court and vacate the order freezing the Osun State Government’s bank accounts ahead of the August 15 governorship election.



IPAC, in a statement issued yesterday by its Caretaker Committee Chairman, Odesola Oluseye Titus, described President Tinubu’s directive to the EFCC as a demonstration of respect for democratic principles and the rule of law.

The council said the President’s action had reinforced confidence in Nigeria’s democratic institutions and should serve as a guide for all agencies involved in the electoral process.



Commending Tinubu for directing the anti-graft agency to vacate the court order, IPAC also praised the President’s insistence on the independence and professionalism of law enforcement agencies.

Quoting Tinubu’s position that anti-corruption agencies should discharge their statutory responsibilities “independently, professionally, without fear or favour or political interference,” the council described the President as “the father of the nation.”



It urged INEC, the Nigeria Police Force, the Nigerian Army and other security agencies to emulate the President’s example by performing their constitutional responsibilities impartially.



According to IPAC, the President’s directive should guide the conduct of all agencies involved in the forthcoming governorship election, stressing that security agencies and electoral officials must act professionally to sustain public confidence in the electoral process.

The council also appealed to political actors to respect the rules of engagement and urged eligible voters to come out en masse on election day, expressing confidence that every vote would count.



However, the opposition Accord Party demanded the immediate resignation of the Chairman of the EFCC, Ola Olukoyede, insisting that he should be held accountable for approving what it described as the unconstitutional freezing of the Osun State Government’s bank accounts.



Speaking at a world press conference in Abuja, the party’s National Chairman, Chief Maxwell Mgbudem, commended President Tinubu for what he termed a timely intervention that prevented a constitutional crisis.

He, however, argued that the EFCC chairman had embarrassed the President, damaged Nigeria’s democratic image and brought the anti-corruption agency into disrepute.

Mgbudem said if Olukoyede failed to resign voluntarily, President Tinubu should remove him from office to restore public confidence in the Commission.



The Accord chairman also called for the immediate release of about 60 of the party’s members allegedly detained in Abuja, Osun and Nasarawa States, saying their continued detention could heighten political tension ahead of the election.

He further urged INEC to conduct a free, fair and credible governorship election, describing the Osun poll as a critical test for Nigeria’s democracy ahead of the 2027 general election.



In a sharp contrast, the Executive Director of CISLAC and Head of Transparency International Nigeria, Auwal Musa Rafsanjani, criticised the President’s intervention, warning that directing the EFCC to seek the lifting of the court order could weaken the operational independence of anti-corruption institutions.



Addressing journalists in Abuja, Rafsanjani argued that while governance should not be unnecessarily disrupted, presidential intervention in specific enforcement actions created a dangerous precedent.

According to him, the EFCC derives its powers from the law and should be allowed to investigate and prosecute economic crimes professionally and without political interference.

He maintained that if the Commission took an inappropriate decision, the proper avenue for redress remained the judiciary rather than executive intervention.

Rafsanjani also stressed that lifting the restriction on the state’s accounts should not signal the end of investigations into the alleged diversion of public funds, insisting that anyone found culpable should face prosecution regardless of political affiliation.

In the meantime, the Inspector-General of Police, Olatunji Disu, assured Nigerians that the Nigeria Police Force had concluded comprehensive security arrangements for the August 15 governorship election.

Hosting civil society organisations in Abuja ahead of the poll, the IGP said the Police had no preferred candidate or political party and remained committed to ensuring that the lawful choice of the people prevailed.

He disclosed that adequate personnel and operational assets had been deployed across Osun State, while intelligence gathering and threat assessments had been intensified in collaboration with INEC, the Inter-Agency Consultative Committee on Election Security (ICCES) and other stakeholders.

Disu warned that anyone involved in vote buying, ballot box snatching, voter intimidation, thuggery or any other electoral offence would be dealt with in accordance with the law, irrespective of political affiliation.

He also urged political parties and their supporters to conduct themselves peacefully, stressing that elections should be contests of ideas rather than violence and intimidation.

The Police boss encouraged eligible voters to come out without fear to exercise their constitutional rights, assuring them that the Force would provide a secure environment throughout the electoral process.

The political atmosphere in Osun also became more charged yesterday as the All Progressives Congress (APC) asked Governor Ademola Adeleke to apologise to President Tinubu and the Minister of Marine and Blue Economy, Adegboyega Oyetola, for accusing them of influencing the EFCC’s action against the state government.

The party maintained that while the President objected to the timing of the account freeze, he did not exonerate the Osun State Government from the allegations being investigated by the anti-graft agency.

The House of Representatives Minority Caucus said the directive issued by the President to the EFCC was due to massive public outcry and not by respect for the rule of law.

It added that the move exposed deep contradictions and a deliberate plot to intimidate the Osun State Government ahead of next week’s gubernatorial election.

Its Leader, Hon. Fredrick Agbedi and the Spokesman of the caucus, Hon. Afam Ogene in a statement issued yesterday, said the President’s directive exposed “a government at war with itself,”.

The caucus pointed out that while EFCC Spokesman, Mr. Wilson Uwujaren, stated on national television on Thursday that the freezing of Osun’s account was done “without a valid court order”, the President’s statement later same Thursday afternoon directed the Commission to go to court to “vacate the order.”

The caucus noted: “So, which is it? Was there a court order or not?. Is the President not aware of what his own appointees are saying and doing?

“Has the President lost control of his army of sycophants who behave like lords over the people? Or are they simply trying to hide an illegality that has already been exposed?”

The Caucus also accused the President’s senior aides of being the first to circulate and defend the EFCC’s initial press release supporting the EFCC overreach.

The Caucus described the August 5 EFCC action as the latest in what they termed a sustained campaign of intimidation against Osun by the APC-led Federal Government.

The caucus decried that for months, the federal government had illegally withheld and seized statutory allocations due to Osun Local Governments, describing it as economic strangulation aimed at crippling governance at the grassroots ahead of elections.”

It noted: “ The gestapo-style arrest and detention of the Secretary to the Osun State Government, Teslim Igbalaiye and others over flimsy accusations is a direct attack on the institution of the state government.”

Also yesterday, the World Bishops Council (Africa Chapter) and the Religious Engagement (Christianity) Committee working for Governor Adeleke’s re-election endorsed the governor for a second term, describing him as “a man of destiny” who had promoted peace and religious harmony in the state.

The groups urged voters to re-elect Adeleke and announced a seven-day fasting and prayer programme for peaceful elections and the governor’s victory.

In another development, the Imole Campaign Council dismissed an alleged oath-taking video circulating on social media and purportedly linked to Governor Adeleke, describing it as a desperate smear campaign orchestrated by the APC.

The council insisted that Adeleke neither authorised nor participated in any oath-taking exercise, maintaining that his re-election bid was anchored on his performance in office and the goodwill of the people rather than intimidation or superstition.

World.title: Senior Goldman Sachs Executives Visit Dangote Industries Limited, Laud World-class Refinery
World.content:
* Dangote targets $100bn annual revenue by 2030

*Goldman Sachs hails scale, quality of refinery

Sunday Ehigiator

Senior executives from leading global investment banking and financial services firm, Goldman Sachs have toured the Dangote Industries Limited’s integrated petroleum refinery, petrochemicals and fertiliser complex in Lagos.

The delegation, led by Co-Chief Executive Officer of Goldman Sachs International and Global Co-Head of Investment Banking, Anthony Gutman, visited the Dangote Petroleum Refinery & Petrochemicals, Dangote Fertiliser Limited and supporting infrastructure during a recent visit to Nigeria.

Speaking after an extensive tour of the 700,000 barrels per day refinery, the Goldman Sachs executives remarked, “It is extraordinary what Mr. Dangote and the whole organisation have achieved. The ambition, the scale of the project, the quality of the project and the culture of the people is very impressive.”

Responding, the President and Chief Executive of Dangote Industries Limited, Aliko Dangote, said the refinery and associated industrial facilities demonstrate the transformative potential of long-term investment in Africa, adding that the Group’s growth ambitions extend well beyond its current strategic plan.

“No matter how we try to explain what we have built, you cannot fully appreciate it until you see it. But this is only the beginning. We need to look beyond 2030. The next phase of our journey will include new investments and acquisitions as we continue to scale the business,” he was quoted to have said.

Dangote said detailed internal modelling had reinforced management’s confidence that the Group’s target of generating US$100 billion in annual revenue by 2030 was achievable. He noted that the projections were based on conservative assumptions and had strengthened the company’s conviction that it could pursue an even more ambitious long term growth strategy.

He added that the level of employee participation in the recent private placement of the Dangote Petroleum Refinery reflected strong internal belief in the company’s growth strategy and prospects.

The Goldman Sachs team included Adib N. Zouein, Co Head of EMEA Emerging Markets Regional Sales and Head of the Middle East and North Africa region for Global Banking & Markets Public; Ryad Yousuf, Global Head of FICC Sales Strats and Structuring; and Jimi Adesanya, Head of Sub Saharan Africa Sales (excluding South Africa).

They were received by Aliko Dangote; Group Vice President, Oil & Gas, Devakumar Edwin; Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of Dangote Petroleum Refinery & Petrochemicals, David Bird; Group Executive Director, Oil & Gas, Fatima Aliko Dangote; Chief of Staff to the President/CE, Ibrahim Dikko; Group Chief Branding and Communication Officer, Anthony Chiejina; Group Chief Economist, Dr Hassan Mahmud; and Group Chief Strategy Officer, Aliyu Suleiman, among others.

The visit came a few days after Aliko Dangote held discussions with Canada’s Prime Minister, Mark Carney, on opportunities to strengthen investment partnerships and deepen economic cooperation between Canada and Africa.

The meeting focused on expanding investment opportunities in Canada and exploring how the Dangote Group, alongside other African investors, could contribute to Canada’s economic growth. Both leaders also exchanged views on Canada’s Africa Strategy and the importance of promoting stronger two-way trade and investment flows between Canada and African countries.

Dangote had also emphasised the growing potential for collaboration between African and Canadian businesses, noting that closer economic ties would unlock new opportunities for job creation, innovation, industrial development, and long-term prosperity.

“Strategic partnerships between Africa and Canada have immense potential to drive sustainable growth and create value for both regions. There is a strong case for increasing investment, fostering innovation, and building mutually beneficial commercial relationships,” Dangote had said.

World.title: US Appeals Court Blocks Trump’s $400m White House Ballroom Project
World.content:
Oluchi Chibuzor with agency report



A United States federal appeals court yesterday ordered Donald Trump’s administration to stop construction on a $400 million ballroom on the site of the White House’s demolished East Wing, dealing the Republican leader a major setback in a case testing his presidential authority.



“Each ‌President is a temporary tenant, not the owner, of the White House,” and cannot fundamentally reshape it without congressional approval, Reuters quoted the Washington-based U.S. Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit to have said in a 2-1 opinion.

The order upheld a preliminary injunction won by the National Trust for Historic Preservation, which sued last year after the administration tore down the East Wing and began building a 90,000-square-foot (8,360-square-meter) ballroom without seeking authorization from Congress.



“Whether or not a massive ballroom should be constructed is for Congress to decide and is not a matter for Executive self-help,” the panel’s majority wrote.

The appeals court placed its ruling on hold for 14 days to allow the Trump administration to appeal to the U.S. Supreme Court.

Trump, who has increasingly claimed that the ballroom project was a security necessity, referred to the structure as a “military center” in a post on Truth Social on Friday and said the administration would appeal to the Supreme Court. He called the decision “horrendous” and politically motivated and said it left him, other White House officials and visitors exposed to attack.



“This unjust decision must be overturned by the Supreme Court in its entirety,” Trump wrote. He said the ballroom plan includes bomb shelters, medical facilities, shielding from drones and missiles and other security features that are “all tied together as one big, expensive, and very complex unit.”



National Trust President Brent Leggs said in a statement that the ruling marked “a great day for our country and for the American people’s right to voice their opinions about the historic places they cherish, including the White House.”

Trump appealed after U.S. District Judge Richard Leon, an appointee of Republican former President George W. Bush, twice blocked above-ground construction on the site while allowing underground work to continue.

The ballroom plan, which the administration has described as necessary for large formal functions and to preserve the safety of the White House, is the grandest ‌of several Trump efforts to reshape central Washington’s landscape of government buildings and national monuments.



A judge in a separate lawsuit recently said Trump’s name was illegally added to the exterior of the Kennedy Center performing arts venue and ordered its removal.

In the ballroom case, Justice Department attorney Yaakov Roth said during D.C. Circuit arguments on June 5 that the courts have no role in weighing the privately funded project. He said the National Trust’s “architectural preference” should not take precedence over national security concerns, claiming evidence that the former East Wing left thepresident and others in the White House vulnerable to attack.



The Democratic-appointed judges in the appeals court’s majority — Circuit Judges Patricia Millett and Brad Garcia — said their order does not permanently bar construction of a ballroom, but halts above-ground work during the lawsuit and until the White House secures approval from Congress.



National security arguments “are not an automatic get-out-of-law-free card,” the opinion said.

“The bold assertion that the Executive can act with utter lawlessness, destroying treasured national landmarks and harming the interestsof individuals, and that no court can stop it flouts our constitutional order,” the judges wrote.

Circuit Judge Neomi Rao, whom Trump appointed during his first term, said in her dissent that the trial judge’s injunction blocking the project “is beyond the proper province of the federal courts” and that construction should be allowed to continue.



“The district court seized supervision of construction at the White House, and my colleagues affirm this judicial overreach,” Rao wrote.

World.title: Extend Pay Rise for Military to Other Security Agencies, Rewane Tells FG
World.content:
· Reveals electronic payment transactions rose to N122.98trn in July

· Projected to hit N126.7trn in August

Nume Ekeghe

The Managing Director and Chief Executive of Financial Derivatives Company (FDC), Mr. Bismarck Rewane, has called on the federal government to extend the recently approved increase in the salary of military personnel to other security agencies, warning that excluding them could create distortions within the country’s security architecture.

This is as the economist also revealed that the value of electronic payment transactions in Nigeria increased by 5.54 per cent month-on-month to N122.98 trillion in July 2026, up from N116.52 trillion recorded in June. He projected that the figure would climb further to N126.70 trillion in August, as seasonal spending and the continued adoption of digital payment channels lift transaction values.

Rewane, while weighing in on the increase in emoluments, in a presentation he made at the August edition of the Lagos Business School (LBS) Breakfast Session, a copy of which was obtained by THISDAY yesterday, argued that following the federal government’s approval of a comprehensive wage review for personnel of the Nigerian Army, there should be a corresponding salary adjustment for the Nigeria Police Force, Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC) and other security agencies to maintain equity and morale across the security services.

The wage review approved for the Nigerian Army provides for an 80 per cent increase for lower-ranking personnel, 50 per cent for officers from warrant officers to colonels, and 30 per cent for officers from colonels to generals, with the total cost estimated at N924 billion.

While acknowledging the importance of improving the welfare of military personnel, Rewane warned that the policy would inevitably have wider implications for the public and private sectors.

He said the salary adjustment would affect wage relativities across the public service and place pressure on private sector employers to review compensation packages.

“The knock-on effects will affect the rest of the public sector and the relativity factor for the private sector,” he stated.

He further cautioned that higher wages without a corresponding increase in productivity could fuel inflation, estimating that the adjustment could add between two and three percentage points to inflationary pressures.

“This will push wages higher without productivity. Inflation is bound to increase by a minimum of two to three per cent,” he noted.

Rewane stressed that fairness demanded a compensating salary review for all other security agencies.

“There must be a compensating review of all other security agencies and armed forces, including the Police and Civil Defence,” he said.

He, however, warned that such an expansion of the wage review would significantly increase recurrent expenditure across all tiers of government.

According to him, extending similar salary adjustments across the security services would lead to “a ballooning of government revenue expenditure at all levels,” further tightening fiscal conditions.

The economist urged policymakers to balance the imperative of improving the welfare of security personnel with measures that enhance productivity and strengthen government revenue in order to avoid worsening inflationary pressures and fiscal deficits.

Meanwhile, the report presented at the LBS showed that the Nigeria Instant Payment (NIP) platform remained the dominant payment channel, accounting for the bulk of transaction values. NIP transactions rose by 4.89 per cent to N109.59 trillion in July from N104.48 trillion in June.

The report also showed that the Nigeria Electronic Funds Transfer (NEFT) platform recorded the fastest growth among the major payment channels, with transaction values surging 18.03 per cent to N6.48 trillion from N5.49 trillion in June. Point-of-Sale (PoS) transaction values increased by 5.56 per cent to N6.65 trillion, while cheque transactions rose modestly by 4.35 per cent to N264 billion.

Looking ahead, FDC projected that electronic payment transactions would expand further to N126.70 trillion in August. NIP transaction value was expected to rise to N112.21 trillion, while PoS transactions are forecast to jump sharply to N7.97 trillion as consumer spending strengthens during the holiday period. Although NEFT transactions are expected to moderate slightly to N6.29 trillion, overall electronic payment activity is projected to remain resilient, reinforcing the steady transition towards a cashless economy.

The latest monthly performance mirrors the longer-term expansion of digital payments highlighted in the Central Bank of Nigeria’s (CBN) 2025 Annual Report and Statement of Accounts.

According to the apex bank, the value of electronic payment transactions increased by 26.07 per cent to N3, 458.77 trillion in 2025, while transaction volume rose by 2.62 per cent to 47.88 billion transactions.

The CBN attributed the growth to stronger consumer preference for digital payment channels, expanding e-commerce activity and continued improvements in payment infrastructure.

It stated: “Analysis of retail payments showed notable changes between 2024 and 2025. The volume of e-payments transactions increased by 2.62 per cent to 47,879.73 million in 2025, compared with 2024. The value of transactions also rose by 26.07 per cent to N3, 458.77 trillion.

“The increases reflected user preferences, adoption of digital channels, growth in e-commerce, and infrastructure improvements.”

At the recent launch of the Payments System Vision 2028 (PSV 2028), CBN Governor, Mr. Olayemi Cardoso, had reaffirmed the apex bank’s commitment to achieving 95 per cent financial inclusion and enabling “faster-than-a-blink” digital transactions through sustained reforms of Nigeria’s payment ecosystem.

World.title: 2027: PDP, 15 APC Guber Aspirants Negotiate Power-sharing in Kwara
World.content:
.Cracks deepen in Kwara APC as PDP drafts Saraki to woo aggrieved members ahead of 2027

.Kwara APC reconciliation committee submits report, hails support of gov AbdulRazaq, party exco

Chuks Okocha in Abuja and Hammed Shittu in Ilorin

The Kwara State chapter of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) and the 15 aggrieved gubernatorial aspirants of All Progressives Congress (APC) in the state have commenced negotiations on the sharing of elective positions ahead of 2027 elections.

With political permutations ahead of the 2027 general elections gathering momentum, the Kwara State PDP has also moved to capitalise on the growing discontent within the ruling APC, mandating former Senate President, Bukola Saraki, to begin talks with aggrieved members of the party.

As part of efforts to put its troubled house in order which engulfed the party after the conduct of the party primaries in the state, the Kwara State APC Reconciliation Committee yesterday submitted their report to the State Working Committee of the party.

The parley according to THISDAY checks might not be unconnected with the recent resolutions of the PDP leadership to meet the aggrieved 15 APC gubernatorial aspirants towards fostering political understanding ahead of the forthcoming elections.

At the meeting of the aggrieved gubernatorial aspirants held in Ilorin on Thursday, they had pledged their commitment to the electoral victory of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu come 2027, but vowed not to work for the success of the APC in the state.

However, the PDP and the 15 aggrieved gubernatorial aspirants have set up a committee on how to share the elective positions before the final closure of the portal of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC).

Sources close to the two groups told journalists in Ilorin yesterday, that the PDP camp was said to have presented six members of the state House of Assembly, two senatorial tickets and two House of Representatives slots to the 15 aggrieved gubernatorial aspirants’ camp.

On the part of the 15 aggrieved APC gubernatorial aspirants, the group was said to have demanded 10 slots of the members of the state House of Assembly, two senatorial tickets and two House of Representatives tickets from the PDP.

Speaking at a press briefing in Ilorin, spokesperson of the coalition and former Senator, Yahaya Oloriegbe, alleged that the governor’s leadership had sidelined many stakeholders and deepened divisions within the party.

He warned that unless the APC national leadership intervenes, the lingering crisis could undermine the party’s electoral prospects in the 2027 general elections.

According to Oloriegbe, the Oto Ge Progressives was formed to protect the principles of fairness, inclusiveness and transparency, alleging that many party faithful had been excluded from critical political decisions.

He also claimed that members of the coalition had been subjected to intimidation and pressure to support what he described as a predetermined succession arrangement.

The coalition insisted that candidates for elective offices must emerge through transparent and democratic processes rather than through the influence of any individual, urging the APC leadership to urgently address the grievances before they escalate.

Seizing on the apparent cracks within the ruling party, PDP stakeholders at a two-day strategic meeting in Ilorin authorised Saraki to commence consultations with members of the APC’s G15 bloc and other political groups as part of efforts to expand the party’s support base ahead of the next general elections.

The decision was contained in a communiqué jointly signed by the Kwara PDP Chairman, Adamu Bawa, and the State Secretary, Abdulrahman Kayode, following the meeting attended by party leaders, former political office holders, aspirants, women and youth representatives.

The communique said, “At the meeting, His Excellency, Dr. Abubakar Bukola Saraki appreciated all aspirants and stakeholders for the serious sacrifices they made before, during and after the 2026 party primaries, and for their commitment to the unity and growth of the PDP in Kwara State.

“After extensive deliberations, the stakeholders unanimously resolved as follows: stakeholders passed a vote of confidence on our National Leader, His Excellency, Dr. Abubakar Bukola Saraki, for his consistent leadership, political sagacity and unwavering commitment to the PDP and the people of Kwara State.

“Noting that the PDP in Kwara State is already strong and united, the meeting mandated His Excellency, Dr. Abubakar Bukola Saraki to proceed with engagements with members of the Kwara APC’s G15 and other political parties, with the objective of further strengthening the PDP and expanding its base ahead of future elections.”

The meeting also resolved that all stakeholders, aspirants, and candidates must be prepared to set aside personal ambitions and individual interests in the greater interest of the party.

Meanwhile, the APC had on 3rd of July 2026 set up the five-member committee, chaired by retired Col. AbdulWahab Ademola Lawal(rtd) to resolve internal disputes following the party’s primary elections.

Presenting the report at the party’s Secretariat in Ilorin, Col. Lawal, appreciated the governor and the party executives for their trust and for giving them an enabling environment to operate.

He said the committee had invited all the aggrieved members in the course of their findings and provided them with a level playing ground to ventilate their grievances – a step he noted aided their work.

He said that the committee, however, got assurances of the members to remain in the party and to “not go back to Egypt.”

“I want to say that on the mandate given to us we received the blessings of His Excellency (Governor AbdulRazaq), and the Party Chairman made it clear to us that: “please allow everybody to vent their anger and sentiments and also do what is needful,” he said, adding that the report will go a long way to resolving the disagreement.

“We made it clear to them that this is a family affair; no one is outside the family. All of us are together and in a family. But there are bound to be disagreements and therefore they should see us as mediators,” Lawal said.

The state APC Chairman Prince Sunday Fagbemi, thanked the committee for their effort, and pledging that the state leadership of the party will do everything humanly possible to do justice to the report.

He described Col. Lawal as highly disciplined and a diplomat par excellence, adding all members of the committee are people of integrity.

“When we go through the report of the committee, we will do all that is humanly possible to make sure we remain as a family.

“We are appealing to all that are aggrieved to await the actions that will be taken after the presentation of the committee’s report,” Fagbemi said.

Other members of the reconciliation committee are the Assistant Comptroller of Immigration, AIG Ahmed Abbas, Engr. Musa Yeketi, Dr. Oluwatoyin Opawoye and Hajia Kubura Kassum.

World.title: Woro Community Rescued Victims Arrive Kwara
World.content:
Hammed Shittu in Ilorin

The rescued victims abducted during the deadly February 3, 2026 attack on Woro community in Kaiama Local Government Area of Kwara State have arrived in Ilorin, Kwara state capital.

The victims numbering 163 were rescued on Wednesday August 5, 2026, by security forces after spending six months in captivity.

THISDAY checks revealed that the rescued victims arrived Ilorin, the state capital late Thursday night.

Sources told THISDAY that the affected rescued victims were received at the Nigerian Army’s 2 Division, Sobi Barracks, Ilorin.

They said the affected rescued victims were said to have been moved to an undisclosed location where they spent the night.

It would be recalled that the victims were abducted when armed bandits invaded the community earlier this year, killing scores of residents and whisking away many others into the forest, triggering widespread outrage and intensified security operations.

Following sustained military operations and coordinated efforts by security agencies, the victims regained their freedom and were transported from Niger State to Ilorin.

The rescued victims are expected to be officially handed over to Governor AbdulRahman AbdulRazaq.

Their arrival marks a major breakthrough in the month-long efforts to secure the release of the abductees, while authorities continue to verify the number of those rescued and provide necessary care and support.

World.title: COAS Charges Troops to Uphold Professionalism as Army Expands New Formations
World.content:
.Troops arrest 4 Lakurawa terrorists, recover livestock in Sokoto

Linus Aleke in Abuja

The Chief of Army Staff (COAS), Lieutenant General Waidi Shaibu, has charged soldiers graduating from Exercise RESTORE HOPE X to uphold the highest standards of professionalism, discipline and operational excellence as they prepare to serve in the Nigerian Army’s newly established divisions, formations and units.

This was as the troops of 8 Division Garrison of the Nigerian Army have apprehended four suspected Lakurawa terrorists while selling six cows at the Darussa Village market in Gudu Local Government Area of Sokoto State.

Speaking at the graduation ceremony of the Advanced Infantry Training Programme at the Nigerian Army Training Centre (NATC), Kachia, Kaduna State, the COAS described the exercise as the flagship of the Army’s post-basic infantry training framework, designed to sharpen combat proficiency, strengthen the warrior ethos and prepare soldiers for the realities of contemporary military operations.

According to a statement by the Acting Director of Army Public Relations, Colonel Appolonia Anele, Shaibu said the graduation coincided with the Army’s ongoing force expansion and capability enhancement following President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s approval for the restructuring of the Service. He noted that many of the graduands would form the nucleus of the newly established divisions, formations and units.

The Army Chief urged the soldiers to justify the investment in their training by demonstrating professionalism, sound judgement and unwavering commitment to mission accomplishment.

He also called on them to remain physically fit, mentally agile and technologically proficient while upholding the rule of law, protecting human rights and strictly observing the rules of engagement.

Earlier, the Chief of Training (Army), Major General Valentine Okoro, described Exercise RESTORE HOPE X as a critical component of the Nigerian Army’s training architecture, saying it had consistently produced combat-ready soldiers through realistic operational scenarios, leadership development and counter-insurgency training while strengthening institutional capacity across Army training establishments.

Meanwhile, a security source told the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) yesterday that the four Lakurawa terrorists suspects were engaged in trading livestock suspected to have been rustled.

The source, who pleaded anonymity, identified the suspects as Usman Bammo, 45, Ali Usman, 23, Abubakar Garba, 30, and Muhammadu Dage, 25.

The source added that other items recovered from the suspects included two Tecno mobile phones and the sum of N165,000.00 in cash.

According to the source, the success was recorded following credible intelligence as part of efforts to safeguard the lives and property of the people against all forms of criminality.

The source commended community members for prompt information sharing and urged them to continue supporting security agencies, stressing that the fight against banditry, terrorism and other crimes should be viewed as a collective responsibility of all citizens.

World.title: Bauchi Governor Orders Security Forces to Intensify Crackdown on Criminal Hideouts
World.content:
Segun Awofadeji in Bauchi

Bauchi State Governor, Senator Bala Abdukadir Mohammed, has directed security agencies to sustain joint operations against criminal elements, warning that renewed threats require coordinated action to protect lives, property and vulnerable communities across the state.

This was as the governor commended the security agencies for their successful operations against terrorists in Alkaleri Local Government Area, describing the military offensive as a major breakthrough in the state’s fight against insecurity.

Governor Mohammed, who was speaking during a meeting of the Bauchi State Security Council on Thursday, instructed security forces to replicate the recent successes recorded in Alkaleri, Ningi, Ganjuwa, Toro and other affected local government areas through intensified patrols and coordinated ground operations.

He urged security agencies to deny criminals freedom of movement by increasing patrols, dismantling forest hideouts and strengthening surveillance across border communities vulnerable to kidnappings, banditry and infiltration.

The governor warned traditional rulers against harbouring criminals, allocating land to suspicious persons or facilitating illegal activities, stressing that offenders would face sanctions in accordance with the provisions of the law.

He reaffirmed the state’s commitment to supporting security agencies through improved logistics, technology, expanded military presence and additional police stations, while encouraging stronger collaboration with communities and traditional institutions across Bauchi.

Mohammed further urged security agencies to remain professional and impartial during forthcoming political activities, ensuring adequate protection for citizens, political parties and democratic processes while maintaining peace and public order across the state.

He praised the Nigerian Army, the Police, Department of State Services (DSS), Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC), vigilante groups and other security operatives for their gallantry and coordinated efforts.

The governor also commended troops of the Nigerian Army’s 3 Division and the 33 Artillery Brigade for intelligence-led operations that dislodged terrorists from Mansur Village and surrounding enclaves, dismantled their camps and neutralised several high-profile criminal elements.

According to him, the operation also paved the way for thousands of displaced residents to safely return to their ancestral communities.

Mohammed expressed appreciation to President Bola Tinubu, the National Security Adviser and the Service Chiefs for supporting the operations that resulted in the military successes.

World.title: No extension: SASSA Gold Card warning for 43 000 beneficiaries
World.content:
SASSA beneficiaries are being urged to replace their Gold Cards as the deadline approaches. Image: SASSA/X

More than 43 000 SASSA Gold Card holders in the Western Cape still need to replace their cards before 31 August.

Postbank has confirmed it will not extend the deadline.

The Democratic Alliance (DA) in the Western Cape has urged beneficiaries to act now. The party also welcomed steps taken by Postbank and the South African Social Security Agency (SASSA) to speed up the replacement process.



More than 29 000 card holders are in Cape Town

Figures presented to the Western Cape Legislature’s Standing Committee on Social Development show that 43 515 beneficiaries still need to replace their SASSA Gold Cards.

The breakdown is as follows:

City of Cape Town: 29 847

29 847 Cape Winelands: 4 868

4 868 Garden Route: 4 312

4 312 West Coast: 2 675

2 675 Overberg: 1 720

1 720 Central Karoo: 447

Retail partnerships expand replacement sites

The DA said Postbank has expanded access through partnerships with Pick n Pay, Boxer, Shoprite and Spar. The partnerships now provide 39 card replacement sites across the province.



Postbank and SASSA have also increased awareness through SMSs, WhatsApp messages, radio campaigns, municipal councillors, traditional leaders and community organisations.

The party further welcomed progress reported to the committee. This includes filling critical vacancies at SASSA, improving systems and working with municipalities to establish dedicated SASSA service points.

DA urges beneficiaries to replace cards now

DA Western Cape spokesperson on Social Development Wendy Kaizer-Philander urged beneficiaries not to leave the replacement process until the last minute.



“We encourage beneficiaries not to wait until the last minute. Those who are able to do so should consider switching their grant payments to either a Postbank black card or a bank of their choice.”

She also called on SASSA and Postbank to increase daily replacement capacity and strengthen outreach efforts to prevent long queues and ensure beneficiaries continue receiving their grants without disruption.

The DA said it will continue monitoring the replacement process to protect the interests of vulnerable residents across the Western Cape.

World.title: New Orlando Pirates striker arrives in South Africa
World.content:
Orlando Pirates welcoming new striker Sebastian Pedersen to South Africa. The Norwegian Embassy confirmed the attacker’s arrival on social media.

“Welcome to South Africa, Sebastian Pedersen! The whole Embassy is very excited that a Norwegian footballer has joined Orlando Pirates,” the Embassy of Norway posted on X.

SEBASTIAN PEDERSEN ARRIVES IN SOUTH AFRICA

The 27-year-old signed a two-year contract with an option for an additional season. He arrives with considerable experience from Norway. He represented his country at every junior international level from Under-15 through to Under-21.



His club record also highlights his goalscoring ability.

Across the last four-and-a-half seasons with Sogndal and Moss FK, Pedersen scored 51 goals and provided eight assists in 117 appearances.

Pirates believe his movement and finishing will add another dimension to the attack. The Buccaneers described him as a one-touch finisher rather than a traditional physical striker.



ORLANDO PIRATES FACE DURBAN CITY IN THE MTN8

Pedersen arrives as Orlando Pirates prepare for their MTN8 quarter-final against Durban City. The Buccaneers face the Nedbank Cup holders on Saturday, 8 August, at the Orlando Amstel Arena.

Kick-off is scheduled for 15:00 SAST.

Orlando Pirates are defending their MTN8 crown and chasing a historic fifth consecutive title. However, Pedersen will have to wait for his opportunity to make his competitive debut for the Buccaneers.

World.title: St Stithians tragedy: Cameron honoured amid murder investigation
World.content:
The President’s Award for Youth Empowerment has paid tribute to Cameron Waldeck-Cooks, a Bronze Award holder and Gold Award participant. Images: St Stithians Girl's College, The President’s Award for Youth Empowerment

A new tribute has revealed more about 17-year-old Cameron Waldeck-Cooks as police continue investigating her death in Sabie, Mpumalanga.

The President’s Award for Youth Empowerment has confirmed that the St Stithians Girls’ College Grade 11 learner was a Bronze Award holder and Gold Award participant.

“Cameron was a dedicated Bronze Award holder and Gold Award participant whose warmth, kindness and determination touched those around her,” the organisation said in a statement.



It extended its condolences to her family, friends and school community.

The tribute follows statements from the families of Cameron and 19-year-old Ethan Coetzee, who were found dead at a lodge in Sabie on Monday, 3 August.

Parents remember Cameron

Cameron’s parents, Derrick Cooks and Claire Waldeck-Cooks, described their daughter as warm, kind-hearted and determined.



They said she had been working towards completing the Gold level of The President’s Award and had travelled to Sabie after being invited on a hiking trip.

Her parents said her death had left an “immeasurable void” in their lives.

They also confirmed that an independent pathologist had been involved following Cameron’s death.



Ethan’s family pays tribute

Ethan, a former St Stithians Boys’ College pupil, was also remembered by his family following the tragedy.

His father, Graham Coetzee, previously described his son as a young man who loved sport and the outdoors.

The family asked for privacy while mourning their loss.



Police open murder case

Mpumalanga police initially investigated the deaths through an inquest.

However, the investigation took a significant turn following post-mortem examinations.

Police subsequently opened a murder case in connection with Cameron’s death. The investigation into the circumstances surrounding both deaths remains active.



Police have not publicly announced an arrest or identified a suspect in both murder investigations.

The President’s Award said it was keeping Cameron’s loved ones in its thoughts during what it described as a profoundly difficult time.

World.title: Carte Blanche coming up: Right to the city
World.content:
The Sunday, 09 August episode of Carte Blanche examines South Africa’s ongoing struggle with urban spatial inequality through the daily commute of Nadia, who leaves her home in Hanover Park before dawn to travel to Sea Point in Cape Town’s affluent tourist hub for work.

Her journey reflects the reality faced by millions of working-class South Africans who live on the outskirts of cities but travel long distances to access jobs and economic opportunities in urban centres.

The programme focuses on a prime government-owned site in Sea Point that has become a flashpoint in the fight for urban spatial justice, exploring whether a landmark Constitutional Court judgment could force South Africa to confront the geographical legacy of apartheid-era urban planning and the deep divisions that continue to shape its cities.



Credibility among South African viewers

Carte Blanche is a South African investigative journalism television series that airs on M-Net every Sunday at 19:00.

Its first episode aired on 21 August 1988 and over the last 34-plus years has earned credibility among South African viewers for its investigation into corruption, consumer issues, and current events.

World.title: Latest report: SAFA find new Bafana Bafana coach
World.content:
Pitso Mosimane is reportedly set to make a sensational return as Bafana Bafana head coach. According to SoccerBeat, the South African Football Association (SAFA) has decided to appoint Mosimane as the successor to Hugo Broos.

An official announcement is believed to be imminent. SAFA had previously confirmed that its National Executive Committee (NEC) would meet on Saturday, 8 August, to ratify the recommendation for the new coach.

PITSO MOSIMANE SET TO BAFANA BAFANA

Broos officially left Bafana Bafana after more than five years in charge. The Belgian took over in May 2021 and transformed the national team into one of Africa’s most competitive sides.



Under Broos, South Africa won the bronze medal at the 2023 Africa Cup of Nations. He also guided South Africa to the 2026 FIFA World Cup, where the team reached the knockout stages for the first time.

SAFA wanted to keep the experienced coach beyond the expiry of his contract. However, Broos decided against continuing with the national team.

The potential appointment of Mosimane would now give Bafana Bafana another highly decorated South African coach.



MOSIMANE BRINGS WINNING PEDIGREE

Mosimane has built one of the most impressive coaching resumes in African football.

He made his name at SuperSport United before taking charge of South Africa. He later joined Mamelodi Sundowns and created a domestic and continental dynasty.

During his time at Sundowns, Mosimane won five PSL titles and guided the club to the 2016 CAF Champions League trophy. That triumph made him the first South African coach to win the competition.



He then moved to Egyptian giants Al Ahly, where he added two more CAF Champions League titles to his collection and guided the club to two FIFA Club World Cup bronze medals.

Mosimane later coached in Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates and Iran, further expanding his international experience. A return to Bafana Bafana would therefore represent another major chapter in his career.

For SAFA, the decision would also signal a clear desire to maintain the momentum created during the Broos era while placing the national team in the hands of one of South Africa’s most successful coaches.

World.title: PREVIEW of September 2026 SASSA Old-Age Grants
World.content:
Here’s your latest preview for September 2026 SASSA Old-Age Grants. The country’s four-million elderly beneficiaries can mark Wednesday 2 September 2026 in their calendars as the next day for payment.

And for the first time in a while, the wait time between August and next month’s disbursements isn’t too bad – just 29 days. This is an improvement over last cycle’s 33 day wait …

SEPTEMBER 2026 SASSA OLD-AGE GRANTS

We take an all-important look ahead to September 2026 SASSA Old-Age Grants for the country’s four-million beneficiaries. Image: File

As ever, the South African Social Security Agency increased Old-Age Grants by R80 back in April 2026, and they will pay the following next month:



SASSA Old-Age Grants 60 to 74 years old – R2 400 (up from R2 320)

(up from R2 320) SASSA Old-Age Grants 75 years and older – R2 420 (up from R2 340)

What is encouraging is that September 2026 SASSA Old-Age Grants will be the last before the usual mid-year increase in October 2026. The Department of Social Development (DSD), under new ministerial control of Dina Pule, is yet to confirm how much increases will be. However, state-sponsored pensioners have been lobbying hard for meaningful increases to their grants through various marches and protests …

HOW MUCH COULD GRANTS INCREASE BY?

As part of September 2026 SASSA Old-Age Grants, the agency is forging ahead with its strict review policy. As last count, it was targeting more than 300 000 suspect profiles and said it’s saved more than R170 million already thanks to this process. However, the DSD also revealed in parliament earlier this year that it had underspent its budget on social grants by R4.8 billion for the financial year 2025/26.

That makes what the agency is fighting to save each year look like a drop in a vast ocean. Simple calculations reveal that split across all four-million Old-Age Grant recipients, SASSA could increase grants by R100 per month for a full year and not need any more budget. Which is why beneficiaries awaiting September 2026 SASSA Old-Age Grants know all-too well of the importance of eLife certification and eligibility review to keep their grants.



STRICTER REVIEWS FOR SEPTEMBER 2026 SASSA OLD-AGE GRANTS

New SASSA minister Dina Pule is back in the governmental hot seat 13 years after being fired for misconduct. Image: File

SASSA can cross-reference all your personal data with a host of other government departments and banks. Therefore, anyone who has been claiming a government grant that shouldn’t be will be found out. Worse still, if you are caught misrepresenting your means, not only will you lose your grant, but you will have to pay back the money with interest.

For those who are reviewed by SASSA and clear their names, they receive a deferred payment on a fourth date. Next month this looks likely to fall on Saturday 5 September 2026 (TBC). However, if you cannot clear your name, you face the option of two different payment plans: One is the lump-sum payback, which is most affordable. But the vast majority end up paying back their ill-gotten SASSA money on a layaway plan, incurring high interest rate penalties in the process.

ADJUSTED MEANS (INCOME) TESTS

To make things tougher, the agency has also increased the income (means) and asset eligibility for September 2026 SASSA Old-Age Grants:



Your income must be less than R9 350 (single) or R18 700 (married) per month.

(single) or (married) per month. This adds up to R112 200 (single) or R224 400 (married) per year.

(single) or (married) per year. Total assets (property) in your name cannot be worth more than R1 584 000 (single) or R3 168 000 (married).

Here’s what you need to know and be able to show the agency when applying for September 2026 SASSA Old-Age Grants:

Official RSA identity document (ID) preferably a Smart ID Card with digital ID photo.

with digital ID photo. Valid three months’ statement certified by your bank, plus copies.

statement certified by your bank, plus copies. All documents proving your marital status, plus death certificates if necessary.

Proof of residence (a utility bill with your name on it, not older than three months ).

). Documents proving your income and/or any financial dividends (very important).

Comprehensive information regarding assets/valuation of any property you own.

Full declaration of any and all private pension in your name.

Unemployment Insurance Fund (UIF) membership book, or discharge certificate from your previous job.

A copy of your will, first and final liquidation and distribution accounts, if your spouse has passed away in the last five years.

HOW LONG DOES IT TAKE TO BE APPROVED FOR SASSA OLD-AGE GRANTS?

Be sure to keep your contact details up to date with the agency to avoid missing any nasty eligibility review notices. Image: File

September 2026 SASSA Old-Age Grants typically take around three months to be processed, so, you will receive your first payment in December. However, you will be back paid to the date of your first application, so, three months in the first tranche. But that’s assuming you have all your documents correct at the first time of asking. It is now possible to complete eLife certification and biometric verification at the agency’s new online service portal HERE to save time and beat the queues.

Plus, if you’re too old, sick or live in a remote rural area you can get a loved one to help with your September 2026 SASSA Old-Age Grants application. All you need is a letter from your doctor. And all of the above documentation copied and certified by a commissioner of oaths. If you are denied the grant you do have three months to appeal the decision with the DSD HERE.



You can try to contact SASSA directly here:

SASSA toll-free line: 0800 601 011

Head Office of SASSA: 012 400 2322

Email SASSA: grantsenquiries@sassa.gov.za

But what do you think? Are you a first-time applicant for September 2026 SASSA Old-Age Grants? How did you find the experience and what tips do you have for other beneficiaries applying? Be sure to share your ideas in the comments section below …
