World.title: Albanian Court Puts Turkish Activist in Custody After Extradition Demand
World.content:
Protesters rally with pictures of victims of the 2013 Gezi Park protests in Istanbul, April 2022. Photo: EPA-EFE/SEDAT SUNA.

The Tirana Court on Friday ordered a custody remand for Julide Yazici, who is wanted for extradition by Turkey to serve a prison sentence for aiding a terrorist organisation – charges that she claims are motivated by her political activism.

Yazici was arrested on August 4 at Tirana Airport while travelling from France to Albania after it was discovered that she was wanted for extradition to Turkey.

The judge granted the prosecution’s custody request despite Yazici’s lawyer’s arguments that his client “holds political asylum status in France and poses no danger”, and could be placed under house arrest instead.

The lawyer, Artan Shllaku, said that the decision will be appealed.

Shllaku added that Yazici, who teaches at an elementary school in France, had visited Albania a year earlier to see relatives and had encountered no issues.

Yazici is wanted by Turkish authorities to serve the remainder of a four-year prison sentence – three years, five months and 22 days – for providing logistical support to and participating in a terrorist organisation.

According to a decision by the French National Court of Asylum dated November 2020, a document obtained by BIRN, Yazici was involved in political activism in Turkey and participated in the Gezi Park mass protests in 2013 against the administration led by Recep Tayyip Erdogan.

She actively supported the former People’s Democratic Party, HDP, a left-wing political group that supported Turkey’s Kurdish minority, and which later became the DEM Party.

The French court decision granting asylum to Yazici stated that she was arrested in January 2016 “for having allowed a young woman she did not know, who had been introduced to her by a friend, to stay in her student room”.

The French court decision in the document that Yazici had “a well-founded fear … of being persecuted if she returns to her country due to her political activism”.

Yazici is not the first Turkish national to be arrested in Albania for extradition in controversial circumstances in recent years. Teachers and others linked to the movement previously led by the now-deceased cleric Fethullah Gulen, which is classified as a terrorist organisation by the authorities under Erdogan, have also been detained and then deported in line with Ankara’s demands.

World.title: Secrecy Surrounds Croatia’s Arrest of Alleged Serbian State-Linked Hacker
World.content:
Photo illustration: EPA/SASCHA STEINBACH.

The Croatian and Serbian authorities are remaining tight-lipped over the arrest last week of a Serbian businessman named as Georgije V., 33, on suspicion of hacking into the computer systems of various Croatian state institutions and public agencies.

The Serbian man is reportedly suspected of hacking into the Croatian Interior Ministry, the Central Register of Pension-Insured Persons, the Croatian Health Insurance Fund, the Croatian Regulatory Agency for Network Activities, the Croatian Pension Insurance Institute, the Croatian Tax Administration and the Croatian Automobile Club.

Tomo Medved, the Minister of Croatian Veterans, was asked about the case on Friday but declined to provide details.

“I would like to commend the entire security and intelligence system for its responsible and vigilant monitoring and protection of the interests of the Republic of Croatia. Given the ongoing proceedings, I cannot comment further than that,” Medved told journalists.

Croatian daily Jutarnji list has reported that the arrest took place on July 28, when Georgije V. was on holiday in Croatia. He had arrived with his wife, two children and mother at a tourist resort on the Adriatic coast a few days earlier.

Following his arrest, police searched his electronic devices, vehicle and accommodation under court orders. They seized items and digital data allegedly linking him to criminal acts, including two mobile phones and a laptop containing a large amount of data.

The court ordered one month of pre-trial detention, despite the man offering 20,000 euros in bail money and his family home in Novi Sad as collateral.

Croatia’s Chief State Attorney, Ivan Turudic, initially sparked public interest on Monday when he made a comment about a case related to national security. It was then reported by Jutarnji list that Turudic was referring to the arrest of an alleged hacker linked to Serbia’s Security Intelligence Agency, BIA.

It is not known whether the suspect’s alleged access to the computer systems of various institutions and agencies endangered Croatia’s national security in any way, or what he did with any data he may have obtained.

Nera Gajdarov Beg, the suspect’s lawyer, told Jutarnji list that the court’s custody order is being contested.

“An appeal has been filed against the decision to order pretrial detention because we believe that not all legal requirements for such a decision have been met. At this point, I cannot provide details of the defence because the proceedings are in the investigation phase, which is secret,” Gajdarov Beg said.

The Serbian authorities have not commented on the arrest so far. However, Serbian media have reported that Georgije V. is the owner of an active Novi Sad-based company specialising in computer programming and cybersecurity.

World.title: Croatian Serb Leader Deplores Hate Speech at Operation Storm Commemoration
World.content:
This post is also available in this language: Shqip Bos/Hrv/Srp

Milorad Pupovac, president of the Independent Democratic Serb Party, SDSS, and MP, on Friday said that slogans and chants heard on the streets of Knin on August 5, the day marking the 31st anniversary of Operation Storm, represented a “serious attack on constitutional values and democracy”.

Pupovac, leader of the main party representing Serbs in Croatia, argued that “hatred and incitement to crime are incompatible with true patriotism”.

At a press conference, he showed a compilation of recordings from Knin, the town that was the headquarters of a rebel Serbian statelet crushed by the Croatian Army’s Operation Storm in 1995.

They included sports fans and army veterans singing songs glorifying the Ustasha – the army of the Independent State of Croatia, NDH, a World War II fascist puppet state operating under the patronage of Nazi Germany and Fascist Italy.

The recordings also showed people chanting: “We Croats do not drink wine, only the blood of Chetniks [Serbian nationalists] from Knin”; “The battle is fought, it is fought, the Ustasha flag is flying”, as well as insults directed at St Sava, the patron saint of the Serbian Orthodox Church.

“Those who have been trying to pass this off as an act of patriotism for years are actually seriously violating the true values of patriotism. In peacetime, the greatest patriotic virtue is constitutional patriotism,” Pupovac said.

He added that such behaviour was a “vicious attack on democracy”.

The SNV cited articles of the Croatian Constitution that it believes were violated by the shouting of the Ustasha salute “For the Homeland, Ready” and other glorifications of the NDH. The violations came after, not during, the official anniversary celebrations, it said.

Every year, Knin hosts a commemoration of Operation Storm, which liberated about 18 per cent of Croatia’s territory from rebel Serb forces and was followed by the flight of around 200,000 Serbs from Croatia. Some of them later returned.

SDSS leader Pupovac also criticised the Croatian judicial authorities, questioning why the State Attorney’s Office often does not react to hate speech and incitement to violence, appealing for an end to what he called a policy of appeasement.

He warned that failure to condemn such phenomena represents a direct threat to the Serb community in Croatia, and to all citizens who advocate for a state governed by the rule of law.

World.title: Week in Review: The Electoral Merry-Go-Round
World.content:
Last week, a no-confidence motion in the Serbian government was held in the country’s parliament. A boisterous discussion ensued between ruling and opposition MPs, but the motion failed – as expected.

Its real significance was not so much the outcome as the fact that the holding the vote, tabled at the beginning of the year, cleared an important obstacle to calling early parliamentary elections.

President Aleksandar Vucic has fuelled speculation that polls are imminent. Our analysis takes a look a look at what will determine when they happen – and whether they will happen at all.

World.title: One Year in the Palace: How Nawrocki Made the Polish Presidency His Own
World.content:
Nawrocki vetoes again and again

At home, he has repeatedly used his veto to frustrate the government. In his first year, Nawrocki vetoed 41 bills, more than any other Polish president since the fall of Communism. Among the most consequential were legislation linked to Poland’s access to nearly 44 billion euros under the EU’s SAFE defence program, bills concerning the justice system and public finances, two laws expanding rights for unmarried couples and, three times, legislation regulating the crypto-assets market.

The conflict, however, extends beyond legislation. Forty four ambassadorial nominations remain unsigned amid a long-running dispute between the palace and Foreign Minister Radoslaw Sikorski. Poland still has no fully accredited ambassador in Washington, one of its most important diplomatic postings; Bogdan Klich continues to run the embassy as chargé d’affaires.

But Nawrocki has also been unusually active in proposing legislation of his own. In a year, he submitted 22 bills; if he continues at this pace, he is on course to breaking another record by the end of his term. His predecessor Andrzej Duda by comparison submitted 32 during the entire first five years of his presidency.

“I want, in fact, to change the model of the presidency,” Nawrocki told the crowd on Thursday. “The president is not only there to review the law and deal with bills that come from parliament. The president is also there to come forward with legislative initiatives and carry your voice and your demands.”

That ambition goes beyond the number of bills. Poland is a parliamentary democracy in which the government runs most day-to-day policy, while the president has important but more limited powers, including the veto and a role in foreign and defence affairs. Nawrocki has repeatedly floated constitutional change and has been pushing the Presidential Palace towards something closer to a parallel centre of power. His ministers regularly speak on the same issues as their government counterparts, while the 17 presidential councils that aid him, involving around 700 people, are working on a broader development strategy that Nawrocki says he will unveil within months.

“I deeply believe that the presidential development strategy… will become, in the next parliamentary elections, a point of reference for all those who aspire to govern Poland,” he said.

Tusk has accused Nawrocki of trying to change Poland’s political system in practice without changing the constitution. Government spokesman Adam Szlapka described the first year of the presidency as a “bad time”, accusing Nawrocki of thinking primarily in political terms and obstructing government policy.

So far, however, the confrontation has not hurt the president much. Nawrocki remains Poland’s most trusted politician: an IBRiS poll published in late July found that 51.3 per cent of respondents trusted him.

Foreign policy has been another central part of his presidency. Nawrocki has worked hard to cultivate ties with Donald Trump and the US, while taking an increasingly confrontational line towards Ukraine over the historical legacy of the Ukrainian Insurgent Army (UPA), which was responsible for massacres of Polish citizens during World War II.

On Thursday, he again tried to hold both positions at once. It was in Poland’s strategic interest, he said, for Ukrainian soldiers to keep Russia as far from Poland as possible. But it was also in Poland’s interest that “Banderite flags” should not fly in Warsaw, referring to the common term used for fighters of the UPA. “You can help and you can demand.”

World.title: Democracy Digest: Study Finds Slovakia Has Europe’s Weakest Spy Agency
World.content:
Police investigate Czech MP over car crash; countdown to municipal elections; Havel human rights award to be preserved

Czech police this week launched an investigation into MP and government commissioner for the Green Deal Filip Turek on suspicion of bodily harm through negligence over a car crash last month, which saw the honorary president of the Motorist Party – a ruling coalition junior partner – collide with an ambulance at a busy thoroughfare in Prague’s city centre. Caught on CCTV, the traffic accident led to the ambulance’s driver being injured and incapacitated for several days, sparking calls from opposition parties as well as President Petr Pavel for Turek to step down from both his parliamentary and government positions – although experts remain divided on who precisely was to blame for the collision. Turek has since temporarily vacated his position as the government’s plenipotentiary for climate change and the Green Deal pending the results of the investigation and vowed not to use his parliamentary immunity should the police file criminal charges against him. “I think the investigation will go well for me because I kind of know the regulations,” he told TV Nova, also suggesting the injured ambulance driver was “talked into” staying under hospital care longer than necessary for the optics.

This week was the deadline for political parties, movements and coalitions to officially register for the upcoming municipal elections, scheduled to be held across Czechia on October 9-10. Candidacies will now be reviewed by state electoral authorities by August 22. In the capital Prague, two dozen political groupings will take part in the race to win the big and hotly contested prize, a couple more than four years ago, on top of electoral fights for the city’s 57 local districts. In addition to electing their political representatives in the Czech Republic’s more than 6,000 towns, cities and municipalities, voters will also vote for a third of the Senate’s seats. About 155 candidates have registered to run for this year’s partial Senate race, less than the last ballot, mainly a result of pre-election agreements and joint candidates put forward by opposition parties.

Dagmar Havlova, the widow of the former dissident and president, along with the Vize 97 foundation confirmed this week that the Vaclav Havel Human Rights Prize will be preserved and continue to be awarded every year. This follows a previous announcement by the Vaclav Havel Library – which has faced an exodus of staff, sponsors and funding in recent months – that it would no longer participate in the annual award ceremony after Havlova withdrew her consent for the NGO to use the former playwright’s name. Coming with a cheque of 60,000 euros, the award was established shortly after Havel’s death in 2011 to recognise outstanding achievements in the field of human rights and has been awarded by the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe since 2013 together with the Vaclav Havel Library and the Charter 77 Foundation. Past laureates include Venezuelan opposition leader Maria Corina Machado, Russian journalist Vladimir Kara-Murza and Belarusian activist Maria Kalesnikava.

World.title: Lands in Limbo: Danube ‘Microstates’ Dream Big Despite Lack of Recognition
World.content:
From the village of Batina in Croatia's far northeast, the only land route leads to the Free Republic of Liberland, a self-proclaimed microstate on the banks of the Danube River.

A bicycle is the only practical means of transport. The journey begins on an asphalt road before continuing onto gravel and then a dirt track, until the road disappears altogether.

The final kilometre must be covered on foot, across the dried-up bed of a Danube backwater. In summer, it feels more like walking across desert sand before reaching the dense forest that forms the "centre" of Liberland.

World.title: Letter from Brussels: Ceuta Migrant Panic Casts Shadow Over EU’s Summer
World.content:
The weeks that bridge July and August are a period when the EU buildings around Schuman here in Brussels grow quiet, and correspondents’ group chats go mute.

But this year the last week of July was far from quiet. While EU spokespersons were cycling through out-of-office messages and the unlucky ones were covering for absent colleagues, tens of thousands of people crossed from Morocco into the Spanish enclave of Ceuta - the largest single-day surge in irregular arrivals ever recorded on EU territory.

Dozens died. Within two days, the story had stopped being about victims. It had become a story about Europe’s political nerves.

World.title: Croatian Chamber of Commerce: Climate Change is Costing Croatia Dearly
World.content:
August the 8th, 2026 – The Croatian Chamber of Commerce (HGK) has stated that climate change is already costing Croatia exceptionally dearly, and that major investments are required sooner rather than later.

Record heat, droughts and fires are no longer a problem of the future but already represent a serious risk to the Croatian economy, warned Marija Šćulac, vice-president of the Croatian Chamber of Economy (HGK), on HRT. According to the estimates she presented, damages from climate change at the European level without adequate adaptation measures could reach a staggering 126 billion euros annually.

“All these extremely high temperatures, droughts, fires and other disasters today have their real, concrete economic price,” Šćulac warned. Index reports that she added that Croatia belongs to the group of countries particularly exposed to climate risks, among other reasons because of the size and structure of its economy.

Croatia should invest an additional 1.1 percent of GDP annually

According to World Bank estimates cited by Šćulac, Croatia would need to invest an additional around 1.1 percent of GDP annually for climate change adaptation and decarbonisation. Although this is a large amount, she warns that postponing adaptation could be significantly more expensive in the long run. “When we talk about climate change and climate resilience today, we are not talking only about environmental protection, but primarily about economic competitiveness,” she said.

Šćulac says that almost no economic sector is immune to the very serious consequences of climate change, but that some are particularly vulnerable. Agriculture is already facing extreme temperatures, droughts and heavy rainfall that reduce yields. Climate change could also alter tourist habits. “Because of high temperatures, guests will change their habits and come less and less during the hottest summer months,” Šćulac said.

The tourism sector will therefore have to extend the season and adapt business models, while construction must find ways to organise work during extreme heat. The consequences of droughts and low water levels are already being felt in transport and logistics as well.

there’s no alternative to the energy transition

A particular problem is the energy sector, where high temperatures increase electricity consumption while simultaneously creating pressure on production.

“The energy transition, especially in the context of climate change, has no alternative. However, Croatia must accelerate this process tremendously,” Šćulac warned. She emphasised that the transition doesn’t mean only building new solar and wind power plants. She considers the modernisation of the electricity grid key so that it can accept an ever-greater share of production from renewable sources. Battery systems should also play an important role, storing surplus electricity during periods of high production and returning it to the grid when demand rises.

“The modernisation and construction of the electricity grid is the key, largest and most important infrastructure project of Croatia’s energy transition,” Šćulac concluded.

all of europe’s agriculture is suffering

Extreme weather conditions are already strongly affecting agriculture outside Croatia as well. In parts of Europe, pronounced drought and very high temperatures are being recorded, while food price growth has accelerated again. Up in northern Europe, particularly in England and Wales, an exceptionally dry July was recorded, and drought was declared in certain areas of England. The consequences are already visible on agricultural land.

“This picture was taken on the 26th of June this year, and this one on the 29th of July. So the difference is only one month. But look at how it looks after we had such a pronounced heatwave, and this month there was no rain at all,” said geospatial data expert Tom Gray, showing changes in the area of southern England.

Problems are also pronounced in the German state of Bavaria, where farmers expect very weak grain yields. “In my region, there has been practically no precipitation for two months and that’s an absolute catastrophe, especially for cereals. We are recording some of the worst grain yields since records began. And after a strong storm we also had to deal with hail damage,” said farmer Michael Pellmeyer from Freising. High temperatures are also affecting the prices of agricultural products elsewhere in the world. In South Korea some products at markets rose by a third in just one week, and cases of prices doubling were also recorded.

hunger risks are mounting

The UN World Food Programme warns that strong climate disruptions can further increase the number of people facing hunger, especially in combination with wars and economic instability.

“Such conditions include the warming of the Pacific Ocean, which affects the climate around the world. The previous El Niño caused a large increase in hunger,” said Jean-Martin Bauer, director of the Food Security and Nutrition Analysis Service of the World Food Programme. Climate change is thus already simultaneously affecting food production, energy, tourism, transport and infrastructure, which is why the HGK warns that the ability to adapt will increasingly determine the competitiveness of the Croatian economy.

World.title: Czech Tourists Returning to Croatia After Years of Decline
World.content:
August the 8th, 2026 – Czech tourists are finally returning to Croatia in larger numbers after years of decline, with interest in the pre-season also on the up.

Croatian tourism is once again recording growing interest from some of its key European markets, with the biggest shift visible on the Czech market. Ana Roksandic reports for Poslovni that this is occuring after several years of marked decline.

The first data from the eVisitor system for this year confirms the continuation of positive trends on several traditionally important European markets. Croatia is currently recording a strong return of guests from the Czech Republic, stable growth in interest from Hungarian tourists, and a renewed positive dynamic with the Italian market, the Croatian National Tourist Board (HTZ) announced, noting that these are preliminary figures.

Umag, Poreč and Medulin…

Results achieved in the first seven months of the year show that interest from guests from these markets is growing not only during the main summer season, but also in the pre-season, which is particularly important for Croatian tourism in its efforts to further extend the tourist year and reduce dependence on the peak of the season. The most pronounced growth is visible on the Czech market. During the month of July, the number of arrivals by Czech guests was 12 percent higher than in the same month last year, while the number of overnight stays rose by seven percent. Cumulatively, from January to the end of July 2026, Czech tourists recorded five percent more arrivals and overnight stays than in the same period last year.

The return of Czech guests is particularly significant because this is a market that in recent years had been recording a decline in tourist traffic to our country. The largest number of overnight stays by Czech guests during the first seven months was recorded in Istria, Split-Dalmatia and Zadar counties, while among the most visited destinations were Umag, Poreč and Medulin. The return of Czech guests is important for the tourism sector because this is a traditionally large and stable source market whose guests often stay longer and choose different parts of the Croatian coast.

the hungarians are also recording more promising numbers

In addition to the return of the Czech market, positive results are also coming from neighbouring Hungary. This market has for years played an important role in Croatian tourism, primarily due to geographical proximity, good transport connections and the continuous interest of Hungarian guests in holidays on the Adriatic. In July, Hungarian tourists recorded eight percent more arrivals and seven percent more overnight stays than a year earlier, while in the first seven months of 2026 growth of seven percent was recorded in both arrivals and overnight stays.

The largest number of Hungarian guests stayed on Kvarner, in Istria and in Zadar County, confirming their importance for the northern and central parts of the Croatian coast. Particular attention is also being drawn by the renewed positive dynamic with the Italian market. After a period of stagnation, Italian guests have since the beginning of the year once again been showing greater interest in Croatia.

In the first seven months they recorded two percent more arrivals and overnight stays compared with the same period last year, while in July alone the number of arrivals increased by one percent. The Italian market has additional importance for Croatia because of specific travel habits. Italians often choose shorter holidays, weekend trips and stays outside the main season. This year they were particularly attracted by destinations in Istria and on Kvarner.

“experience real croatia”

Alongside the growth in interest from European guests, an additional contribution to strengthening competitiveness is being made by the development of the private accommodation offer. In July, the Croatian National Tourist Board (HTZ), in cooperation with the Booking.com platform, launched the campaign “Experience real Croatia”, aimed at promoting hosts gathered under the Local Host label. The campaign was launched in Germany, Austria, Poland, the Czech Republic and Hungary.

“Today’s guests increasingly seek authenticity, a personal approach and experiences that allow them to get to know the destination in an interesting way. It is precisely with this goal that the Local Host label was developed, which recognises and promotes hosts whose work contributes to the preservation of the identity of the destination, its culture, tradition and environment,” said Kristjan Staničić, director of HTZ.

World.title: Two Super Yachts in Dubrovnik Aquatorium, One Belongs to Ex Google Boss
World.content:
August the 8th, 2026 – Two incredible super yachts are currently in Dubrovnik, and of particular interest is Whisper, a 95-metre-long motor yacht that previously carried the name Kismet.

The luxury yachts Whisper and Anshin, two impressive representatives of the world of super yachts, have been spotted in the Dubrovnik aquatorium. Especially standing out is Whisper (in the photo), a 95-metre-long motor yacht that previously bore the name Kismet. It was built at the renowned German shipyard Lürssen and, after a change of ownership in 2023, was renamed Whisper.

Its current owner is the American entrepreneur and former Google CEO Eric Schmidt, reports Dubrovački dnevnik. It has as many as two helicopter platforms, a pool with a built-in jacuzzi on the sun deck, a private observation platform with a bed for stargazing, wellness facilities, a cinema space, a gym, and a space that can be converted into a sports court.

Before Schmidt, the yacht was owned by the Pakistani-American billionaire Shahid Khan, owner of the Jacksonville Jaguars and Fulham FC. It was precisely from that period that it remained known under the name Kismet, before receiving its new name and owner.

Alongside Whisper, attention was also drawn by Anshin, an elegant super yacht approximately 66 metres long, linked to the Dutch shipyard Feadship, one of the most highly regarded manufacturers of luxury vessels in the world.

It can accommodate up to 14 guests in seven suites, along with 17 crew members. Among its features are a pool, a spa and wellness area, a sea-level club, and a spacious master suite with a private office.

World.title: Ice Deliveries: How Southern Croatia Coped in Summer Before Air Conditioning
World.content:
August the 7th, 2026 – Ice deliveries through the mountains was how southern Croatia coped during the intense summer heat, long before the advent and comfort of air conditioning.

Long before refrigerators and ice machines, the local people of Dubrovnik developed an incredibly organised ice-supply system. Snow was stored in special pits in winter and kept under straw and brushwood.

Imagine what summers looked like a few hundred years ago. The Dalmatian sun is strong, heating the ancient stone walls and streets; electricity doesn’t even exist, nor do refrigerators, freezers, and definitely not air-conditioners. Putni kofer/Lana Mindoljevic writes that instead of getting a full glass of ice in a few seconds, ice was an extremely precious commodity. Down in Dubrovnik, however, it existed even during the middle of summer.

Mountain snow was stored throughout the winter in special pits in the Konavle hills, kept under straw and brushwood, and in summer lowered by horses down to Cavtat and sent by boat to Dubrovnik. This precious ice was so highly valued that it was given as a gift to distinguished guests, and Dubrovnik even had an Ice Street.

Hundreds of kilograms of ice arrived in the City every summer

How was it possible that something considered a real little miracle during the hot summer days could already be found on the tables of Dubrovnik’s nobility? And not just a few accidentally preserved pieces. In the hottest part of summer, according to surviving accounts, around 260 kilograms of ice arrived in Dubrovnik every day.

Hundreds of kilograms of something that had to be produced months earlier, protected from the spring and summer sun, carried across the mountain, loaded onto horses, brought down to the sea and then transported by boat to the City. Apart from showing the fascinating organisational skill of the former Republic of Dubrovnik, this also reveals how much people already sought ways to refresh themselves in summer.

In winter they stored snow in pits and kept it until summer

Dubrovnik’s main reserve of cold lay far from the hot stone of Stradun, in the Konavle hills, in the Sniježnica area. The Museums and Galleries of Konavle write that in the time of the Republic of Dubrovnik three ice-houses (ledenice) were filled every winter – special natural or adapted pits into which snow was collected. The work was most often done in January or February. The snow was thrown in and compacted, then covered with brushwood and straw, and the ice-houses were closed and locked. The prince (knez) was responsible for their operation and maintenance, and the whole process took place under the supervision of a guard.

The ice-houses were by no means just small holes in the ground. They are located about a two-hour walk from the village of Duba and have been thoroughly explored by speleologists. The Konavle museum blog states that the Great Ice-house is 11 metres deep and 12 metres long, while the Small one is four metres deep and eight metres long.

When summer arrived, the night-time delivery operation began

Although collecting the ice was already interesting, the method of transport when summer arrived was even more fascinating. During the warmer part of the year, ice delivery from the Konavle hills to Dubrovnik was organised almost daily. Ice was taken from the ice-houses in the late afternoon, when the greatest heat had subsided, then loaded onto horses and brought down towards Cavtat.

From Cavtat, the journey continued by sea to the City of Dubrovnik. After the horse journey, the ice would set off by boat from Cavtat in the early morning hours so that it would not melt before reaching its destination.

For the year 1783, there’s concrete data: almost 16 tonnes of ice were brought to dubrovnik

How extensively the whole system was used is best shown by one surviving account. HRT’s programme Gradoplov, referring to Zdravko Šundrica’s book The Secret Box of the Dubrovnik Archive II, gives very precise figures for 1783. From 20 May to 20 August, 12,123 oka of ice arrived in Dubrovnik – that is, 15,759 kilograms. Transport required 146 horse-loads, and the whole operation cost 129 of the prince’s thalers.

in some cases, ice was brought in from herzegovina

On average, around 170 kilograms of ice arrived in the City every day during that period. In June about 110 kilograms were used, in July 170, and in August consumption rose. From 1 to 20 August Dubrovnik needed around 260 kilograms of ice daily. And every one of those kilograms first had to be produced with the help of winter alone, preserved for months and physically delivered to the city. If the winters were weak and did not produce enough snow to fill all three ice-houses, ice was obtained from the Herzegovinian mountains.

dubrovnik’s very own ice street

Over time the trade became so organised that ice had its own place in the City. HRT notes that there was an Ice Street (Ulica od leda) in Dubrovnik where ice could be bought, and interesting equipment for its use was also developed. One of the best examples was the kantiflora, a special glass bottle for cooling drinks. Ice was, of course, available only to the wealthier, so it was often given as a gift to distinguished guests. The Museums and Galleries of Konavle mention another tasty detail: ice cream was already spoken of in Dubrovnik in the 18th century.

Remains of the old ice-houses are still hidden on Sniježnica mountain today

The story does not live only in archival documents today. The Great and Small Ice-houses still exist in the Konavle hills, and in 2016 speleologists explored them and drew up their plans. The Cavtat-Konavle Tourist Board notes that the trail to the Konavle ice-houses is marked and starts in the village of Duba by the Church of St Stephen.

World.title: What Does New Pension Increase Mean for Defenders Who Worked After War?
World.content:
August the 7th, 2026 – There is set to be a new pension increase for Croatian defenders, but what will the situation be for those who did continue working after the war ended?

Index reports that the government has now presented a new model for increasing defenders’ pensions, which should apply from the 1st of January 2027 if the legislative amendments pass in Parliament. Among the beneficiaries covered by the changes are also defenders who returned to work after the war.

A defender who returned to work after the war and later retired under the old-age pension scheme basically receives a pension calculated in the same way as other workers, according to years of service and salaries. Then, as a defender, the pension is additionally increased depending on the time spent in the war, especially in the combat sector.

The position of these defenders was precisely one of the main reasons why Možemo demanded a change in the calculation method that would raise the pensions of the covered beneficiaries by up to 20 percent.

The Government today presented a different model under which the new supplement depends directly on the wartime service record. For every month spent in the combat sector the pension would be higher by three euros per month, and for a month in the non-combat sector by 50 cents.

Around 68,000 defenders are drawing pensions from the general system

In the refined proposal by Možemo, 68,561 beneficiaries are listed whose pensions are calculated primarily according to the rules of the general pension system, but with the application of defenders’ rights. On average they had around 31 years of service, and the average pension amounted to 668.37 euros.

The Ministry today presented a very similar current figure of 68,269 beneficiaries in that category.

Možemo intended its proposal primarily for defenders who returned to the labour market after the war and proposed an increase in the starting factor, which could raise their pensions by up to 20 percent. A higher factor would also apply when determining the lowest defenders’ pension.

The Government’s supplement is calculated completely differently. Its amount does not depend on the amount of the current pension, but on the number of months spent in the war and whether it was in the combat or non-combat sector.

what would an actual concrete example of that look like?

Let us take a simplified example of a defender who today receives 668.37 euros, which is the average pension of the mentioned group. If we assume that under the Možemo proposal he would achieve the full 20 percent increase, he would receive around 134 euros more per month, meaning his pension would rise to around 802 euros. Under the Croatian Government’s model, the increase would depend on the length of combat service.

In this concrete example the Government’s supplement would overtake the 20 percent increase after approximately three years and nine months spent in the combat sector.

This isn’t a universal threshold. For every defender, everything depends on their current pension and how large an increase that individual would achieve under the Možemo proposal. In this example, for simplicity, it was assumed that the person did not participate in the non-combat sector.

The length of participation in the war already today affects certain defenders’ pension rights. The Možemo proposal would not change that, but the new increase would not depend directly on whether someone spent one year or five years in the combat sector. Under the Government’s proposal that is precisely the main criterion for the new supplement. One year of combat service means 36 euros more per month, three years 108 euros, and five years 180 euros. The difference between the combat and non-combat sectors is also large. Five years in the non-combat sector would bring a monthly increase of 30 euros, while five years of combat service would bring 180 euros.

government proposals encompass a wider number of people

The Government’s increase isn’t intended only for defenders who continued working after the war. The Ministry announced today that the new supplement according to wartime service will be received by 104,560 defenders, while various proposed amendments would cover a total of 201,304 defenders and members of their families.

Defenders who continued working are thus included in the Government’s model, but they are not singled out as a special group. In other words, Možemo proposed an increase of up to 20 percent for a narrower circle of beneficiaries, while the Government proposes a supplement for a wider circle of defenders whose amount will depend directly on the number of months spent in the combat and non-combat sectors.

former pension reductions are also being scrapped

The Government also proposes the abolition of the pension reduction of 8 to 20 percent that is still applied to some retired soldiers, police officers and other authorised officials. This is a separate measure, distinct from the new supplement calculated according to the time spent in the Homeland War.

The abolition of the reduction should from 2027 cover around 34,000 beneficiaries, and the Ministry estimates that their pensions would as a result rise on average by around 70 euros per month. This measure is not limited only to defenders, but applies to all beneficiaries covered by that special pension regulation. The Government’s amendments have not yet been adopted. After public consultation they should be sent to the parliamentary procedure, and application is planned as of the 1st of January 2027.

World.title: Croatian Mountain Rescue Service Rescues Another Foreign National on Biokovo
World.content:
August the 7th, 2026 – The Croatian Mountain Rescue Service (HGSS) has had to rescue yet another foreign national stuck on Biokovo.

As Index reports, the Croatian Mountain Rescue Service (HGSS) has reported a night-time rescue of a foreign national who got lost last night in the area of Sutvid above Živogošće near Makarska, at around 1,050 metres above sea level on the southeastern part of Biokovo. HGSS received the call on Wednesday at around 18:30.

The man reported that due to high temperatures and lack of water he had become severely dehydrated, felt extreme weakness and was no longer able to safely continue moving or find the way. Four rescuers from the HGSS Makarska Station immediately set out into the field, and due to the demanding terrain they were soon joined by another four.

“After several hours of night ascent, the rescuers reached the injured person at 22:50. First aid was provided at the scene and after a rest and rehydration, accompanied by the rescuers, he began the descent towards the vehicle,” the HGSS Makarska Station announced.

The operation was successfully completed at 02:50. Photos published by HGSS show that the man had set out on the ascent in sandals. HGSS once again warns everyone not to go into the mountains without appropriate equipment and a sufficient amount of fluids.

“We’d once again like to appeal to all visitors to Biokovo to please, please carefully plan their trip before going into the mountains. During the summer months it is absolutely paramount that you bring a sufficient amount of water, avoid the hottest part of the day and use appropriate hiking footwear,” HGSS said.

World.title: This Croatian Island is Closer to Italy Than to the Mainland of its Own Country
World.content:
August the 7th, 2026 – There’s a far-flung Croatian island that is closer to neighbouring Italy than to the Croatian mainland. Only a lighthouse keeper lives there, and he’d be able to arrive on Italian shores much more quickly than he’d manage to arrive in Croatia.

Far out in the Adriatic Sea sits an isolated island from which, on a clear day, both shores of the Adriatic are clearly visible. Putni kofer writes that only a lighthouse keeper lives there, and day-trippers rarely stop by.

If you look at a map of the Adriatic and study the area from Split towards the shores of Italy, you will see the islands of Brač, then Hvar, then the more distant Vis and Korčula, followed by the open-sea island of Biševo… After that long stretch there is nothing, only deep blue emptiness, and then, almost in the middle of the open sea, another “little dot”. That’s Vela Palagruža, Croatia’s most remote island of all. It’s a narrow rocky islet barely a kilometre and a half long. From here to the Italian coast, you’ll cover just 68 kilometres, while to Split it is more than 120. In other words, this piece of Croatia is almost twice as close to foreign land as to its own.

this position made the island so important

It is precisely this position that for centuries gave Palagruža an importance out of all proportion to its size. It is the only point on the Adriatic from which, in clear weather, both the Italian and Croatian coasts can be made out, so for thousands of years the island served as a landmark and resting place on the long voyages between the Italian shore and Dalmatia.

Archaeologists have been confirming this for decades. At the Salamandrija site, on the plateau right next to the lighthouse, traces of human presence going deep into prehistory have been found, and in later periods the island became a sanctuary for seafarers. Finds of pottery inscribed with the name of Diomedes, the hero from the Iliad, confirmed that Palagruža was a place where sailors paid homage to him before setting out onto the open sea.

it remained under italian control until 1860

Until 1860, Palagruža was under Italian administration. When the Austrian authorities took it over, a lookout service was established on the island, and then in 1875 the lighthouse was built. Twenty years later a meteorological station was added. Since then Palagruža has never been without people.

The stone lighthouse stands in the middle of the island at 90 metres above sea level; with its lantern it rises to about 126 metres above the sea. A steep path about 700 metres long leads up to it – a real mountaineering stretch on which donkeys once helped the lighthouse keepers. About ten years ago they were replaced by a cable winch built specifically for this purpose.

the lighthouse keeper welcomes guests… but rarely

Today only the lighthouse keeper lives on Palagruža all year round; in the past entire lighthouse families – more than ten people – used to stay there. It is he who, during the summer, welcomes the guests who manage to reach this little piece of paradise.

And for those rare visitors that means exactly what it sounds like. There is no shop, restaurant, bar or pharmacy. There is not even the possibility of quickly buying something extra. Plovput looks after the lighthouse, and through them one can arrange summer accommodation in one of the two four-bed apartments, with a minimum stay of seven days. The building stands high on the island’s ridge, so a stay is not recommended for people in poorer health. What you get in return is hard to compare with anything else on the Adriatic: silence, the sea on all sides, and the feeling that you are on a planet of your own.

the highest number of endemic plants in all of southern dalmatia

Vela Palagruža is 1,400 metres long and only 300 metres wide, with gentler slopes on one side and vertical cliffs on the other. The climate is exceptionally mild and rainfall is scarce, so vegetation is lush in spring, autumn and winter, while in summer the coast is almost bare. Among the islands of southern Dalmatia, Palagruža has the most endemic plants. Here grow the Palagruža cabbage, Palagruža centaury, Palagruža horsetail, open-sea spurge and other species you will not find elsewhere. The archipelago around the main island also includes Mala Palagruža and a series of rocks and reefs. To the south-east lies the islet of Galijula, officially the southernmost land point of Croatia.

the former home of the richest fishing grounds in the entire adriatic

The waters around Palagruža were once one of the richest fishing grounds in the Adriatic. Today lobster and white fish are mainly caught here, and the area remains primarily a fishing zone. Visits have to be arranged with the lighthouse keepers or with one of the fishermen from Komiža; organised group excursions practically do not exist. For a place of this kind, that is probably not bad news.

World.title: Hajduk Stun Žalgiris 5-2 Away in Conference League Qualifier
World.content:
Hajduk beat Žalgiris 5-2 away from home in the first leg of the third qualifying round for the Conference League. The Split side celebrated in Vilnius thanks to goals from Michele Šego (5′, 44′), Adrion Pajaziti (56′), Dalisson (73′) and Rokas Pukštas (75′). Nikola Petković (35′) and former Hajduk man Marko Capan (86′) scored for the hosts. The return leg is in a week, on August 13, kicking off at 9 pm at Poljud.

This is Hajduk’s first away win in Europe in almost six years, since a 1-0 triumph at Renova in the second qualifying round of the Europa League. The winner of the Hajduk–Žalgiris tie will face the winner of the clash between Raków and Hammarby in the next qualifying round; their first meeting finished goalless.

Two goals from Šego put Hajduk ahead at the break

Hajduk took the lead as early as the fifth minute. Pajaziti played in Marin Šotiček, who squared the ball back from the edge of the box. Šego ran onto it, and Žalgiris captain Yuri Kendysh brought him down, conceding a penalty and picking up a yellow card in the process. Šego made no mistake from the spot, sending the keeper the wrong way to make it 1-0.

Just four minutes later, Hajduk squandered a big chance to extend their lead. Goalkeeper Vincentas Šarkauskas spilled the ball, and Pukštas crossed from the right for Šotiček, who volleyed wide from close range.

Hajduk won another penalty in the 13th minute. Šotiček again broke through on the left and entered the box, where he was brought down by Deividas Šešplaukis. Šego stepped up again, but this time Šarkauskas got down to save his effort, which was heading into the left corner.

Žalgiris pulled level in the 35th minute. Bilenkyi played in Nikola Petković, who slipped away from the attention of Hajduk’s defense unnoticed. Goalkeeper Silić misjudged the flight of the ball and pushed it into the path of the Žalgiris forward, who made it 1-1.

Hajduk still went into the break in front, however. In the 44th minute, following a foul on Pukštas, Šego produced a phenomenal strike straight from a free kick from around twenty meters to make it 2-1.

Hajduk seal the win in the second half

The second half began with a forced change for Hajduk, as center-back Alec van Hoorenbeeck was forced off through injury and replaced by Ron Raci. Hajduk continued to press forward and extended their lead in the 56th minute. After a short combination from a corner, Pajaziti got into the box and finished precisely from an angle to make it 3-1.

Hajduk then settled the tie with two quick goals. The first came in the 73rd minute, when a long ball from goalkeeper Toni Silić set up Anđelo Šutalo to assist Dalisson, who finished from the right to make it 4-1. Just two minutes later, Rokas Pukštas cut out a pass from the home side’s defense, went past his marker and scored from five meters to make it 5-1.

Žalgiris did manage to pull one back before the end. Former Hajduk player Marko Capan, who had come on in the second half, scored from a free kick from around twenty meters in the 86th minute. In stoppage time, Hajduk also had a goal disallowed, as Šotiček’s effort was ruled out for offside.

World.title: Apple officially enters Iraq under new digital services framework
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Apple has legally joined Iraq’s regulated digital market, having met the country’s standards for digital platforms and services, according to the Communications and Media Commission (CMC).

According to the regulator, Apple has been categorized as a trusted digital service provider in Iraq, which includes the App Store, Apple Music, Apple Podcasts, Apple Arcade, and Apple Ads.

The certification means Apple’s digital services may now function under an official Iraqi regulatory framework, having passed the CMC’s technical and legal standards.

Iraqi officials said the decision is anticipated to boost the country’s digital economy and enhance the investment climate for multinational technology firms.

The development also corresponds with a significant step toward Apple’s physical presence in the Iraqi market. Asiacell has reached a direct arrangement with Apple to include iPhones in its retail network across Iraq.

As part of the cooperation, Asiacell will provide real Apple products with valid warranties throughout its network, while retail personnel will undergo Apple-approved training.

The regulatory permission and Asiacell deal represent a substantial change in Apple’s position in Iraq, pushing both digital services and official device distribution further into a market of over 46 million people.

The move is another indication of Iraq’s quickly emerging technology and consumer market, as Baghdad attempts to lure global corporations, legalize digital services, and promote increased investment in the country’s information technology industry.

World.title: Al-Ghodwa deploys Linde warehouse equipment in Baghdad
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Linde Material Handling of Germany has completed a new warehouse technology project in Baghdad with its official Iraqi partner, Al-Ghodwa Group, as modern logistics systems gain traction in Iraq.

The project was completed in early August, and it comprised the installation and commissioning of two Linde Very Narrow Aisle (VNA) trucks built for high-density warehouse operations.

As part of the turnkey project, Al-Ghodwa installed the guiding system, calibrated and tested the equipment, and taught the local operators.

The technology enables firms to store more items in their current warehouse space by running equipment securely in tighter lanes, which increases productivity and reduces space needs.

The project combines Linde’s German warehouse technology with local installation, maintenance, and after-sales services in Iraq.

Linde Material Handling is a subsidiary of Germany’s KION Group, one of the world’s biggest producers of industrial vehicles and a leading supplier of warehouse automation systems.

The Baghdad installation comes as Iraq’s logistics and distribution industry grows, amid investment in manufacturing, retail, transportation, and private-sector growth.

World.title: Saudi renews invitation to Iraq PM as Baghdad, Riyadh seek to repair ties
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Saudi Arabia has extended an invitation to Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi to visit Riyadh as the two countries try to regain momentum in ties after a dangerous escalation involving Iran-backed militias operating from Iraqi soil.

Al-Zaidi met with Saudi intelligence head Khalid bin Ali Al-Humaidan in Baghdad on Friday, with the Saudi official conveying a message from the kingdom’s leadership extending the offer and discussing greater security cooperation, according to the Iraqi government.

The meeting is notable since Al-Zaidi canceled a scheduled visit to Saudi Arabia last month in response to US-Saudi airstrikes on Iran-aligned armed groups in Iraq.

These operations followed a series of drone assaults on Saudi Arabia.

Riyadh claimed that Iran-backed militias fired drones from Iraqi territory, attempting to damage oil installations in the Eastern Province and targets near Riyadh, and publicly urged Baghdad to prevent its land from being used as a launchpad for assaults against the country.

Saudi Arabia then launched operations with US troops against Iran-backed militia strongholds in Iraq, increasing pressure on Baghdad to bring armed organizations operating outside of effective official control under its authority.

During Friday’s meeting, Al-Zaidi underlined Iraq’s refusal to allow its land to be used for attacks on Saudi Arabia or any other country, emphasizing Baghdad’s commitment to sovereignty, good neighbor relations, and regional security.

According to the Iraqi statement, the two sides agreed to maintain information sharing and security cooperation, with Baghdad aiming to avoid future assaults that may prompt another military reaction on Iraqi soil.

The outreach coincides with Saudi Arabia’s efforts to deepen regional security relationships.

On Friday, Riyadh, Ankara, and Islamabad signed the Mecca Joint Defense Agreement, which states that any military assault on one of the three nations is considered an attack on all.

Saudi authorities are also apprehensive about additional strikes by Iran-aligned forces.

For Al-Zaidi, the repeated Saudi invitation provides a chance to mend ties with one of Iraq’s most significant Arab neighbors while also displaying Baghdad’s determination to prevent Iran-backed forces from dictating its regional connections.

The implications extend beyond security. Iraq has been pursuing more Saudi and Gulf investment as part of a larger push to diversify its economy, attract foreign money, and enhance trade and infrastructural ties with its Arab neighbors.

As a result, Friday’s meeting constitutes a crucial step in moving Baghdad-Riyadh relations past last month’s dispute. However, continued progress is likely to be strongly dependent on Iraq’s capacity to show that attacks on its neighbors would not be launched from its territory in the future.

World.title: Spain imposes border checks on Italy as migrant showdown grows
World.content:
Madrid – Spain announced on Friday it would introduce temporary border checks on travellers from Italy in response to Rome imposing similar measures after a mass migrant rush into Ceuta.

The checks, which come “amid the persistent irregular migration pressure” facing Italy, will start at midnight on Saturday and last until September 7, Spain’s interior ministry said in a statement.

Hours earlier, Spain threatened Italy with countermeasures if it did not swiftly lift its own border checks, drawing a rebuff from Rome.

The rare spat between the European Union and NATO allies came after tens of thousands of people crossed from Morocco to Spain’s North African territory on July 30-31 in an unprecedented, deadly rush.

The scenes infuriated EU members that back a hard line on irregular immigration, including Italy which imposed a one-month suspension of its visa free-travel Schengen deal with Spain.

The Spanish government slammed the measure Friday as “unfair, contrary to the EU’s interests and discriminatory for the Spanish population”.

Foreign Minister Jose Manuel Albares described it as “a torpedo fired at the hull of European unity.”

“We urge the government of Italy to rectify, put an end to the checks and treat Spaniards like other European citizens,” the government said.

He threatened “proportional measures” in response by Sunday if Italy failed to comply.

– ‘Creating rifts’ –

Within hours, the government of Italy’s far-right Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni said it “had no intention of revising the decision” before August 15, when it said Spanish authorities “expected a new wave of migration” to hit Ceuta.

“Italy does not accept ultimatums or impositions from abroad regarding national security and border control,” Meloni’s office said in a statement.

“Only when there is certainty that there are no security or terrorism risks to Italy, that no new wave is occurring, and that no irregular migrants are heading toward European territory, will the decision be reconsidered,” it read.

Spain’s interior ministry announced the reciprocal measures within hours.

Spanish police have been monitoring online rumours and social media about possible fresh arrivals in Ceuta in mid-August, according to local media. But authorities have not expressly said they expect a repeat of last week’s rush.

Border authorities would in the meantime “do their utmost to ensure maximum ease of movement for Spanish and European citizens” who are not affected by border checks, the Italian statement added.

Italy, which does not share a land border with Spain, introduced border controls at maritime and air entry points for third-country nationals arriving from the Iberian country.

The move announced on July 31 was an “extraordinary measure” intended to “safeguard national security and prevent possible repercussions for our nation”, Meloni said at the time.

She was among EU leaders who called for Spain to be suspended from the visa-free Schengen travel zone after the Ceuta incident, despite such a move being legally impossible.

Italy’s coalition government has sought to stop the tens of thousands of people who land in small boats on the country’s shores each year.

The Spanish government warned against “creating rifts and sterile conflicts driven by internal electoral motives” and said “we trust that pro-European sentiment, common sense and good faith prevail”.

Of the 72,000 people who entered Ceuta, 70,000 have returned to Morocco, according to official Spanish figures.

Spanish authorities said 80 people died in the crossings.

Moroccan rights groups however estimate the figure to be higher. The Moroccan Association for Human Rights (AMDH) and the European Coordination for Human Rights in Morocco on Friday said at least 141 deaths were recorded and that the toll was likely to rise.

Morocco’s interior ministry has said 11 people died on its side of the border, all but one by drowning.

Those who remain in Ceuta — including hundreds of unaccompanied children — face dire living conditions with little access to food, water, and shelter.

World.title: Saudi Arabia, Turkey, Pakistan sign defence pact amid regional war
World.content:
Riyadh – Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan signed a joint defence agreement on Friday amid violence in the region from Houthi attacks and the US-Iran war.

Riyadh is looking to strengthen its security ties against the backdrop of war between the United States and Iran, which has drawn in surrounding nations and disrupted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea.

The war has emboldened Iran and its Houthi allies in Yemen, both of which have attacked Saudi Arabia, while analysts say Washington is now seen as an increasingly unreliable partner.

In a joint statement published by the official Saudi press agency and Pakistan’s foreign ministry, the three countries announced the signing of the “Mecca Joint Defence Agreement”.

They declared a “shared commitment to further strengthening their collective security and to promoting peace, security and stability in the region and beyond”.

Pakistan’s foreign ministry said the pact meant an attack on any member would be regarded as an attack on all, adding it was “intended to strengthen collective deterrence”.

Ankara nonetheless said later that the agreement was “not aimed at any particular country”, according to a post on X by the presidency’s communications director.

It added that “the agreement is not in contradiction with the commitments of Turkey’s existing international alliances, including those at the heart of NATO,” according to a post on X by the government’s anti-disinformation service.

Riyadh said “the agreement does not represent an effort to establish a military axis or a sectarian bloc”.

“Nor is it linked to any nuclear ambitions or arms race, rather it is focused on building sustainable capabilities,” Deputy Minister for Public Diplomacy Rayed Krimly said on X.

The “does not constitute a threat to the security of any country in the region”, he added.

– ‘Layers of security’ –

Since the onset of the regional war, Saudi Arabia has grown closer to Turkey, Egypt and Pakistan, which have been pushing for mediation and a resolution to the conflict.

Umar Karim, an expert on Saudi foreign policy at the University of Birmingham, England, said the alignment “is clearly oriented towards Iran and meant to address Iran’s new strategic approach which is geared towards dominance of the broader Gulf region”.

The fact that Turkey and Pakistan border Iran means they could “exercise a different kind of leverage” on Tehran, he added.

A source close to the Saudi military and government told AFP before the signing that although the agreement had been under discussion for a long time, “the latest developments in the region expedite it”.

Andreas Krieg of King’s College London said the deal showed a clear desire to diversify alliances beyond the United States.

“Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan are not trying to replace the United States,” he said.

“They are building the capacity to protect their interests when Washington cannot or will not do so.”

Riyadh, in particular, he added, “wants several layers of security rather than one American umbrella”, after the shock of the Iran war.

The deal will support Saudi Arabia’s ambitions to become an organiser of regional security and diversify its defence umbrella, said Krieg. Turkey and Pakistan gain political clout and access to potential Saudi investments, he added.

Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan met Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman in Mecca on Friday, the Turkish presidency said on X, sharing an image of the meeting.

Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and army chief Asim Munir also travelled to the Gulf kingdom for the signing.

– Renewed Houthi attacks –

Saudi Arabia and Pakistan had already announced a mutual defence pact in 2025, a move that drew attention because Pakistan is the Muslim world’s only nuclear-armed state.

The deal also comes as a truce between Riyadh and the Houthi rebels in neighbouring Yemen has broken down. The Houthis have launched attacks on Saudi soil and declared a maritime blockade against Saudi Arabia, which they have attempted to enforce by attacking Saudi tankers.

The Houthis, backed by Iran, have added pressure to Gulf energy exporters — already under strain from Tehran’s blockade of the Strait of Hormuz — by threatening Red Sea shipping.

Saudi Arabia has led a military coalition backing Yemen’s internationally recognised government against the Houthis since 2015.

A truce was agreed four years ago which largely held until hostilities broke out again in recent weeks.

On Thursday, the Houthis killed at least 58 Yemeni government troops in missile and drone attacks, a military source said, in one of the conflict’s deadliest days in years.

World.title: US dollar exchange rate continues to rise in Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The exchange rate for the US dollar compared to the Iraqi dinar rose on Thursday in the Iraqi capital, Baghdad, and the capital of the Kurdistan region of Iraq, Erbil.

The US dollar exchange rate slightly rose in Baghdad’s al-Kifah and al-Harithiya stock exchanges, reaching 1,523.5 Iraqi dinars compared to 1,520.5 Iraqi dinars on Thursday morning.

The exchange rate in currency exchange shops in Baghdad ranged between 1,530 Iraqi dinars and 1,520 Iraqi dinars, Shafaq News reported.

In Erbil, the US dollar exchange rate also rose, fluctuating between 1,525.5 and 1,525 Iraqi dinars.

The Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) said in February 2023 that it has begun using the new US dollar exchange rate of 1,300 dinars to every US dollar.

The previous official exchange rate was 1,450 dinars to one US dollar, which was being exchanged in the parallel market at a rate of 1,550 dinars.

While the official exchange rate was 1,450 dinars per dollar in January 2023, the US currency was being exchanged at 1,610 dinars during the same month in the parallel market in Iraq. This variation indicated a difference of over 10 percent in the exchange rates.

World.title: Iraq to increase production from Kirkuk oil fields
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Oil Minister Basim Khudair announced on Thursday plans to increase oil production from the Kirkuk oilfields.

The decision intends to capitalize on a recent agreement with Turkey for exporting oil to the port of Ceyhan.

This move also aims to circumvent the closure of the Strait of Hormuz and increase Iraq’s oil exports via ports on the Mediterranean.

The instruction utilizes the recently expanded Kirkuk-Ceyhan pipeline deal, with the goal of increasing exports from 180,000 barrels per day to approximately 750,000 barrels per day.

Khudair stated that increasing production lays the groundwork for boosting export volumes through Turkey to 1.5 million barrels per day.

Turkish Petroleum Corporation (TPAO) has officially partnered with British Petroleum (BP) to bolster cooperation in oil and natural gas projects in Kirkuk oilfields.

In 2025, BP reached a deal with Iraq’s North Oil Company (NOC) to develop oil fields in the northern Iraqi province of Kirkuk, with investments projected to reach $25 billion.

The step is part of the Iraqi government’s attempts to optimize energy sector investments, increase oil output, and minimize gas flaring.

The enhanced output directly addresses the Iraqi government’s growing deficit as a result of continued maritime restrictions in the Strait of Hormuz.

By producing more petroleum from Kirkuk, Baghdad reduces internal shipping expenses from southern fields while increasing supplies to global markets via outlets on the Mediterranean.

World.title: Iraqi Prime Minister orders higher military readiness as security tensions rise
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister and Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces Ali Al-Zaidi has directed all security and military formations to raise their operational readiness and combat preparedness, according to the Security Media Cell.

The directive aims to maintain a high state of preparedness across Iraq’s security forces through intensified training exercises and operational movements designed to strengthen national security and protect public interests.

In a statement, the Security Media Cell said the Commander-in-Chief instructed security and military forces to increase their level of readiness while conducting training exercises and field movements.

The measures are intended to ensure that all security formations remain fully prepared to carry out their assigned duties and respond to potential security developments.

According to the statement, the directive is part of ongoing efforts to maintain continuous operational readiness across Iraq’s armed forces.

The Security Media Cell said the enhanced readiness program is designed to reinforce Iraq’s security framework and improve the capabilities of military and security units.

Officials stated that maintaining high readiness contributes to:

Strengthening national security.

Preserving public stability.

Protecting Iraqi citizens.

Safeguarding public institutions and national interests.

The government has increasingly emphasized preparedness amid evolving regional security challenges.

The announcement comes during a period of elevated security concerns in Iraq following recent regional developments and heightened tensions involving armed groups.

The official statement, however, does not specify any particular threat or military operation linked to the readiness order.

Some media reports and political analysts have suggested the move may be connected to broader security developments or precautionary planning ahead of upcoming government deadlines. These assessments are analytical interpretations and were not included in the official Security Media Cell statement.

The latest directive reflects Baghdad’s continued focus on ensuring the operational effectiveness of Iraq’s security institutions.

By ordering additional training activities and maintaining high alert levels, the government aims to preserve stability while ensuring security forces remain prepared to respond to any developments affecting the country’s security environment.

World.title: Sick teen dies as ambulance gets stuck in mud for hours in J&K's Rajouri
World.content:
NEW DELHI: A 17-year-old girl died while being taken to hospital in Jammu and Kashmir's Rajouri district after the vehicle carrying her remained stuck in mud for nearly three hours.

The district administration has suspended a government engineer and ordered an inquiry into the incident.

The girl, a resident of remote Methyani village, had fallen seriously ill on Friday and was being taken to Government Medical College (GMC), Rajouri, when the vehicle became stranded following a mudslide at Chak Methyani, officials told news agency PTI.

Volunteers later managed to pull the vehicle out, but the girl's condition deteriorated and she died while she was being taken to the hospital, according to officials.

The incident occurred on the Chak Methyani-Panglar-Kotecharwal road, which serves as the only road link for several remote villages in the area. The road was washed away near Methyani during last year's monsoon and had subsequently been restored temporarily.

The same stretch was hit by another mudslide around two weeks ago, leaving the Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana (PMGSY) road unmotorable, officials said.





According to the report submitted by the Additional Deputy Commissioner (ADC), Kotranka, the girl had been suffering from an illness for nearly a month and had previously been admitted to Government Medical College Hospital, Jammu. She was discharged around two weeks ago, but her condition worsened again, prompting her family to take her to GMC Rajouri.

The ADC's report said the blocked road resulted in a delay of nearly two to three hours.

It also found that the stretch remained in "extremely poor condition" due to landslides and deep ditches, making it unfit for vehicular movement.

The report further noted that residents of Narla Bamble, Kotecharwal and Panglar continued to face difficulties in transporting patients, food grains and fertilisers.

The district administration said the executive engineer, PMGSY division Rajouri, had informed officials through an official WhatsApp group that the road had been restored and was "trafficable".

However, subsequent verification by the ADC found otherwise.

Taking note of the report, district development commissioner (DDC) Rajouri Abhishek Sharma ordered the immediate suspension of the assistant executive engineer (AEE), PMGSY Sub-Division Kalakote, who was in charge of the road project, pending an inquiry.

World.title: Rijiju vs Rahul over women's quota Bill: Support 'unconditionally' remark gets 'already passed' retort
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Parliamentary affairs minister

on Saturday targeted Lok Sabha leader of opposition

over his recent remarks on womenâs freedom of expression and challenged him to support the BJP-backed Womenâs Reservation Bill âunconditionallyâ.

However, Rahul strongly countered Rijiju's challenge with questioning women Bill's link to delimitation.

Rijijuâs remarks came after Rahul Gandhi posted a video calling for greater freedom of expression for women and arguing that India cannot fully develop without women being able to express themselves freely.

Responding to the senior Congress leader, Rijiju said Rahul Gandhiâs message appeared to be a positive change and urged the Congress to support the Womenâs Reservation Bill without conditions.

âThis seems to be a positive message from the Congress Party. There's a visible change of heart in Shri Rahul Gandhi Ji about the Women. Now, I hope the Congress Party will support the Women's Reservation Bill unconditionally,â the Union minister posted on X.

However, Rahul Gandhi quickly hit back at Rijiju, pointing out that the Womenâs Reservation Bill was already passed by Parliament in 2023.

The Congress leader then questioned why the Centre is seeking to link the implementation of womenâs reservation with the delimitation exercise.





Taking to X, Rahul wrote in Hindi, which loosely translates to: "Mr Rijiju, who would know better than you, as the parliamentary affairs minister that the Women's Reservation Bill 2023 has already been passed unanimously, with the full support of the Congress."

"The question is, why has it still not been implemented even after three years, and why do you now want to unnecessarily link it to delimitation? Implement the 2023 law.

Without any conditions," he added.

The Congress and other opposition parties have supported the Womenâs Reservation Bill but have opposed linking its implementation to the delimitation exercise. The opposition has demanded that womenâs reservation be delinked from delimitation, which would determine the number of Lok Sabha seats.

The Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam, 2023, was passed by both Houses of Parliament.

However, its implementation did not move forward after the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill failed to secure the required two-thirds majority of members present and voting in the Lok Sabha on April 17.

The legislation provides for 33% reservation for women in the Lok Sabha and state legislative assemblies and links its implementation to delimitation.

Earlier, Rahul said in a social media video that women in India should be given greater freedom to express themselves in all areas of life.

He said, âThe energy of India's women is trapped. It is not allowed to express itself. It is not allowed to imagine. For me, no country can be successful if its women are not expressing themselves. And I think a lot of my politics, and a lot of what politics should be in this country, is about making people understand that our country is stunted and incomplete without the expression of women.â

World.title: QR code, no queue: 25 crore OPD registrations go digital
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The long wait at hospital registration counters is slowly giving way to a QR code. In a sign of India's growing digital health footprint, patients have now completed 25 crore outpatient (OPD) registrations through the ABHA-based 'Scan and Register' service under the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (ABDM), with nearly four lakh people using the facility every day.

Introduced in October 2022, the service allows patients to register for an OPD consultation by simply scanning a QR code displayed at participating hospitals through an ABDM-enabled health app. Once they give consent, their ABHA-linked details are shared with the hospital, eliminating paperwork and reducing waiting time at registration counters.

The service is now available in 30,800 hospitals and healthcare facilities across 36 states and Union Territories and 756 districts, making it one of the country's fastest-growing digital public health services.

More than 24,000 government facilities and 6,400 private hospitals have adopted the system.

The biggest users of the platform are in Bihar, which has recorded over 7.3 crore digital OPD registrations, followed by Uttar Pradesh (4.09 crore), Andhra Pradesh (3.38 crore) and Jammu & Kashmir (1.39 crore).

Among hospitals, AIIMS New Delhi has emerged as the country's busiest digital registration centre, recording over 54.29 lakh Scan and Register transactions.





It is followed by AIIMS Bhopal (29.1 lakh), AIIMS Bhubaneswar (23.93 lakh), AIIMS Patna (19.62 lakh) and AIIMS Raipur (18.63 lakh).

Officials said the service has particularly eased hospital visits for senior citizens, pregnant women and patients requiring frequent follow-ups by cutting time spent at registration counters and doing away with repeated form filling.
