"This milestone reflects the growing trust that citizens and healthcare providers have placed in India's digital health ecosystem.

By simplifying one of the most common touchpoints in healthcare, OPD registration, the service has enhanced patient convenience while improving efficiency for hospitals," National Health Authority CEO Dr Sunil Kumar Barnwal said.

The National Health Authority said the service is now operational across AIIMS, central and state government hospitals, medical colleges, district hospitals, ESIC and railway hospitals, as well as private healthcare facilities, and is expected to expand further as more hospitals adopt ABHA-enabled digital services.

World.title: Akal Takht panel asks Punjab govt to address objections before anti-sacrilege talks
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The expert panel appointed by the Akal Takht on Friday asked the Punjab government to first submit a compliance report on the objections raised by the Sikh temporal seat before any further talks on the proposed anti-sacrilege law.

The panel, formed to discuss the Jaagat Jot Sri Guru Granth Sahib Satkar (Amendment) Act, 2026 with the state government, held its first meeting on Thursday.

The panel said the Punjab government's July 29 response did not address the main concerns raised by the Akal Takht, especially those related to possible interference in Sikh religious matters.

On June 29, Akal Takht Jathedar Giani Kuldip Singh Gargajj had given the state government one month to respond to his objections to the anti-sacrilege law.

In a statement on Friday, the Akal Takht secretariat said the government's response, submitted just before the deadline, was an attempt to avoid the main issues. It said the concerns of the Sikh community had already been conveyed to the Punjab assembly Speaker and members of the state Cabinet on July 31.

The secretariat also accused the Bhagwant Mann-led government of not taking a constructive approach towards resolving the sensitive issue.





It said that despite being given enough time, the Punjab government had not formed its own panel to discuss the matter.

Earlier, Jathedar Gargajj had rejected the government's response as "unsatisfactory" and announced a five-member expert panel to hold discussions with the Aam Aadmi Party government.

The issue came up after AAP MLA Inderbir Singh Nijjar submitted the Punjab government's response to the objections raised by the Akal Takht over the proposed anti-sacrilege legislation.

World.title: 17.4 lakh blood components discarded in 2025 despite record collection
World.content:
NEW DELHI: India discarded over 17.4 lakh blood components in 2025, even as blood collection reached a record 1.58 crore units, according to state-wise data tabled in the Rajya Sabha, highlighting continued challenges in blood inventory management despite a steady rise in donations.

Available official data indicate that China and India are among the world's largest blood collection programmes. In 2025, India collected 15.71 million units of blood, while China collected 25.5 million units, according to China's National Health Commission.

The data, reported by blood centres through the government's e-Raktakosh portal, show that expiry was the leading reason for discarding blood components, followed by reactive units and other operational reasons.

Reason-wise discard data has been captured on the portal since 2024, while such details were not available for 2023.

Replying to a question in Parliament, the Union health ministry, however, said it had not received any report of regional blood shortages. It added that ensuring an adequate supply of safe blood and minimising wastage is primarily the responsibility of state governments and Union Territories, while the Centre advocates a hub-and-spoke model under which blood is collected and processed at high-volume centres before being distributed to smaller blood banks and storage centres.





According to the data, Uttar Pradesh recorded the highest blood collection in 2025 with 21.6 lakh units, followed by Maharashtra (18.73 lakh), Gujarat (11.82 lakh), Rajasthan (10.79 lakh) and Tamil Nadu (9.74 lakh). Overall blood collection increased from 1.42 crore units in 2023 to 1.58 crore units in 2025.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

The annexure also showed a corresponding increase in blood component utilisation, with Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra, Gujarat, Tamil Nadu and Rajasthan reporting the highest utilisation during 2025.

At the same time, Uttar Pradesh reported the highest discard of blood components at 2.40 lakh, followed by Maharashtra (1.87 lakh), Kerala (1.44 lakh), Rajasthan (1.21 lakh) and Tamil Nadu (1.09 lakh). The ministry did not provide an analysis of the wide variation in discard across states.

Dr Hema Goyal, Consultant (Blood centre & Lab services), Aakash healthcare said blood wastage is inevitable to some extent, particularly because platelets have a shelf life of only five days. But discarding 17.4 lakh blood components in a year points to a mismatch between collection and actual demand. The solution is not fewer donations but smarter inventory management through real-time stock sharing and better coordination between blood banks.

NEW DELHI: In a fresh crackdown on food safety violations, the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has acted against two food products, penalising the manufacturer of a fortified sunflower oil after it was found to be substandard and stopping the sale of a Monk Fruit Sweetener over alleged licensing and labelling violations.The regulator imposed a penalty on AWL Agri Business Ltd, Mangaluru, after a laboratory analysis of a retail sample of Fortune "Fryola" Refined Sunflower Seed Oil found that its vitamin D content was below the prescribed standard, making the fortified edible oil substandard under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.FSSAI said the company was given an opportunity to present its case, but the adjudicating authority concluded that it had manufactured and marketed a substandard fortified edible oil before imposing a monetary penalty.In a separate action, the regulator prohibited the sale of PIE Foods' Monk Fruit Sweetener, a natural zero-calorie sugar substitute, after inspections found cartons of the product stored at the company's premises without the required manufacturing licence.FSSAI also alleged that the product carried claims such as "100% Monk Fruit Extract" and "Natural Ingredients", while its online listing did not carry the mandatory endorsement required under food safety regulations.It further said the company failed to produce records showing that the monk fruit extract used in the product had been procured in accordance with the Food Safety and Standards Act.The prohibition order will remain in force until the product complies with the provisions of the Food Safety and Standards Act and related regulations.The regulator said the actions are part of its ongoing drive to tighten enforcement against food business operators and ensure that products sold to consumers meet prescribed safety and quality standards.

The body of a 40-year-old man remained hanging from a 40ft-high 400kV high-tension transmission tower in Badaun for nearly six hours Thursday as police and electricity department officials waited for a power shutdown before retrieving it, officials said Friday.

World.title: Can protection against domestic cruelty extend to live-in relationships? | Explained
World.content:
The story so far: In Dr Lokesh B.H. & Ors v. State of Karnataka & Anr, decided on August 3, 2026, the Supreme Court considered whether Section 498A of the Indian Penal Code (IPC) could apply to a man in a live-in relationship and whether the expression “husband” under the section is confined to a legally valid marriage.

The appellant argued that since he and the complainant were never validly married, Section 498A could not apply to him. The Karnataka High Court had rejected this argument and refused to quash the criminal proceedings against him. He appealed to the Supreme Court.

Rejecting the argument, a Bench of Justices Sanjay Karol and Nongmeikapam Kotiswar Singh held that the protection under Section 498A is not confined to legally married women. It can also extend to women in live-in relationships that are “in the nature of marriage”, subject to certain conditions.

What is Section 498A of IPC?

The provision now corresponds to Section 85 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), which replaced Section 498A of the IPC. It deals with husband or relative of husband of a woman subjecting her to cruelty. It reads that whoever — being the husband or the relative of the husband of a woman — subjects such woman to cruelty, shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years and shall also be liable to fine.

For the purposes of this section, “cruelty means” (a) any wilful conduct which is of such a nature as is likely to drive the woman to commit suicide or to cause grave injury or danger to life, limb or health (whether mental or physical) of the woman; or (b) harassment of the woman where such harassment is with a view to coercing her or any person related to her to meet any unlawful demand for any property or valuable security or is on account of failure by her or any person related to her to meet such demand.

What is the ruling?

The Supreme Court held that the protection against domestic cruelty under Section 498A of the erstwhile Indian Penal Code (now Section 85 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita) is not confined to legally married women. It ruled that the provision also applies to live-in relationships that qualify as “relationships in the nature of marriage”, provided there is an intention to marry.

The court clarified that not every live-in relationship would attract Section 498A. The protection is available only to relationships between two consenting adults that meet the legal test of a relationship in the nature of marriage. It also made clear that this expanded interpretation is limited to Section 498A and does not automatically extend to other statutory provisions.

Rejecting the argument that Section 498A, being a penal provision, should apply only to legally married couples, the Bench held that the law must be interpreted in a manner that advances its object of preventing domestic cruelty.

“The interpretation given to this penal provision must be an interpretation which keeps in view the reformative objective, or else its mandate will be defeated.”

At the same time, the court recognised concerns over misuse of Section 498A. It held that the initial burden of establishing that the relationship was in the nature of marriage and carried an intention to marry would lie on the woman seeking protection.

It also directed that the safeguards against arrest laid down in Arnesh Kumar v. State of Bihar (2014) must be strictly followed and that no partner or relative should be arrested without complying with those safeguards.

The Bench remarked: “In all cases, A and B chose each other and decided to live life together. The only difference is that in the first case they are married and in the other two they are not. Why should there be any difference in the protection that is given to a woman if she faces cruelty at the hands of the husband/partner or his family members? The law fairly well recognises the right and freedom of an individual to choose the person they want to be with as an inextricable part of dignity and personal liberty.”

Is protection under the Domestic Violence Act enough?

The court referred to Indra Sarma v. V.K.V. Sarma (2013), wherein it was recognised that though a live-in relationship between two consenting adults is not an offence, the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 was enacted “to provide a remedy in civil law for protection of women” by covering couples in a relationship in the nature of marriage.

The court held that although the DV Act is a piece of comprehensive welfare legislation addressing various forms of domestic violence, its overall character is civil, whereas Section 498A creates criminal liability.

Drawing a clear distinction between civil and criminal consequences, the court held that it would be “a misstatement of law” to regard the DV Act as providing adequate protection equivalent to Section 498A IPC. While the DV Act primarily carries civil and monetary consequences, Section 498A is backed by the force of criminal deterrence. Except for punishment under Section 31 for violation of protection orders, the DV Act does not create criminal liability for acts of domestic violence themselves. Consequently, the availability of remedies under the DV Act cannot justify denying women in qualifying relationships the protection of Section 498A IPC.

Since Section 498A is penal in nature, the court narrowed the protection by requiring proof of intent to marry. It said this requirement would separate relationships protected under the DV Act from those attracting criminal liability under Section 498A.

The court underscored: “When the intent is absent, a question beckons as to why such relationship needs to be equated with marriage for the purposes of invoking penal provisions. In our view, it does not. Those relationships that are in the nature of marriage and also have the requisite intent to marry are the closest to marriage itself, and it is those relationships that shall be entitled to the protection of this Section.”

The Court concluded that “Cruelty, any which way, does not check at the door, whether the house it enters is that of a married woman or not. Once it enters, its propensity to destroy is aggravated.”

What qualifies as a relationship in the nature of marriage?

Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 has mentioned “relationship in the nature of marriage” in section 2(f). It says, “domestic relationship” means a relationship between two persons who live or have, at any point of time, lived together in a shared household, when they are related by consanguinity, marriage, or through a relationship in the nature of marriage, adoption or are family members living together as a joint family”

The court in the case of D. Velusamy v. D. Patchaiammal(2010) observed that “relationship in the nature of marriage is akin to a common law marriage. Common law marriages require that although not being formally married, the couple must hold themselves out to society as being akin to spouses and must be of legal age to marry. They must also be otherwise qualified to enter into a legal marriage, including being unmarried. They must have voluntarily cohabited and held themselves out to the world as being akin to spouses for a significant period of time. In our opinion, a “relationship in the nature of marriage” under the 2005 Act must also fulfil the above requirements, and in addition the parties must have lived together in a “shared household” as defined in Section 2(s) of the Act.”

The Supreme Court reiterated that there is no straightjacket formula to determine whether a live-in relationship amounts to a “relationship in the nature of marriage”. Referring to its decision in Indra Sarma v. V.K.V. Sarma (2013), it said the factors are illustrative and not exhaustive, and each case would have to be decided on its own facts.

According to the court, a qualifying relationship would ordinarily involve the couple living together for a reasonable period, sharing a common household, and demonstrating financial interdependence, such as maintaining joint bank accounts, jointly acquiring property or making long-term investments. It may also involve shared domestic responsibilities, with the partners jointly managing the household and everyday life.

The court also said that the nature of the relationship should reflect a marriage-like partnership. It includes an intimate and emotional relationship, having and raising children together, and holding themselves out to society as husband and wife. Ultimately, the common intention and conduct of the parties, including how they understood their relationship and their respective roles and responsibilities, would be a key factor in determining whether it is a “relationship in the nature of marriage”.

World.title: When is heavy rainfall a cloudburst, and when is it not? | Explained
World.content:
When a wall of water suddenly crashes from the sky and sweeps away homes and roads within minutes, one of the first words officials and the media in India reach for is ‘cloudburst’. However, the term is often misused in a way that can distract from poor planning and crumbling infrastructure.

According to the India Meteorological Department (IMD), a cloudburst occurs when a small area, around 20-30 sq. km, receives 10 cm or more of rain in an hour.

World.title: BJP blames AAP govt in Punjab for ‘worsening drugs menace’
World.content:
Bharatiya Janata Party Punjab president Kewal Singh Dhillon on Thursday (July 30, 2026) blamed the Aam Aadmi Party government for the State’s, what he termed as “worsening drug crisis”, declaring that the AAP government’s widely-publicised ‘Yudh Nashian Virudh’ (War Against Drugs) campaign has failed entirely.

Mr. Dhillon said the AAP had during the 2022 poll campaign promised the people of Punjab that it would eradicate the drug menace within three months, after the party assumed power. “But today the situation has worsened instead of improving. Punjab’s youth are losing their lives every single day. When drug-affected families and ordinary citizens raise their voices against drug traffickers, they are openly threatened, which clearly indicates that the traffickers enjoy administrative and political patronage,” he alleged.

The BJP leader further said that public faith in the system has eroded to such an extent that families devastated by the drug menace are being forced to put up posters to sell their homes and stage protests.

“The increasing number of drug-related deaths and the growing public anger are clear evidence of the complete failure of the AAP government’s governance on this issue. The AAP government’s so-called promise of ‘change’ has come at a high cost for the people of Punjab and has pushed the state back by several years. The drug menace can be eradicated only through strong leadership and a robust policy framework, not through publicity campaigns and s,” he said, urging people of Punjab to elect a BJP government in the State in the upcoming assembly election, due in early 2027.

World.title: Kuruvai coverage in Tamil Nadu’s Cauvery delta is down by over one lakh acres due to water shortage
World.content:
The impact of non-release of Cauvery water for the delta is visible. This year, the coverage of paddy in the region during the Kuruvai cultivation season is down by over one lakh acres, compared to the previous year.

As on July 27, the coverage was 3.87 lakh acres compared to 5.05 lakh acres on the corresponding day last year. This year too, Thanjavur topped the list of districts with approximately 1.29 lakh acres. It was followed by Mayiladuthurai (97,000 acres) and Tiruvarur (88,700 acres).

Of the seven districts in the Cauvery delta, Cuddalore is the outlier where the coverage is almost double the previous year’s figure. Asked to explain the increase, K.V. Elankeeran, president of the Cauvery Delta Farmers’ Association, who hails from Kattumannarkoil in Cuddalore district, said that the agriculturists had an inkling, at the beginning of the season, that the authorities would ensure full water level at the Veeranam tank, which has become an important source of drinking water for Chennai. In addition, free electricity and the availability of groundwater are the factors that have pushed the farmers to increase their coverage in the district.

On Thursday morning, the water level at the Mettur dam stood at 73.7 ft (full level: 120 ft) with the storage being 35.97 thousand million cubic feet (tmc ft) against the capacity of 93.47 tmc ft. The Cauvery water realisation by Tamil Nadu at Biligundulu was 0.66 tmc ft in the 28 days of July. Since June 1, the State received 3.57 tmc ft while the shortfall was around 34 tmc ft. Unless the inflow position improves dramatically, farmers in the delta may find it extremely difficult to cover even half of the normal coverage of 12 lakh acres during the Samba-Thaladi cultivation season.

World.title: Pursue public services for right reasons, Guntur Collector tells UPSC aspirants
World.content:
Doing the right things in the right way with consistency and dedication is the key to achieving success in the UPSC Civil Services examination, Guntur District Collector C.M. Sai Kanth Varma told aspirants while urging them to pursue public service for the right reasons rather than for money.

Addressing a seminar on Civil Services preparation at the JKC College organised by The Hindu Civil Services Aspirants Club in association with Sri Harini IAS academy, Guntur, on Thursday, Mr. Varma shared his own journey to Indian Administrative Service (IAS) and encouraged students to remain focused, disciplined and stress-free.

He recalled an inspiring interaction with an expert on UPSC exams, during his days at IIT Madras, which motivated him to prepare for the examination after working with Amazon and Google. He said reading The Hindu newspaper every day, particularly its editorials, played a significant role in his preparation. He advised students to give their best to every task and maintain consistency throughout their preparation.

The Collector highlighted his administrative experience as Project Officer of the Integrated Tribal Development Agency (ITDA), Seethampeta, where initiatives helped reduce maternal deaths. He also spoke about the Super 60 programme that provided coaching and wider exposure to tribal students.

The seminar offered students from schools and junior colleges a detailed roadmap for the UPSC and APPSC examinations, covering preparation strategy, answer writing, interviews and career opportunities in public service.

Political Science faculty Amith Narauni stressed disciplined preparation and a thorough understanding of the syllabus, describing it as a key for success. Ecology and Environment expert Amit Singh explained the examination pattern, services such as IAS, IPS and IFS, and the importance of systematic preparation.

Ethics and Current Affairs faculty Nitin Kumar advised students to rely on NCERT textbooks and The Hindu, prepare concise notes, revise regularly and adopt the Logic-Example-Data (LED) format in answer writing. Psychology faculty Allam Srinivas encouraged students to set ambitious goals and remain calm, explaining how a relaxed mind improves performance.

CSAT faculty Amirsetty Sridhar advocated beginning preparation early. Sri Harini IAS Academy Director K. Narendra outlined the academy's initiatives. JKC College Principal P. Gopichand said holistic understanding of subjects was essential for success. College Secretary and Correspondent J. Murali Mohan and others attended the programme.

World.title: CITU stages protest demanding regularisation of contract workers, Minimum Pay Scale
World.content:
Around 50 lakh employees working in scheduled employments are being subjected to exploitation without revising the minimum wages for them, leaders of the Centre of Indian Trade Unions (CITU) said on Thursday, warning the government of a larger strike if demands are not met immediately.

Participating in a protest at the NTR District Collectorate in Vijayawada, CITU State president Ch. Narasinga Rao and general secretary A.V. Nageswara Rao said 71 jobs feature on the list of the Scheduled Employment, for which the government has fixed minimum wages.

“Every once in five years, the minimum wages for these 71 Scheduled Employments have to be revised, but it has been 12 years since the last revision was done,” said Mr. Rao.

Among Scheduled Employments, there are 4 lakh outsourced and contract employees working in different government departments. The CITU demanded implementation of the Minimum Time Scale and regularisation of these workers and increasing the pay of unskilled workers to ₹26,000.

Similar protests were held outside the Collectorates across the State. The CITU State Committee said the State government has neglected the working-class sections and focussed solely on serving investors in the name of development.

Reminding the government that development is impossible without workers, the CITU demanded that all outsourcing and contract employees be regularised.

World.title: Collector calls for coordinated efforts to eradicate human trafficking
World.content:
Coordinated efforts by government departments and society are essential to eradicate human trafficking and bonded labour, NTR District Collector G. Lakshmisha said on Thursday.

Participating in a programme at the Collectorate to mark the World Day Against Trafficking in Persons, the Collector unveiled an awareness wall poster on prevention of human trafficking.

Later, Mr. Lakshmisha said awareness among students would play a vital role in protecting not only themselves but also their families and society from such crimes. He also expressed concern about the increasing misuse of social media platforms and cautioned youth against fraudulent job offers, educational opportunities and other false promises made by traffickers.

The Collector observed that women, children, orphans, school dropouts and economically vulnerable sections were more susceptible to trafficking. He also appealed to the public to contact the Child Helpline 1098 in case of emergencies involving children.

Vigil on bonded labour

Deputy Commissioner of Labour Guntupalli Dhanalakshmi said the district administration was maintaining constant vigilance to eliminate bonded labour. She also encouraged women to make use of safety applications such as the Shakti App for their protection.

On the occasion, Dr. Lakshmisha released ₹6.60 lakh towards immediate rehabilitation assistance for 22 rescued bonded labourers, crediting ₹30,000 each to their bank accounts.

World.title: RTC JAC to continue agitation until written assurance is issued
World.content:
The Andhra Pradesh Public Transport Department (APPTD)-APSRTC Employees’ Joint Action Committee (JAC) on Thursday said it would continue its third phase of agitation until the assurances given by the APSRTC management during talks are formally recorded and communicated in writing.

The decision was announced after discussions between APSRTC Vice-Chairman and Managing Director N. Balasubramanyam and JAC representatives led by conveners Y. Srinivasa Rao and P. Damodara Rao.

Addressing the media after the meeting, the JAC leaders said the management had agreed to issue the official minutes of the meeting incorporating the assurances made during the discussions.

They said the management had also agreed in principle to reopen the four depots that were earlier closed. The JAC State Executive Committee would meet after receiving the written minutes and decide on its future course of action. Until then, the third phase of the agitation, announced earlier to oppose the alleged privatisation of APSRTC through private electric bus operations, would continue as scheduled, they said.

The JAC has been demanding that all electric buses be procured and operated directly by APSRTC instead of private operators. It has also sought the reopening of the four closed depots, withdrawal of tenders issued to private electric bus operators, and protection of employees’ interests while strengthening the State-run public transport system.

JAC co-conveners P.V. Ramana Reddy, G.V. Narasayya, Ch. Sundarayya, S.V. Seshagiri Rao and K. Surya Prakash Rao, besides other union leaders were also present in the meeting.

Meanwhile, Mr. Balasubramanyam said the State government was framing its electric bus policy in-line with the Centre’s push for eco-friendly public transport while ensuring that the interests of APSRTC employees were safeguarded. He said the management had accepted nearly 90% of the demands raised by the Employees’ JAC and expressed confidence that the remaining issues could also be resolved through dialogue.

World.title: Captain martyred, 7 terrorists killed in intelligence-based operation in Hangu: ISPR
World.content:
The military media affairs wing said on Saturday that a captain was martyred while seven terrorists were killed during an intelligence-based operation (IBO) in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s Hangu district.

In a statement, Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said security forces conducted an IBO in Hangu on Friday following reports about the presence of terrorists belonging to Fitna al Khawarij — a term the state uses for terrorists belonging to the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan.

During the operation, troops effectively engaged the terrorists, it said.

“In desperation, the khawarij took refuge inside a mosque, blatantly disregarding the sanctity of the place of worship. In ensuing fire exchange, seven khawarij, belonging to Indian-sponsored Fitna al Khawarij were sent to hell,” it said.

The statement went on to say that during the exchange of fire, 27-year-old Captain Hamza Akram, a resident of Punjab’s Narowal district who was “leading his troops from front and relentlessly pursuing” the terrorists, embraced martyrdom.

“Weapons and ammunition were also recovered from the killed khawarij, who remained actively involved in numerous terrorist activities against the security forces and law enforcement agencies as well as killing of innocent civilians,” it said.

ISPR said that a sanitisation operation was being conducted to eliminate any other Indian-sponsored terrorists in the area.

President Asif Ali Zardari paid tribute to the martyred captain saying, “The motherland pays its profound tribute to the great sacrifice of its brave son.”

“The entire nation is indebted to the eternal sacrifices of these brave sons for the motherland,” the president added, offering prayers for the bereaved family.

Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi paid tribute to the martyred captain and offered his condolences to the bereaved family. He said that the martyred officer had paid the ultimate sacrifice for the homeland and would remain alive in our hearts.

A day earlier, ISPR said 10 terrorists were killed in two separate engagements in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. It said that in the first encounter, a group of terrorists attempted to attack security forces’ checkposts in Azam Warsak area in South Waziristan, which was effectively thwarted, resulting in the deaths of eight terrorists.

“In another encounter that took place in Dir district, own troops successfully neutralised two more khawarij,” it added.

Terrorist commander killed in Bannu

Separately, security forces killed a key terrorist commander, identified as Jamidullah, during an operation in Jani Khel area of KP’s Bannu district, a security official said.

The official said that the terrorist commander was involved in terrorist activities and was considered a quadcopter expert.

The official said that security forces conducted the operation in Jani Khel on the basis of intelligence reports, during which Jamidullah was targeted and killed.

World.title: Efforts underway to end deadlock over judges’ appointments
World.content:
• Govt’s legal team set to meet Presidency officials as summary remains pending with Zardari

• Officials say matter now sub judice after petition filed in IHC

ISLAMABAD: In a last-ditch effort to break the deadlock over judicial appointments, the government’s legal team has scheduled a meeting with its counterparts at the Presidency on Sunday, as authorities explore the possibility of unilaterally notifying the confirmation and appointment of high court judges.

The development comes as the Islamabad High Court (IHC) has yet to issue its ruling on the maintainability of a petition challenging President Asif Ali Zardari’s alleged failure to assent to the recommendations of the Judicial Commission of Pakistan.

The JCP, during its meetings on July 20 and 21, recommended the confirmation of four additional judges of the Peshawar High Court, a six-month extension for an additional judge of the Sindh High Court, and the appointment of 19 additional judges to the Lahore, Islamabad, Sindh and Balochistan high courts.

Under Clause 8 of Article 175-A of the Cons­titution, the recommendations were forwarded to the prime minister, who then sent the summary to the president. However, the summary has remained pending with the president since then.

Amid the stalemate, the government is examining the possibility of invoking Article 48(1) of the Constitution to issue the notifications through the law ministry, arguing that the president was required to act on the summary within a fortnight of its submission — a period that has since expired.

However, government functionaries have maintained that with the matter now sub judice, notifications cannot be issued at this stage.

Sources said the government’s legal team planned to pursue an “out-of-court” settlement with its counterparts at the Presidency.

The president’s legal team has raised certain objections to the JCP proceedings, noting that nearly all nominees proposed by the PPP were rejected. They also conveyed that some candidates recommended for appointment have criminal records.

The Presidency’s legal team contends that Article 175-A does not prescribe a specific timeframe for the president’s action and that the provision cannot be overridden by Article 48(1) to bypass the Presidency.

They have also referred to Article 48(2), which empowers the president “to act in his discretion in respect of any matter in respect of which he is empowered by the Constitution to do so” and states that validity of anything done by the president shall not be called into question on any ground whatsoever.

Sources in the Presidency cautioned that any unilateral action in such a sensitive matter would be a “political and legal disaster”. According to them, the only way forward is to reach a consensus through democratic means.

They warned that bypassing the prescribed procedure could trigger significant complications and suggested that any ambiguity regarding Articles 48(1), 48(2) and 175-A(8) should be resolved through mutual consultation between the president and the prime minister rather than through unilateral action.

On the other hand, government sources maintained that judicial appointments were governed by constitutional provisions and that any deadlock must be resolved strictly in accordance with the Constitution.

Meanwhile, the IHC has reserved its verdict on the maintainability of a petition filed by advocate Luqman Chaudhary through his counsel Zahid Chaudhry, seeking a direction to the president to approve the summary.

During Thursday’s hearing, Justice Arbab Muh­ammad Tahir questioned how the court could issue directions to the president and reserved his order.

It was initially expected that the ruling would be issued the same day, but Justice Arbab left his office without delivering it.

The order was then anticipated on Friday morning, but the file had not been returned from the judge’s chamber by the close of business.

The delay has already created practical complications. Four additional judges of the PHC, whose confirmations were recommended by the JCP, ceased to hold office after their tenure expired on Aug 4 due to the absence of formal notifications.

Similarly, an additional judge of the SHC, whose term was extended by six months, relinquished office after his tenure expired on July 29.

Minister of State for Law and Justice Barrister Aqeel Malik said the government would resolve the matter within the constitutional framework and in accordance with the principles laid down by the superior courts.

Published in Dawn, August 8th, 2026

World.title: Pakistan joins Saudi Arabia, Turkiye in ‘all for one’ pact
World.content:
• MBS, Shehbaz, Erdogan sign Makkah Joint Defence Agreement to boost ‘collective deterrence against any aggression’

• PM hopes accord will serve as ‘shield of peace’; Erdogan says alliance is open to other friendly nations • Saudi minister insists new bloc no threat to ‘any country’

ISLAMABAD: Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye on Friday signed a joint defence pact in the holy city of Makkah, which empowers member states to treat an attack against one of them as an attack against all.

The Makkah Joint Defence Agreement, which seeks to strengthen the collective security of the three states, was signed by Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, Saudi Crown Prince and PM Mohammad bin Salman, and Turkiye’s President Recep Tayyip Erdogan at the Al-Safa Palace.

The signing of the agreement was announced by three countries through a joint statement, which was published by Pakis­tan’s Foreign Office (FO) and Saudi Arabia’s official SPA press agency.

It said the pact reflected the three countries’ “shared commitment to further strengthening their collective security and to promoting peace, security, and stability in the region and beyond, in pursuit of a secure and prosperous future”.

“The agreement is intended to strengthen collective deterrence against any act of aggression, and stipulates that any armed attack against any one of the three states shall be regarded as an attack against them all.”

It also “provides for the enha­ncement of all aspects of defence cooperation” among the three countries, the statement added.

The agreement is “guided by the longstanding historical ties among the three states, based on the enduring bonds of brotherhood and Islamic solidarity that unite them, and building upon their shared strategic interests and longstanding defence cooperation”.

During the Makkah Summit for Joint Defence, the “distinguished relations” between the three countries were reviewed, “along with a number of issues of mutual interest”, the statement noted.

From Pakistan’s side, Chief of Defence Forces (CDF) and Chief of the Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir, Deputy PM and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, and Defence Minister Khawaja Asif were also present at the signing ceremony.

The defence and foreign ministers of Saudi Arabia and Turkiye were in attendance as well.

Following the formal signing of the pact, photos released by Saudi media showed the world leaders offering prayers at the Al-Safa Palace, overlooking the Holy Ka’aba.

‘Shield of peace’

PM Shehbaz Sharif described the signing of the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement as a “historic pact”, saying the three countries were united by faith, friendship and a shared commitment to peace and security.

In a post on X, the prime minister said he was honoured to sign the agreement alongside the Saudi crown prince and the Turkish president.

He said the pact would serve as a “shield of peace” for generations and expressed hope that it would bring prosperity to the three countries and the wider Muslim world. Shehbaz also appreciated Field Marshal Asim Munir’s efforts and dedication towards the agreement.

Saudi Foreign Minister Faisal bin Farhan said that the signing of the joint defence agreement by the crown prince, the president of Türkiye and the prime minister of Pakistan underscored the depth of the fraternal and strategic relations between the three countries.

He said the agreement marked an important milestone in their defence cooperation and reflected their shared desire to coordinate efforts to address challenges and threats affecting regional security and stability. He added that the pact embodied the three countries’ shared political will to safeguard security, support a more secure regional environment and pave the way for greater development and prosperity.

Saudi Arabia’s Deputy Minister for Public Diplomacy Rayed Krimly said the agreement “does not represent an effort to establish a military axis or a sectarian bloc”. “Nor is it linked to any nuclear ambitions or arms race; rather, it is focused on building sustainable capabilities,” he wrote on X.

He noted that the deal “does not constitute a threat to the security of any country in the region, nor does it represent an escalation of tensions between any two states”. The Saudi official further said the agreement “does not supersede or replace any existing bilateral or multilateral agreements between these countries”.

‘Open to other nations’

Turkish President Erdogan also reiterated this sentiment, saying that the pact targets no country and remains open to participation of other friendly nations seeking peace, prosperity and stability in the region.

In a post on the Turkish social platform NSosyal, Erdogan said on Friday the agreement, based on the principle of collective deterrence, would strengthen security and defence cooperation, joint defence industry projects and counterterrorism efforts. He said the agreement also reaffirms the right to self-defence as defined under Article 51 of the UN Charter.

“The agreement does not target any country and is open to the participation of all brotherly countries seeking peace, prosperity and stability in our region,” Erdogan said.

Türkiye, he added, would firmly maintain its principled stance in favour of resolving conflicts and crises through dialogue and diplomacy, based on respect for international law and in line with its vision of regional ownership.
